## 2026-11-17 — Investigation of NVIDIA cuPotential (OpenMM plugin 0.3.5): does not run on floyd because of R550; switching to OpenMM 8.4 is possible

- Request: "I want to use cuPotential in environments where it can be used. Investigate first." No code changes; investigation only.
- cuPotential: an NVIDIA CUDA-X library. The OpenMM plugin `nv-openmm-plugin` (`import nv_openmm_plugin as nv`) provides replacements for `NonbondedForce`, `CustomNonbondedForce`, `LangevinMiddleIntegrator`, and isotropic `MonteCarloBarostat`. The published figures are 2.6-4.0x versus stock OpenMM 8.4.0 NPT mixed (24k-409k atoms). Early access. 0.3.5 is the only public release (2026-11-15). The plugin part is Apache-2.0; `libcupo.so` (636 MB) is under NVIDIA's proprietary license.
- Requirements (0.3.5):
  - Linux x86-64 only. There is no aarch64 build, so it cannot be used on RIKYU (GB200).
  - Python 3.12, **OpenMM 8.4.x only** (`openmm >=8.4,<8.5`; pinned by ABI because it depends on the internal CUDA platform API).
  - CUDA 13.4 runtime (cudart / cuFFT 12.4 / nvJitLink / NVRTC 13.4). Driver R615 or later. Data-center GPUs and professional RTX also work with cuda-compat-13-4 on R535/R570/R580/R590/R595/R610. GeForce requires R615.
  - SM 75 or later. n1 (TITAN X), n2 and n4 (1080 Ti) are out of scope.
  - `libOpenMMNvidiaCUDA.so` requires **GLIBC_2.38**. The same holds for the conda package, so it cannot be loaded on Ubuntu 20.04 (2.31) or on the current amd64 image (ubuntu22.04, 2.35). An Ubuntu 24.04-based image is needed.
- Physical constraints: the original force field must use PME or LJPME only, and the **Ewald tolerance is fixed at 5e-4** (MDClaw leaves it unset, so it is OpenMM's default 5e-4, which matches). An explicit PME grid is not allowed. CUDA single / mixed only. Each box edge must be at least 3x the cutoff (even after shrinking under NPT). With a barostat, the NPT box can grow to at most 1.15x its initial length (equilibration that compresses from low density only shrinks, so it is fine). Electrostatics use C2 Prolate splitting by default (it does not agree with Ewald to within rounding error; passing `nv.NonbondedForce.PME` gives Ewald). Custom mode does not support interaction groups, tabulated functions, computed values, or parameter derivatives of the energy, so MDClaw's FEP / ABFE softcore forces are not expected to carry over as-is. There is no replacement for the membrane or anisotropic barostats.
- **Measurement on floyd (A6000, driver 550.54.14)**: calling `cuInit` with the `libcuda.so.1` from cuda-compat-13-4 (615.71.10) returned **803** (`system has unsupported display driver / cuda driver combination`). The host libcuda returns 0 (CUDA 12.4). R550 is not a branch covered by forward compatibility, so it will not run unless the driver is raised to R580 or later (with cuda-compat) or to R615 or later. n5 (2080 Ti, GeForce, R530) also needs R615.
- **Checked the basis for the OpenMM 8.5.1 lower bound (correction to the note in 3003478)**:
  - No basis could be found for "8.6 brings SourceWithCMAP fixes used by the ff19SB and phosaa19SB conversions" in `environment.yml`. The OpenMM 8.5.0-8.6.1 release notes contain no CMAP fix, and the name "SourceWithCMAP" exists in neither OpenMM nor openmmforcefields.
  - "8.5.1 is the lower bound for openmmforcefields 0.15.1 and later" is also inaccurate. On conda-forge, 0.15.0 / 0.15.1 depend on `openmm >=8.1.2` and **0.16.0 on `>=8.5.1`**. What 0.16.0 added is only SMIRNOFF virtual sites and constraints, molecules spanning multiple residues, faster template matching, and making the `forcefield` argument required. ff19SB and Lipid21 are in 0.15.x, and the 0.15.1 CI includes OpenMM 8.4.0.
  - No 8.5 / 8.6-only APIs used by MDClaw were found (PythonForce, multistate sampler, `ScaleMoleculesAsRigid`, LCPO, FlexibleBarostat: none are used). openmm-torch's PythonTorchForce (b653290) is an implementation independent of OpenMM's PythonForce.
  - Serialization: from 8.4.0 to 8.6.1 the force proxy version numbers did not change; the only additions are the optional `rigidScaling` attribute on barostats and LCPOForce. system.xml / state.xml written by 8.6 are expected to be readable by 8.4 (not measured).
  - #5236 in 8.5.1 (misassignment of template constraints) was a bug introduced in 8.5.0 and is not present in 8.4.0.
  - What would be lost by downgrading to 8.4 (additional investigation):
    - The GPU energy minimization in 8.5. MDClaw's min / eq / relax use `minimizeEnergy` and `LocalEnergyMinimizer`. The divergence countermeasure in `relax.py` (capped steepest descent → L-BFGS) was tuned against the 8.5 / 8.6 minimizer, and it is unconfirmed whether 3WD5- and 1GQV-type clashes are resolved the same way on 8.4, whose implementation differs.
    - The long-range-correction cache for CustomNonbondedForce in 8.6 is not lost. MDClaw's FEP / ABFE turn the long-range correction off (`fep/hybrid.py:712`, `fep/decouple.py:179`), so it was never in effect (corrects the statement in the first draft above).
    - Bugs present in 8.4.0 and fixed in 8.5-8.6 that lie on MDClaw's paths:
      - #5379: the default inter-ion distance in `Modeller._addIons` is 0.05 nm (0.5 nm in the documentation). Used by `addSolvent` in `solvation/water.py`. Ions can be placed next to each other.
      - #5220: when `addHydrogens` chooses HIS by hydrogen bonding, `ne2IsBonded` is never set, so neutral HIS is always HID. Also present in 8.4.0. The main protonation path specifies variants explicitly, so the impact is small. It does lie on the automatic-selection paths (`terminal_caps.py`, `glycam_topology.py`, the nucleic-acid path in `clean_protein.py`).
      - #5179: in PDBFixer, CONECT records in a PDB containing MODEL / ENDMDL are not read. Only when a multi-model PDB is passed to PDBFixer as is.
      - #5346 (GPU synchronization for RMSD / RG / OrientationRestraint) is not used in MDClaw.
    - openmmforcefields would go down to 0.15.1. MDClaw's `SystemGenerator(small_molecule_forcefield="gaff-2.11", ...)` has the same API in 0.15.1. What is lost is the faster template matching in 0.16 and support for molecules spanning multiple residues.
    - Other dependencies: pdbfixer 1.12 needs `openmm >=8.2`. openff-toolkit / nagl / interchange / mdanalysis / pymbar and SST2 (`>=7.7`) have no constraint. conda-forge's OpenMM 8.4.0 has CUDA 12.6, 12.9, and 13.0 builds for both linux-64 and aarch64 (12.6 still needs R560 or later, so it does not rescue floyd's R550; the cuda118 source build would continue from the 8.4.0 tag). The openmm-torch / openmm-plumed recipes would have to be rebuilt against 8.4.
  - Confirmed why it does not run on RIKYU: the runtime library `libcupo.so.0.3.5` and the LTO-IR `cupo_math.cu.o` exist only as x86-64 ELF. The same holds for the release tarball (`cupo-0.3.5+cuda_13.4.sm_…tar.gz`), the wheel, and conda. libcupo is proprietary and its source is not published, so even if the plugin part (Apache-2.0) is rebuilt for arm64, there is no runtime library for it to load. The driver (R580) and GB200 (SM 100) meet the requirements. There is no GitHub issue requesting ARM support yet (as of 2026-11-17 there is only one issue).
  - Decision inputs: as of 2026-11-17, the lab has no machine that can run cuPotential (floyd is R550, n5 is GeForce below R615, RIKYU is aarch64). Even with (a), nothing is gained until the drivers are upgraded.
- Undecided (first draft): (a) downgrade everything to OpenMM 8.4 + openmmforcefields 0.15.1, or (b) build a separate Ubuntu 24.04 + OpenMM 8.4 + cuPotential environment only for the run side (min/eq/prod). Either way, we need code that swaps `NonbondedForce` just before `new_simulation` (`mdclaw/_common.py`), and a guardrail that excludes systems that do not meet the requirements (membrane barostat, FEP, non-PME). It will not be enabled by default until accuracy and speed are measured on a GPU with a supported driver.

## 2026-11-15 — FEP hybrid: map CB hydrogens by position rather than by name (root fix for bug 1 of 2026-11-03, uncommitted)

- Request: "Investigate the root cause of why that happens." "Fix it with the approach that maps by position." The target is the dummy-atom misplacement found in the NcPNG1 study (bug 1 in the 2026-11-03 entry, `/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/pngase/mdclaw_fix_request.md`).
- Cause (measured on the study's 14 hybrids from the saved end states):
  1. `mapping.py` makes the CB hydrogens common atoms by name and fixes them at the WT coordinates. The mutant side chain is built by HPacker / PDBFixer with its own chi1, and the names HB2/HB3 are determined by the position of the γ atom, so when chi1 differs, names and positions disagree. They disagreed in 10 of 14, and in 7 of those the new γ atom (HB1 for Ala) was placed 0.5-1.2 Å from a common hydrogen.
  2. The local minimization in `relax_dummy_atoms` moved 4 of those 7 to the old γ atom's position and stopped 3 at an inverted stationary point (about 60° from the two common hydrogens, 144-161° from the old γ). They cannot be distinguished from the starting placement.
  - The side chains themselves are normal rotamers (HPacker near ±60° / 180°). The problem is only how they are placed.
- Fix: added `old_positions` / `new_positions` to `map_mutation`. When bonds and coordinates are available, the CB substituents are compared by direction in each state's N–CA–CB frame, paired one-to-one within 45°, and only pairs where both are hydrogens become common atoms (`cb_hydrogen_pairs_by_site`). A hydrogen facing a heavy atom on the other side becomes unique. Without coordinates, pairing by name is used as before. `build_hybrid_system` (`_assemble_hybrid`) passes the coordinates of both end states. The mutant side chain is placed in the orientation the model built.
- Verification:
  - Rebuilt the 14 with the new mapping and ran relaxation and endpoint validation on the GPU (`pngase/scripts/hyb_verify_site_mapping.py`). Endpoint validation passed 14/14, and `check_dummy_placement` also passed (max 38°). The dummy bond energies (after relaxation) of the 3 that had been misplaced went 239 → 1, 439 → 31, 395 → 19 kJ/mol. Legs whose chi1 already matched give the same values as before.
  - S273F_fold went 364 → 194 kJ/mol and is still high (35 before relaxation; the side chain distorts to avoid clashing with the surrounding protein).
  - Tests: added to `tests/test_fep.py` 5 pure-Python mapping tests and 5 in vacuum for SER→LEU/PHE/ALA and PHE→SER with the mutant rotated by ±120°. Reverting to name-based mapping makes the latter fail 5/5. 281 FEP and registration tests pass, and ruff passes.
- Not done: FEP has not been rerun with this mapping. Since it can now start from the orientation the mutant prefers, the forward/reverse disagreement for S273F (2026-11-05 entry) may shrink, but this is an untested hypothesis.
- The working tree still contains the separately added, uncommitted guardrail (`check_dummy_placement`, `fep_dummy_misplaced`). Kept as insurance.

## 2026-11-10 — Reran the 68 attempts of test-v7 that failed because of a GPU fault (GPU 3 on c196), and corrected the numbers

- **Cause**: GPU 3 on compute node c196 was broken (drained at 11-04 11:21 by the healthcheck with "GPU uncorrected ECC errors=1"). OpenMM either stopped within seconds with `No compatible CUDA device` / `The requested CUDA device could not be loaded`, or silently ran on the CPU and was cut off at 20 minutes. MDClaw's `gpu_allocated_platform_unavailable` worked correctly by stopping before computation, but its guidance text said "add `--nv`", which was not the cause this time (improvement candidate: name the failed GPU and advise resubmitting on another GPU).
- **The 68 affected attempts** (ran on c196 and failed because the GPU was unusable; identified by GPU memory 0 in sacct and by the logs): test-v7-base 47, test-v7-sifonly 15, test-v7m 6. None in test-v7-cli, MDCrow, or the no-DAG experiment.
- **Rerun**: from working copies of each experiment's MDDataBench version (acfbbb7, 3d601c3, 4b8c8b9), `reset_attempts --reason gpu_fault_c196 --force true`, `SBATCH_EXCLUDE=c139,c196`. The original records were kept under each attempt's `retired/`. test-v7-base was run with the pi skills reverted to 8aa6be6, then returned to main after finishing (`runs/test-v7-base/chain-rerun-c196.sh`, log).
- **Results (pass^3, 124 cells)**: the current version (optimized) went tools-only 109→**111**, tools + skills 117→**119**. The pre-optimization version (8aa6be6) went tools-only 67→**84**, tools + skills 100→**112**. Between before and after development, 37 improved and 3 regressed. The gap between tools-only and tools + skills went from 33 to 28 (pre) and 8 (optimized). Container-only went pass@1 20→21/372. For the membrane task 7DTD, tools + skills 12/12, tools-only 11/12.
- **Paper**: updated the numbers in Figure 3, the Abstract, and Results (`tex/figures/refresh_after_rerun.sh`). Figure 3g was replaced with a breakdown of failed checks.
- Correction: in the earlier 11-04 version comparison (67/100 vs 109/117), the pre-optimization version was underestimated because of the GPU fault. This is revised to 84/112 vs 111/119.

## 2026-11-09 — Applied the process audit to the with-DAG control too (0/343). Metrics other than success rate

- In the control runs/test-v7-cli cli_sif (360 attempts, 343 passed), traced parents back from the scored production (the last completed prod) to examine the lineage. The same questions as the no-DAG audit, checked against the `node.json` records: stage order (prep → solv → topo → min → eq → prod), whether all nodes in the lineage are completed, whether prep, topo, min, and eq are in the lineage, whether the system.xml sha recorded by min, eq, and prod matches the current file of the topo in the lineage (overwrite after use), and whether eq's starting point is in the lineage. The script was for this work only (audit_dag.py in the scratchpad) and was not added to the repository.
- Result: **of the 343 passing attempts, 0 had a process defect**. Without the DAG, 11 of 334 passing attempts (3.3 %). Even across all 360 attempts including failures, the only problems were 8 with no production and 1 with no job folder.
- Limitation: the with-DAG records do not hold the sha of production's starting state (the resolver passes the parent node's artifacts, so the agent cannot swap them). This one item is "guaranteed by code", not "verified from records".
- The statement "structurally cannot happen with the DAG" in the 2026-11-07 entry is now a measured value (0/343). The denominator for no-DAG is 334 (as in the 11-07 table). Saying "11 of 343" during the conversation was wrong.
- **Correction to the 11-07 breakdown**: re-examining the 11 cases one by one, the breakdown was 6, 2, 3, not 9, 1, 1. 6 cases where eq started from the topo state instead of min's output (min ran but its output was not used); 2 cases where prod also started from the topo state (148 1hoe glm r2, 150 1kpt deepseek r1; min, eq, and prod all read the same topo state); 3 cases where the structure was edited or replaced outside the recorded stages (146 5o14 glm r3: modified after writing the prep output and before solvation; 149 5n76 qwen r2: solvation read a prep intermediate file; 153 1d4t qwen r3: the topology was built from a structure the agent wrote). The topo state has only build_amber_system's short initial relaxation (10 iterations) and is no substitute for the minimization stage. Fig. 4a of the paper uses this 6, 2, 3 (paper_mdclaw tex/figures/data/nodag_ablation_audit.json).
- Metrics other than success rate (control → no DAG, 360 attempts each): episodes with tool failure 41 → 147, Slurm job failures 1 → 23, abandoned episodes 30 → 97, recovered episodes 49 → 65. Median agent working time 438 → 457 s, median LLM calls 37 → 36, total GPU time 31.8 → 29.8 h, MD jobs 1141 → 1162. With-DAG node failures (retries via branching) have no counterpart without the DAG, so they are not counted among the failures.
- Paper (~/paper_mdclaw, 319504a-3016d92): rewrote the Abstract and Introduction around the axis "in research without a reference, whether to trust a result is decided by the process, and the tool writes that record". MDDataBench (verification of results) and the DAG (verification of the process) are written as complementary verifications, and the ablation reports "11 of the successful attempts had process errors". Sections for Results and Methods are not yet added. The ablation covers 30 systems excluding membrane systems, a different population from the 31 systems in the main text.

## 2026-11-07 — Ablation results for MDClaw without the DAG (test-v7, CLI only, 360 attempts)

- The control is cli_sif in runs/test-v7-cli (6524d3e); the main run is runs/test-v7-nodag (ablate-no-dag 2a447a3, MDDataBench nodag-ablation). Scorer fixes and rescoring are in runs/test-v7-nodag/CORRECTIONS.md.

  | | Control (with DAG) | No DAG |
  |---|---|---|
  | pass^3 (120 cells) | 108 | 103 |
  | Passing attempts (360) | 343 | 334 |
  | Passed but process defective (audit) | — | 11 |

- Per cell, no-DAG was better in 5 and worse in 10 (sign test p ≈ 0.30, not significant). For this task set, the DAG's contribution to the pass rate is small.
- Failures specific to no-DAG (9): forgot to pass disulfides to the topology (143, 144 glm), prod ran at the default NVT, 300 K (136 kimi r3), file hand-off failures in chained jobs (3 in 145). All are of the kind where the computation finishes normally, or that would not occur with the DAG.
- 11 attempts passed scoring but had process defects: 9 where eq or prod did not start from the previous stage's output (2 of them ran production without equilibration), 1 where an input was overwritten after being consumed, 1 that used a structure that was not the preparation stage's output (2 cases of only `record_not_in_ledger` were excluded for reasons on the audit side). With the DAG, input resolution and stage-order checks make these structurally impossible. The scorer only looks at final artifacts, so this difference does not show in pass.
- Command complexity (median number of arguments, with DAG → without): build_amber_system 1 → 5, solvate_structure 2 → 5, prepare_complex 3 → 5. Call counts: solvate 286 → 695, build 289 → 517. LLM calls and output tokens are about the same (37 → 36 calls, +6 %).
- In trial run 1, 9 of 16 attempts were lost to guessing the file layout before it was documented (resolved by fixing and documenting where outputs go).
- Conclusion: the essential contribution of the DAG lies not in the pass rate but in preventing "errors that look like normal completion" and in traceability of the process. Without the DAG, tracing required a hidden ledger, sha matching, and three fixes to the scorer.

## 2026-11-06 — Implemented the no-DAG MDClaw ablation and started the main run on test-v7

- Purpose: compare against an MDClaw with the entire DAG layer removed (splitting and recording of stages, automatic input resolution, carry-over of conditions, enforcement of dependencies and branching) and the same chemistry code. The control is cli_sif in test-v7-cli (6524d3e, pass^3 108/120, per run 343/360). No skills.
- MDClaw: branch `ablate-no-dag` (worktree ~/mdclaw-nodag, from 6524d3e). `MDCLAW_NO_DAG=1` hides the DAG commands and `--job-dir/--node-id`, and each command works with explicit paths and `--output-dir`. Outputs are written directly into `--output-dir` with fixed names, and their locations are stated in `--workflow` / `--list-json`. No carry-over of conditions at all (the standalone behavior of reading the JSON next to the PDB was also disabled). Each call leaves `mdclaw_result.json` (sha256 of inputs and outputs) and a ledger. Design: `docs/research/no-dag-ablation.md`. Final image `/data1/$PROJECT/sif/mdclaw-0.6.15-nodag-2a447a3-arm64-cuda13.sif` (sha256 4c9bd396…, 2a447a3). The fast tests in normal mode: 3140 pass; the 1 failure is a pre-existing Molstar wrapper problem that also fails on 6524d3e.
- MDDataBench: branch `nodag-ablation` (5b44e11). Condition `cli_nodag_sif`. The agent writes the final production folder in `submission.json`, and `mddatabench/nodag.py` reconstructs the lineage from the records and runs it through the same scorer. Provenance problems are reported as `provenance_ok`, separately from pass/fail.
- Trial runs (train only): run 1 5/16 (10 were mistaken guesses of an undocumented output subdirectory → fixed by flattening the outputs), run 2 18/20, run 3 6/8. Three independent reviews found implicit carry-over from the JSON next to the PDB, concatenation of separate productions, scoring of failed calls, ledger gaps within a job, and misidentification of helper outputs; all were fixed.
- Real failures that appeared without the DAG: (1) production was split into 2 segments with the same output destination, and segment 1 was overwritten (only 0.5 ns left); (2) forgot to pass the ligand charge (`--ligand-chemistry`) to solvation, and the system was charged −2 (glm and kimi, 039). Neither would occur with the DAG because of automatic carry-over.
- Main run: runs/test-v7-nodag, 360 attempts (30 tasks × 4 models × 3), started 2026-11-06 17:58, 8 agents. Task texts are byte-identical to the control in 30/30.

## 2026-11-06 — Counted the content of failures and recoveries from the logs of the 3 versions of test-v7 (groundwork for the ablation)

- Material: each attempt's `result.json` `recovery.episodes` (failure episodes and recovery means counted by MDDataBench), `failure_code`, `scoring_failures`. 720 attempts for each of the 3 versions (CLI + skills and CLI only, 360 each).

  | | 08-27 | 09-10 | 11-01 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Attempts containing failure episodes | 480 | 512 | 120 |
  | Attempts recovered by branching to a new node (of which passed) | 314 (274) | 357 (302) | 74 (69) |
  | `node_terminal` / `node_context_required` / `node_failed` episodes | 183 / 98 / 111 | 199 / 103 / 261 | almost 0 |
  | Slurm job CANCELLED + FAILED episodes | 45 | 265 | almost 0 |
  | `forcefield_water_blocked` episodes | 119 | 119 | 0 |

- Reading: the gains across versions come mainly from "fail, then fix by branching" turning into "do not fail in the first place". DAG-related execution errors (rerunning a finished node, missing node specification, Slurm jobs that ran before the parent finished) have nearly disappeared. Retry by branching was the most used DAG feature, used by about 40-50 % of attempts in the old versions. The node failures remaining in 11-01 are mostly `blocking_ligand_failure` (77, of which 68 recovered). Not fixed in any version: `agent_no_submission` (8-10 per condition).
- Limitation: each version differs in its whole environment, so this cannot establish which feature caused what. Causation needs an ablation. In 11-01 refusals themselves are rare (attempts that got a refusal code: CLI + skills 33, CLI only 58, nearly all passed), so an ablation of the current version may show a small pass^3 difference.
- Aggregation scripts: refusal codes were counted with `guard_stats.py` in the session scratchpad (picks `code` from transcripts). The episode counts can be reproduced from `result.json` alone.


## 2026-11-05 — Compared 3 versions on the unseen test-v7 (hackathon 94eb819, first campaign 8aa6be6, current 6524d3e)

- pass^3 (sum over 4 models, out of 120).

  | Condition | 08-27 (hackathon) | 09-10 | 11-01 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | CLI + skills | 111 | 97 | 115 |
  | CLI only | 77 | 66 | 108 |

- 08-27 → 09-10 is a significant regression (23 newly solved, 48 no longer solved, p = 0.004). Using 09-10 alone as the baseline would exaggerate the gain with skills.
- 08-27 → 11-01: CLI only improved greatly, 33 to 2 (p = 3.7e-8). With skills, 111 → 115, nearly flat (no significant difference). Development did not raise the ceiling with skills; it made the tasks solvable with the tools alone. The difference between with and without skills shrank from 34 tasks to 7.
- Caution: each image has a different environment (8/27 and 9/10 are conda with OpenMM 8.5.1; the current one is pixi with 8.6.1). Part of the 9/10 drop may be due to rebuilding the environment; this was not separated. Details in `runs/RESULTS-test-v7.md`.

## 2026-11-05 — Extension of NcPNG1 S273F (FEP +30 ns per window, plain MD +500 ns). Updates the ΔΔG in the 2026-11-03 entry

- Request: "You may extend the S273F FEP calculation and the plain-MD validation by about another 24 hours, so improve the precision." Working location is the same as in the 2026-11-03 entry, `/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/pngase/study`.
- What was extended:
  - The FEP folded legs (forward S273F, reverse F273S g− and g+): 36 nodes, 1 GPU per node, +30 ns per window (40 ns total). 6,500 s per window, 12.7-14.5 hours per node.
  - plain MD at 310 K (3 F273, 3 WT) +500 ns with `--continue-from` (about 0.94 µs total). `run_production`'s time-estimate protection refused 600 ns with `production_exceeds_time_limit`, so it was set to 500 ns. The `core/prod_041` created at the time of the refusal remains unexecuted (the actual extension is `prod_045`).
- ΔΔG after extending the folded legs (kcal/mol; SD over 3 replicas). **Replaces the 3 S273F rows in the 2026-11-03 entry.** The tripeptide legs are unchanged.

  | Calculation | 11-03 | 11-05 | SD (11-05) | DAG nodes |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | S273F forward | +6.38 | **+5.23 ± 0.02** | 0.18 (before 0.92) | `core` analyze_262-265 (estimate_ddg) |
  | S273F reverse, g− | +3.58 | **+3.77 ± 0.02** | 0.30 | `fep_rev_gm` analyze_021-024 |
  | S273F reverse, g+ | +2.93 | **+2.89 ± 0.02** | 0.25 | Subtraction only (separate job; no DAG node) |

  - The difference between forward and reverse (g−) shrank from 2.8 to 1.5, but 2.3 remains between forward and g+. The spread is small, so we read this not as insufficient sampling but as the rearrangement around Phe not being finished even at 40 ns. The true value is +2.9 to +5.2; the average of forward and reverse is about +4.1 to +4.5.
  - The minimum overlap between adjacent windows is 0.083-0.11, no warnings. S273A (+0.38), S279L (+4.16, forward only), and I390V (+0.05) are unchanged.
- plain MD (310 K, t ≥ 100 ns, mean ± SD over 3 runs). **Replaces the 440 ns values in the 11-03 entry.**

  | Metric | WT | F273 (S273F) |
  |---|---|---|
  | Local RMSD 230–300 (nm) | 0.141 ± 0.005 | 0.160 ± 0.017 |
  | Core RMSD (nm) | 0.203 ± 0.010 | 0.219 ± 0.037 |
  | SASA of residue 273 (nm²) | 0.084 ± 0.001 | 0.487 ± 0.037 |
  | Waters within 0.45 nm of the side chain (count) | 3.05 ± 0.20 | 8.36 ± 0.51 |
  | Hydrophobic SASA (nm²) | 60.5 ± 0.8 | 61.1 ± 0.1 |

  - In all 3 runs the fold is maintained up to about 0.94 µs, and Q (whole backbone) is 0.99 or higher.
  - Only F273 r1 showed a transient deviation at 100-300 ns (100 ns mean of local RMSD 0.295 nm) and returned by 800 ns to 0.13-0.14 nm, the same as WT.
  - The SASA of 273 decreases slowly over 900 ns in all 3 runs, from 0.57-0.67 to 0.31-0.45 nm², and the waters also drop from 9-10 to 6-8. This is a tendency of Phe to sink slowly into the cavity, consistent with the slow relaxation of the FEP folded leg.
- Impact on the verdicts:
  - H1 and H4 are unchanged (only the range of H4 is updated as above). H2 and H5 are also unchanged.
  - Falsification clause (if stable for about 1 µs, then the kinetic side): the condition was met (3/3 stable at 0.94 µs). However, a destabilization of 3-5 kcal/mol does not show up as loss of the fold in µs MD of the native state, so this MD cannot distinguish thermodynamic destabilization from kinetic misfolding. The basis for ΔΔG lies in the FEP.
- Analysis changes: `scripts/metrics.py` now reads multiple comma-separated prod directories (parent, extension) with continuous time (the original is `scripts/metrics.py.bak_before_ext`; the old results are in `analysis/attic_pre_ext/`). New: `scripts/submit_fep_fold_ext.py`, `submit_md_ext.py`, `block_stats.py`.
- Cost: FEP 490 + MD 136 + analysis 0.6 = 626 GPU-h (about 157 node-hours), about 190,000 yen (210,000 yen including tax). Together with the 11-03 portion, 1,624 GPU-h (about 406 node-hours).
- Registration: the metrics for the extended MD are registered in 6 `metrics_*` nodes. How `generate_md_report` should aggregate replicates is still undecided.

## 2026-11-03 — Tested the 5 hypotheses for NcPNG1 S273F (un-7) with MDClaw (`/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/pngase/study`)

- Systems: the core 47–368 of AF v6 model Q7SI01 + Zn (Zn placed by hand at C150/153/182/185; biomni's "no cofactor" was wrong), and 47–412 with the C-terminus. ff19SB + OPC, HMR 4 fs, SIF 0.6.15 pinned. WT, S273F (3 chi1 rotamers), S273A, and S279L at 298/310 K × 3 runs × about 440 ns; the C-terminal systems WT, I390V, S273F, and S273F/I390V at 310 K × 3 runs × about 265 ns; NVT at 400/450 K, 3 runs × 100 ns each.
- Folding ΔΔG (hybrid FEP, folded leg 31 windows × 10 ns, tripeptide leg 24 windows × 40 ns, minimum adjacent overlap ≥ 0.08):

  | Mutation | ΔΔG (kcal/mol) | SD over 3 runs |
  |---|---|---|
  | S273F forward | +6.38 | 0.92 |
  | S273F reverse, from relaxed F273 (g−) | +3.58 | 0.14 |
  | S273F reverse, from g+ | +2.93 | 0.29 |
  | S273A | +0.38 | 0.54 |
  | S279L (forward only) | +4.16 | 1.08 |
  | I390V (21 windows × 5 ns) | +0.05 | 0.03 |

  The difference between forward and reverse is about 3 kcal/mol, which shows that relaxation of the folded leg is insufficient at 10 ns/window. We read the true value as lying within this range. The forward/reverse difference of the tripeptide leg shrank from 4.2 kJ/mol at 10 ns/window to 2.3 kJ/mol at 40 ns/window.
- Verdicts:
  - H1 is supported in the form "Phe does not become fully buried". SASA273 at 310 K is 0.54 nm² for F273, 0.085 for WT, 0.040 for S273A. Waters near the side chain: 9.1 vs 2.9. On the other hand, the LJ repulsive term of residue 273 is the same as WT (14.0 vs 13.2 kJ/mol), and the RMSD of 230–300 shows no difference at 298 K either. In other words, it is neither a persisting steric clash nor local unfolding.
  - H2 is not supported. WT's OG273–E233 hydrogen bond breaks within 50–200 ns in all 6 runs, and its occupancy after 100 ns is 0.017 at 310 K and 0.086 at 298 K. The E233 carboxyl group becomes hydrated. S273A, which lacks this bond, has ΔΔG near 0 and MD the same as WT.
  - H3 shows only a weak trend. At 100 ns no system unfolds globally (mean of whole Q ≥ 0.91). Core RMSD at 450 K is F273 0.47±0.10, WT 0.33±0.12 nm, overlapping within the SD.
  - H4 is supported.
  - H5 is not supported. PCA, inter-subdomain distance and tilt, Rg, and hydrophobic SASA are all within the inter-replica SD.
  - The falsification clause (if stable at 1 µs, then kinetic misfolding) cannot be judged because 1 µs was not run. At 0.44 µs × 3 runs the structure is stable, so we read the destabilization shown by FEP as thermodynamic.
- Cost: 212 jobs, 998 GPU-h (250 node-hours), about 300,000 yen (330,000 yen including tax). Wall time of the heavy computation was about 21 hours.
- Bugs found (the repository was not changed):
  1. `build_hybrid_system` does not overlay the appearing side chain onto the disappearing one. In the tripeptides for S273A, S279L, and F273S(g+), the dummy was placed 160–180° on the opposite side (CB 5-coordinate, dummy bond energy 239–439 kJ/mol). These 3 legs were discarded and rebuilt. A guardrail that checks the angle between the old and new side chains on CB is needed.
  2. `_ALPHAFOLD_MODEL_VERSION="v4"` in `mdclaw/research/fetch.py` gives 404 (the DB is v6).
  3. `analyze_q_value` stops with a ValidationError unless `native_pdb` is passed, and does not infer it from the DAG. Also, 2 lines from dcdplugin leak to the start of stdout.
  4. When the same window run from the same equilibrated state with a different seed still gave NaN, extending the equilibration node by 0.5 ns fixed it (r3 of the S273F folded leg).
  5. In our own analysis, superposing before applying the minimum image across periodic boundaries breaks Zn–SG and LJ (fixed).
- `generate_md_report` stopped with `report_selection_required` (302 candidates). It is waiting for a specification of how to aggregate replicates.

## 2026-10-31 — Investigated the agent-side causes of the 46 failures in the held-out test test-v6-cli and fixed 5 tool-side defects in MDClaw (branch `test-v6-fixes`, unmerged)

User request: "Investigate the causes of the failures and fix what should be fixed in MDClaw." Target: `/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/runs/test-v6-cli` (720 attempts, 46 failures). Image `/data1/$PROJECT/mdclaw.sif` (main `ac0e328`), pi skills 8f45de7. The scoring side (scorer, tasks) is handled by someone else, so MDDataBench was not touched. Working files are in the session scratchpad (`condense.py`, `codes.py`, `grepcalls.py`, etc.).

**1. No submission (`agent_no_submission`, 19 cases)**
- **7 cases of 106_metal_6rnt (kimi CLI + skills r1–r3, qwen CLI + skills r1–r3, qwen CLI only r2): an MDClaw bug**
  - `build_amber_system` was refusing 2'-AMP (`2AM`) with `unsupported_modified_nucleic_residue`. prep treats 2AM as a ligand and records its SMILES and charge −2 in `ligand_chemistry.json`. Even so, a string-based check (4 or more sugar-phosphate atoms and not in the AMP/ADP/ATP allowlist) regarded it as a modified nucleotide.
  - 29 of 30 attempts hit this refusal at topo_001. Every successful attempt used a workaround: renaming the residue to AMP (kimi CLI only r1/r3, "to pass nucleic guardrail"), changing atom names to the old `*` notation (glm CLI + skills r1), or hand-writing an ffxml and assembling with `build_openmm_system` (glm CLI + skills r3).
  - kimi solves it with CLI only but not with CLI + skills because the skill says "do not rewrite the source to get around validation". kimi r1 did not rename the residue, and from the refusal at 307 s until 1,800 s it read `content_detection.py`, tried Pablo's matching, attempted to assemble with tleap, and ran out of time. The refusal's next_action "use modXNA" was also wrong.
- **6 cases of 110_complex_3k1r and the `production_incomplete` of qwen CLI only r3: an event in the measurement environment, not MDClaw**
  - 7 of the 8 agents running at the time terminated simultaneously at 05:13:22–23 UTC (exit_reason `error`, rc 1, stderr `unshare: sigprocmask unblock failed`). Elapsed time since start varied, 64–826 s. Only kimi CLI + skills r2 survived.
  - qwen CLI only r3 stopped just after submitting min and eq, and prod remained unsubmitted. Handed to the person in charge of the scoring side.
- **4 qwen cases of 105_ligand_6mj7: mainly insufficient guidance from the tool**
  - split reads the free L-Arg (label chain E, author A:204) as a 1-residue protein component. Hence `--include-ligand-resnames ARG` gave "not found". Selecting chain E as protein lets prep pass, but `build_amber_system` failed with OpenMM's "No template found for residue (ARG) ... matches CARG" (26 of 30 cases).
  - The remaining means was `--ligand-components`, and the agents ended up guessing residue names (ARG refused; ARGL and ARGX refused as 4 characters) and SMILES.
  - qwen CLI only r2 additionally created a practice study under `$TMPDIR` and did not use the real study (model error).
- **101 qwen CLI only r2 and 119 qwen CLI only r1: model errors**
  - In 101, after topo completed, the agent took the absence of X–H bonds from HarmonicBondForce (natural, since they are constraints) to be a bug and investigated for over 15 minutes.
  - In 119, the agent kept running its own OpenMM benchmark and energy cross-check on the login node's GPU for about 1,000 s.

**2. Composition failures (8 cases: 109 glm CLI only r1, qwen CLI only r3, qwen CLI + skills r2; 115 qwen ×2; 116 qwen ×2; 117 qwen r2): all unrequested terminal caps**
- Every attempt has 1 or 2 extra residues (ACE or NME). The S–S bond failures are merely the result of numbering shifted by one (M1:20 vs M1:21).
- 7 of the 8 started with `--cap-termini` and were refused with `terminal_cap_on_native_terminus`. Following its next_action "Drop --cap-termini and cap only the cut termini with --n-terminal-cap ACE", they capped only one side. In other words, the tool was recommending caps.
- In 117 both ends are cut ends, and `--cap-termini` passed as is.

**3. One-off failures**
- **112 qwen CLI only r2 (measured temperature 318 K, setting 298 K): a single run on 4 GPUs ran hot**
  - prod was run with `--gpus 4 --device-index 0,1,2,3` and averaged 318 K from the first frame. The eq run on 1 GPU had held 298 K (kinetic energy 94.5k → 100.1k kJ/mol).
  - The docstring of `run_production` gave `"0,1"` as an example.
- **105 qwen CLI + skills r2: the charge is +1, but not the requested chemical species**
  - After the charge refusal, it passed with `N[C@@H](CCCNC(=[NH2+])N)C(O)=O` (both amine and carboxylic acid neutral, only the guanidinium +1). The total is +1, but it is not the zwitterion, so it missed in the scoring SMILES match.
- **106 glm CLI + skills r3 (no `parameters.water_model`): an MDClaw bug**
  - `build_openmm_system` never set water_model, and there was no water model in `amber_metadata.json` or in the node metadata (the water in the solution was solv's TIP3P).
- **109 glm CLI + skills r3 (only the fluctuation magnitude at 1.78 Å, limit 1.70 Å): regarded as sampling variance** (not a model error).
- **Out of scope**: 4 cases of 105 CLI only (only the S–S bond check is "not comparable"). 3 of them kept the free Arg as a 1-residue protein and passed a hand-made SDF via `--ligand-chemistry` (these stop upstream at the prep refusal below). The 10 cases of 114 (fluctuations) are also handed to the scoring side.

**What was fixed** (branch `test-v6-fixes`, from main `ac0e328`)
- **Free nucleotides**: added `ligand_residue_names` to `detect_nucleic_content`. A residue handled by ligand_chemistry that is not connected to a chain by an O3'–P bond (within 1.9 Å) is not regarded as a modified nucleotide (`ligand_parameterized_nucleotides`).
  - Modified residues connected to a chain are refused as before, even with the same name.
  - When a free nucleotide has no ligand_chemistry, the next_action is now "reselect in a new prep with `--include-ligand-resnames 2AM`; do not rename the residue".
  - Rebuilding topo with the fixed checkout on a copy of the kimi CLI + skills r1 DAG completed with 2AM as is (ff99SBildn + tip3p, 1 GAFF ligand, 40,065 atoms, validation passed, 34 s).
- **Water model in `build_openmm_system`**: the solv node's water model is put into `parameters.water_model` and the node metadata. Outside the DAG, if there is exactly one water XML, its name is used.
  - If the bundle's water XML differs from solv's water, the node is left pending and refused with `solvation_topology_water_model_mismatch`.
- **Free amino acids** (new `structure/free_amino_acid.py`; the SMILES of the 20 L zwitterions (pH 7) were checked against RDKit CIP and charge)
  - If a ligand specification points at a 1-residue protein component, returns `ligand_is_amino_acid_component`.
  - Selecting a 1-residue protein component is refused before prep with `single_residue_protein_component`. Limited to free amino acids complete with OXT (ARG 204 of 6MJ7). 1-residue stubs without OXT are used by 11 existing tests to exercise prep logic, so they pass as before.
  - Both next_actions include a ready-to-use `--ligand-components '[{"selection":"E:204-204","residue_name":"ARL","smiles":"[NH3+][C@@H](CCCNC(N)=[NH2+])C(=O)[O-]"}]' --ligand-net-charges '{"ARL": 1}'`. `ligand_component_invalid` (residue-name collision, SMILES mismatch) shows the same declaration.
  - On the real 6MJ7, typing exactly as the next_action says completed prep with ARL (+1).
- **Terminal caps**: reordered the next_action of `terminal_cap_on_native_terminus` to "if not requested, remove all cap flags; add caps to cut ends only when requested".
  - One line of the prep summary prints "terminal caps added, each an extra ACE/NME residue". The help for `--cap-termini` etc. also says "only when requested".
- **Multiple GPUs**: listing multiple GPUs in `--device-index` is refused with `multi_gpu_device_index`. In `run_guard.md_preflight` it stops before begin_node (inside one's own job, it seals the node and shows the branching command). In preflights such as `submit_job`, it shows, before sbatch, a `--script` with `--device-index` removed and `--gpus 1`.
  - To override, `MDCLAW_ALLOW_MULTI_GPU=1`. Removed `"0,1"` from the docstring of `run_production`.
- **skill**: added only one paragraph on free amino acids to `peptide-ligands.md` and one sentence on caps to `prep-chemistry.md`.
- **Registry and goldens**: added the 3 new codes to the guardrail registry table and goldens (525 codes). The CLI contract goldens are unchanged.

**Tests** (checkout overlaid on SIF `/data1/$PROJECT/mdclaw.sif`)
- ruff is clean.
- fast suite (`-m "not slow and not integration"`, excluding `test_molstar_mcp.py`): 3,109 passed / 0 failed / 5 skipped (567 s).
- `test_pipeline_nucleic_dag.py`: 2 passed. The modXNA DAG is skipped because `MDCLAW_MODXNA_DIR` is absent.
- New tests: `test_free_nucleotide_ligand.py`, `test_free_amino_acid_ligand.py`, multi-GPU in `test_md_run_guard.py` and `test_slurm_condition_preflight.py`, water model in `test_openmm_system_server.py`, and the cap next_action and summary.
- On real data, checked with 106 (topo rebuilt on a copy of kimi's DAG) and 6MJ7 (4 paths).
- No GPU jobs were submitted. The multi-GPU heating phenomenon rests on only 1 example from the campaign (the eq and prod energy records) and has not been reproduced.

**What was not fixed**
- The simultaneous termination in 110 is an event in the measurement environment.
- The derailments in 101 and 119, the initial cap choice in 117, and the fluctuation in 109 glm r3 are model errors or variance.
- The S–S bond check in 105 CLI only and the fluctuations in 114 belong to the scoring side.

## 2026-10-31 — Published all images under one tag and rewrote the README (v0.6.15)

The user: "It is a real waste to lose out because of deployment." "Make it easy to see what is supported and what is not." "Attractive and beautiful, but without undermining experts' trust." "It would be convenient if pushing a tag also built the ARM, RIKYU, and Mac versions."

- **Images**: on a `vX.Y.Z` tag, GitHub native runners build 3 kinds. `mdclaw:X.Y.Z` / `:latest` are multi-arch (amd64 = `cuda118`, CUDA 11.8, R520 or later / arm64 = `default`, CUDA 12.9, R575 or later); `mdclaw:X.Y.Z-rikyu` / `:latest-rikyu` are `cuda13`. `Dockerfile.pixi` is shared via the build args `PIXI_ENV`, `CUDA_TOOLKIT`, and `RUNTIME_IMAGE`.
- **Mac**: a "Mac image" cannot be made. SIF does not run on macOS, and Docker is a Linux VM, so it cannot see the GPU. The arm64 image can run on the CPU under Docker, and the GPU (OpenCL) is the pixi path. The README says so.
- **Pitfalls found by trying the README as written on real machines**:
  - On Linux without a GPU, `pixi install` stops for lack of `__cuda`. `CONDA_OVERRIDE_CUDA=12.9` is needed (not needed at run time; confirmed).
  - With a driver older than R575, `pixi install` runs to completion but produces an environment that cannot use the GPU. Turned the README into a per-machine table so the choice is made first.
  - The first install has a large `.pixi/bld` (`cuda118`: env 12 GB + bld 21 GB, 14 minutes). Testing 2 environments filled floyd's `/` (`default` env 16 GB + bld over 36 GB). The README states about 60 GB. Confirmed that after `rm -rf .pixi/bld` doctor still passes fully, and CUDA, OpenCL, and `test-gpu.py` pass.
  - With only `cuda118` installed, the runtime could not be found on a host without a driver (login node). Fixed `_mdclaw_pixi_env` and confirmed on the real thing.
  - The plugin is a separate checkout, so it could not see the pixi checkout on PATH, and on hosts with Singularity the startup hook was fetching the SIF. `setup-container.sh` now treats the checkout on PATH as the runtime.
- **Corrections to the text** (checked against the code): PLUMED is not container-only. Mol* is vendored ("no third-party code" was wrong). The SIF needs about 25 GB, not 60 GB. The POPC/POPG statement had no basis and was removed; the 13 bundled patches are listed (DOPC is OPC only; `membrane.md` also fixed). Vacuum systems go only up to minimization, and eq/prod are refused. ff14SB phospho is refused (roadmap fixed). SST2 is also in pixi. For analysis, the cavity hydration tool in the README example does not exist, so the example was changed.
- **Substantive differences between pixi and the container**: rebuilding PPM3 (`immers`) is container-only. ## 2026-10-31 — Viewing a supercomputer's in-progress state and outputs in Molstar from an outside Claude Desktop

The user: "I want to see in-progress state and outputs in Molstar from Claude Desktop too." "I want to see results on the internal supercomputer from Claude Desktop connecting from outside the firewall."

- Conclusion on the path: the answer is an Artifact page, which does not need the display side to reach the compute machine. `serve_molstar` cannot be reached, and the MCP viewer is not rendered in Claude Code. The coordinates go into the page and pass through claude.ai (starting private), so it cannot be used when data must not leave the compute machine.
- Holes found with real data, and fixes:
  - **Could not open a DCD being written**: a growing DCD gave `Input changed; open the viewer again with finished files`, because size and mtime were checked for exact equality. Frames counted at open time are not broken by appending, so it now allows the same file as long as it has not shrunk. `DisplayData` is a component shared by HTTP, MCP, and Artifact, so this also helps Codex's MCP viewer. Replacement and truncation are refused as before. A final frame cut off midway was already ignored.
  - **The page was in a form the current publishing path rejects**: the output of `export_molstar_page` was a fragment starting with `<title>`, and `claude-artifacts` requires a document starting with `<!DOCTYPE html>`. Changed it to a complete document.
  - **The `Artifact` tool the skill assumed does not exist in the current session**: the same function had become `publish_files`. The skill checks for both.
  - **File selection was left to the agent**: `mdclaw --job-dir J --node-id N export_molstar_page` alone determines the stage and inputs (for prod, the ancestor topo and `*trajectory.dcd`). A running node registers artifacts on completion, so the disk is read directly. While running, `in_progress: true`. min and eq write coordinates only on completion, so they return `molstar_node_not_ready` with the parent node in `next_action`. source is mmCIF, so it points to prep.
  - **Large systems could not be published**: the full-system page was 145 B/atom and hit 16 MB at about 110,000 atoms. The embedded PDB is now gzipped (88 → 17 B/atom) and decompressed with the browser's `DecompressionStream`; the full CLN025 system (19,572 atoms) went from 2.84 MB → 0.99 MB, and the computed limit is about 400,000 atoms. Production thins frames to 8 MB as before.
- In practice: while running a 10 ns production on floyd's GPU 1, exported 17 → 43 → 625 frames from the running node and republished to the same URL. Export took 6.7 seconds (17 frames). Confirmed in headless Firefox that it loads as a complete document through to Mol* loading.
- Verification: ruff clean, related pytest 257 passed, JS 15 passed. The 1 failure, `test_switch_datasets_in_one_stdio_connection[wrapper]`, is pre-existing, caused by floyd's checkout lacking a pixi environment.

## 2026-10-29 — pixi `cuda118` environment: build OpenMM from source with CUDA 11.8 and run on the GPU via pixi even with drivers older than R575

The user's questions: "Like Mol-1's `-e ".[cuda12]"`, can pixi support multiple CUDA driver versions?" "Can pixi also build OpenMM ourselves, as the SIF does?"

- Investigation of the premise: Mol-1 only chooses CUDA 13/12 via the version range of torch on PyPI (no CUDA 11). MDClaw's problem is not torch but OpenMM >= 8.5.1: conda-forge's 8.6.1 CUDA build requires `cuda-nvrtc >=12.9.86` (R575 or later), and all wheels of PyPI's `openmm[cuda12|cuda13]` are manylinux_2_34 (floyd's Ubuntu 20.04 has glibc 2.31; n1–n5's Ubuntu 18.04 has 2.27). Adding a CUDA 13 environment would not rescue more machines, since the 12.9 build also runs on R580 or later.
- `recipes/openmm-cuda118` (pixi-build + rattler-build): builds OpenMM 8.6.1 with nvcc/NVRTC/cuFFT from NVIDIA's `cuda-11.8.0` label, gcc 11, sysroot 2.17 (about 3 minutes). The product links to `libnvrtc.so.11.2` and `libcufft.so.10`; maximum glibc requirement 2.14. Stumbling blocks: NVIDIA's 11.8 `-dev` packages only require runtime `>=11.8`, so conda-forge's CUDA 13 runtime gets mixed in (pin `cuda-version 11.8.*` and the full runtime set); conda's `CMAKE_ARGS` look for libraries only in the host prefix (`CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_LIBRARY=BOTH`).
- `pixi.toml`: moved the CUDA 12.9 pin to the `cuda129` feature and added the `cuda118` environment on the `linux-64-cuda118` platform (`cuda = "11.8"`, `glibc = "2.17"`). The default environment's lock is identical to before on all platforms, except for the SST2 rev. `cuda118` has 425 packages; PyTorch/jaxlib are CPU builds; 0 packages require glibc 2.28 or later.
- **The problem of PyPI's OpenMM overwriting**: because of SST2's pip dependency `openmm>=7.7.0`, uv added PyPI's OpenMM 8.1.1 wheel. Confirmed in the pixi v0.83.0 source: the PyPI name of a source package is taken only from its own PURL, and pixi-build-rattler-build always gives `purls: None` → `conda-pypi-map` has no effect. Results of testing alternatives: (a) put the build product in a local channel and map it via `conda-pypi-map` → works, but the lock records the channel as an absolute path, and in another checkout `--locked` fails with "channels do not match". (b) an unsatisfiable env-marker in `[pypi-options.dependency-overrides]` → the wheel disappears, but the lock freshness check does not account for the override, and `--locked` fails for every environment (CI, Dockerfile). Adopted: in the SST2 fork, moved openmm to the `SST2[openmm]` extra (`matsunagalab/SST2` mdclaw branch `3dc7013`, pushed with the user's approval, 0.0.1+mdclaw.2). Updated the pins in 5 places and added a test that checks they match (resolves the outstanding item from 10/1).
- The lock uses a relative path (`openmm @ recipes/openmm-cuda118`), and in another checkout both `cuda118` and `default` pass `--locked`. Without `recipes/` the Dockerfile sees the whole lock as stale, so `COPY recipes/` was added, and `pixi install --locked` was confirmed with the same file layout as the Dockerfile. The build working trees (several GB) are excluded with `.gitignore`/`.dockerignore`. Generating the lock needs Python from the default environment with `__cuda >= 12.9`, so on floyd use `CONDA_OVERRIDE_CUDA=12.9 pixi lock`.
- GPU measurements (CLN025 19,572 atoms, 4 fs, 10 ps, pixi `cuda118` / SIF v0.6.12): floyd A6000 R550 772/800, n1 TITAN X R530 487/477, n2 1080 Ti 493/487, n4 1080 Ti 500/499, n5 2080 Ti 647/652 ns/day. On all nodes, the OpenMM CUDA check and the PME Reference comparison in `test-gpu.py` pass (−130.075944). `test-gpu.py` requires torch CUDA, so with the CPU torch of `cuda118` only the OpenMM part was reused (`/data/mdclaw/accept-cuda118/`). floyd was `down` in Slurm, so it ran on GPU 0 of the login host.
- `bin/mdclaw` (`runtime.sh`): reads the driver version from `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` (3 ms versus 0.1 s for nvidia-smi), and if older than R575 uses `cuda118` (if not installed, uses `default` with a warning and shows `pixi install -e cuda118`). It can be set explicitly with `MDCLAW_PIXI_ENV`, and if that is not installed it stops instead of silently switching to another runtime. Along the way, noticed that on a host without a driver, the exit code of `awk` brought down the whole launcher under `set -e`, and fixed it. The tests hide the host's driver to be deterministic.
- Unresolved / pre-existing: `test_container_setup_skips_when_pixi_env_exists` fails when run inside the SIF because the host's `MDCLAW_RUNTIME`/`MDCLAW_SIF` leak in (same on main). openmm-torch/PLUMED and GPU PyTorch are not in `cuda118` (SIF only).

## 2026-10-29 — Fixed a pre-existing bug where building a new membrane patch on the GPU breaks: CUDA sums forces in fixed point, so steepest descent on overlapping atoms made no progress. Redo it on the CPU (`relax.py`)

User request: "Fix the pre-existing bug" (the GPU failure of `test_pipeline_membrane_dag::test_step3_embed_in_membrane` found during SIF acceptance). Investigated in `/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/mdclaw-validation/membrane-cuda-20261029/`.

- **Isolation**
  - The failure was before equilibration, at the step that runs `build_amber_system` on the POPC patch right after packmol-memgen packs it. The energy after relaxation was 6.52e11 kJ/mol (`built_system_energy_implausible`), and the patch was not saved to the cache.
  - Built the same patch 5 ways and compared (probe, Slurm 241520). CPU passed; CUDA failed with the same value for single / mixed / double and automatic platform selection alike. It is not a precision problem.
  - At the positions after relaxation on the CPU, the per-force energies matched between CPU and CUDA (probe2). The force computation itself is correct.
  - Values before relaxation starts (probe4)
    - E0 is 5.78e11 kJ/mol for both.
    - The maximum force is 1.6e14 on the CPU and 3.7e9 kJ/mol/nm on CUDA. The CUDA value is capped by 64-bit fixed point (2^32 / kJ/mol/nm), and the direction information is lost.
    - Capped steepest descent on CUDA tried 15 steps and accepted 0. L-BFGS rose to 6.5e11, and trying once more gave the same. On the CPU it went down to -1.18e5 in 26 steps.
- **Fix** (`mdclaw/simulation/relax.py`)
  - When descent runs on a platform other than CPU / Reference and accepts 0 steps, or the maximum force is 1e9 or more (`GPU_SATURATED_FORCE_KJ_MOL_NM`), a copy of the System is made on the CPU platform and the descent is redone. For systems with constraints, a copy with the constraints turned into springs is used, as before. The coordinates are projected back into the original Context, and L-BFGS continues on the original platform.
  - The report records `cpu_fallback` (`platform`, `from_platform`, `steps`, `accepted`).
  - The body of the descent was split out into `_descent_pass`, and `_spring_context` got an argument that can specify the platform.
- **Tests**
  - Added 2 to `tests/test_relax.py`: with a stand-in Context that claims to be CUDA and inverts and caps the forces, the CPU redo untangles the overlap; with a CPU Context, no redo happens.
  - 131 tests in `test_relax.py` and `test_md_helpers.py` passed. ruff is clean.
  - In a GPU job (Slurm 241527, c167), `test_pipeline_membrane_dag.py` 5 passed (152 s). The patch was saved to the cache (`packmol-memgen+equilibrate`, run through equilibration). The same test takes 45 minutes on the CPU.
- **Impact**: building a membrane that misses the cache inside a GPU job had always failed until now (same with the pre-fix `82bc431` and the old v4fix SIF). The same relaxation routine (`minimize_robustly`) is also used by `run_minimization` and `build_openmm_system`, so this also helps other systems with large solvent overlaps right after packing.
- The shared SIF (`6d252ca`) does not yet include this fix.
- **Addendum (same day 08:52)**: put into the shared SIF (user request "update the SIF too").
  - How it was made: on top of the `6d252ca` SIF, only `relax.py` was overwritten (`apptainer build --sandbox` → rewrite the labels → regenerate `.pyc` → SIF). The result is `/data1/$PROJECT/sif/mdclaw-0.6.12-d65eca2981a4-arm64-cuda13.sif` (sha256 `8ef9e9e0…cf6c1`). The procedure is in `/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/mdclaw-validation/sif-relaxfix-20261029/`.
  - Content check: all 254 files of the baked-in package matched `d65eca2`.
  - GPU acceptance (Slurm 241860, c285): `test-rikyu-gpu.sh` PASS. The POPC patch that CUDA had refused was built with the baked-in package as is (after relaxation -1.29e5 kJ/mol, 0 accepted on CUDA, 26 in the CPU redo).
  - Swap: repointed `mdclaw.sif`, and created `mdclaw.pre-relaxfix-20261029.sif` → the `6d252ca` SIF for rollback. The old path is an alias of `mdclaw.sif`, so it automatically points here. Updated "Current SIF" in RIKYU.md (a copy from before the rewrite is in the same place).

## 2026-10-29 — Fixed together the tool-side defects of MDClaw found in the v5 investigation (branch `v5-tool-fixes`)

User request: "Fix them all together" (all of items 1-8 in the 2026-10-27 investigation entry). Fixed in parallel in 5 worktrees from main `82bc431` and combined into the integration branch `v5-tool-fixes`. Discrepancies that came up during integration were also fixed. Tests were run with the checkout overlaid on RIKYU's v4fix SIF (`test_molstar_mcp.py` excluded because the old image lacks `mcp`). The fast suite on the pre-fix main was 2,892 passed / 1 failed; this 1 failure (`test_mddb_export.py::test_concat_tool_then_cli_export_preserves_conditions`) is because a child process loads the old mdclaw inside the image, not a code bug.

- **Structure preparation** (`5d0416d`, `0e71a41`)
  - Unified chain interpretation into `split.resolve_chain_selection`. The S–S bond and metal-site filters and glycan inclusion also use the same resolution result. The S–S bonds detected in 2DD8 / 1DFJ / 3RVW went 6→9, 0→4, 5→7.
  - Added S–S bond invariants: if a deposited bond is not formed, `detected_disulfide_not_formed`; if an unbonded SG–SG < 2.5 Å exists in topo, `unbonded_disulfide_geometry`. A request to drop the deposited bonds with `--disulfide-pairs '[]'` is refused.
  - Ligands: if the charge is ambiguous among Dimorphite states, `ligand_protonation_ambiguous`; a new argument `--ligand-net-charges`; `ligand_smiles_ccd_mismatch`.
  - Caps on native termini are refused with `terminal_cap_on_native_terminus`. `--exclude-ligand-ids` that matches nothing is refused with `exclude_ligand_id_unmatched`. When a range is passed, selecting only that chain is now the default.
- **At MD run time** (`89b020e` and others): new `simulation/run_guard.py`.
  - Running MD outside a Slurm allocation is refused with `md_outside_allocation`, and the node is left pending. The refusal includes the submit_job command. To override, `MDCLAW_ALLOW_LOCAL_MD=1`.
  - An unusable platform gives `platform_unavailable`; if a GPU was allocated but CUDA is absent, `gpu_allocated_platform_unavailable`. Both are returned before begin_node.
  - Fixed eq / min and the CLI swallowing `NodeAlreadyRunningError` and sealing a running node. When declared conditions disagree, the node is left pending and the same command with the flag added is shown.
  - Stopping eq just before the time limit was put on hold because a design decision is needed. If it stops, an eq lacking its NPT stage becomes completed, and prod silently runs under NVT.
- **Slurm submission** (`2245a44`, `c0a20e1`, `30cd2cd`): submit_job / array / mps now return, at submission time, the refusals that would otherwise occur inside the job.
  - argparse checks for all tools (`script_arguments_invalid`, with a suggested fix) and refusal of placeholders (`script_placeholder_unfilled`).
  - Checks of the declared conditions of min / eq / prod.
  - Dependencies: afterok on the parent's job is added automatically. Also `parent_not_submitted`, `dependency_not_parent_job`, `dependency_unsatisfiable`.
  - Paths on `/tmp` or tmpfs give `submission_path_not_shared`. Bind extraction was switched to shlex (bug fix), and missing paths give `container_bind_missing`. `--nv` is added automatically to GPU jobs.
  - Tried on the 5,629 sbatch scripts of v5: 61 were refused, and all were jobs that actually failed (0 false positives).
- **CLI and DAG** (`27f01de` and others)
  - Removed `...` from next-step commands, and added `status_line` at the end of every output.
  - Tool-name rewriting (category-name prefix, aliases) and `node_id_value_missing`. Failures of `--output id` are written to stderr and exit nonzero. Abbreviated arguments are no longer accepted (except abbreviations of unit and plural suffixes).
  - `create_node --conditions` refuses keys that are not reported with `condition_key_unknown`, and the bug of ambiguous matching across units was fixed.
  - `inspect_molecules` / `list_source_candidates` choose the source node automatically if there is only one. Non-study directories with content and nested studies are refused.
- **Solvation** (`02058b3`, `1396c2c`)
  - The water model is inherited from the node's declared conditions, or, if not specified, refused with `water_model_required` (the default `opc` was dropped).
  - With `--no-salt`, if the solute is charged, `solvation_charged_without_ions`. The charge estimates matched in 84/84 cases of v5.
  - Builds that miss the membrane patch cache are stopped outside Slurm (pass with `--allow-patch-build`). Warnings are issued for a cubic box around an elongated solute and for systems over 500,000 atoms.
- **Fixes during integration** (`863b09a`, `60dde6d`)
  - Unified the reading of condition keys into one place (`node/condition_vocabulary.literal_condition_keys`). eq's `actual_conditions=_actual` could not be read, and `create_node` was refusing `ensemble`.
  - Submission-time checks read the reason from `_CliUsageError.message`.
  - `node_sync` no longer marks a node failed on the end of a job that is not its current submission.
  - rounds' `list[str]` arguments are passed element by element.
  - Replaced the `<stage tool> ...` guidance in `lifecycle.py` with `explain_node`.
- In each worktree's fast suite, only the same 1 failure as the pre-fix main occurred (3 tempering tests for the solvation worker were out of memory because the GPU was shared, and passed when rerun alone). The fast suite of the integrated `60dde6d` was 3,083 passed / 1 failed / 3 skipped, the only failure being the same 1 as on the pre-fix main (616 s). ruff is clean. Merged into main (`6788460`, user instruction "if the fast suite passes, merge into main"). The slow suite will be run in acceptance when the SIF is built.
- **Behavior changes**
  - MD cannot be run on login nodes.
  - Solvation requires specifying the water model.
  - Argument errors are returned as JSON.
  - Abbreviated arguments are not accepted.
  - Unknown condition keys are refused at creation time.
  - Caps on native termini are refused.

## 2026-10-27 — From the failures in the 2 CLI conditions of the 3 campaigns under the v5 conditions (glm / qwen / kimi), identified what should be fixed on MDClaw's tool side (not started)

User request: "Investigate the results of the v5 test: what should be fixed on the harness side?" Ran 3 investigations in parallel (read-only), and corroborated the main findings against the code. Target: 1,764 attempts in CLI + skills and CLI only; failures glm 11, kimi 17, qwen 138. Working files are in the session scratchpad (`details.txt`, `fails.txt`, `jobs.txt`, `login.jsonl`, `an/`).

**A. Composition and S–S bond failures (44 cases)**
- **Bug (13 cases, all 3 models): `ss_select_chains` in `prepare_complex.py:1794-1803`**
  - It first interprets the passed chain ID as a label ID and converts it to an author ID. If there is a label chain (water, etc.) with the same name as an author ID, it gets swapped for a different chain.
  - Examples: 2DD8 became H→S, 1DFJ E→I, 3RVW C→D and D→A, and the S–S bonds vanished without warning (CYS remain with SG–SG at 2.03 Å).
  - In the 36 attempts of 019 and 022, every attempt that passed author IDs failed, and every attempt that passed label IDs passed.
  - The comma-separated `--select-chains A,B,E` is not split on the `ss_select_chains` side, so the filter becomes empty. The subsequent refusal `disulfide_endpoint_unresolvable` returns a wrong next_action, and even when `--disulfide-pairs '[]'` removed all bonds it passed with only a warning (2 cases).
  - Proposed fix: use the resolution result of `split_molecules`. Add invariant checks to prep and topo (refuse unbonded SG–SG < 2.5 Å, `unbonded_disulfide_geometry`).
- **Unrequested terminal caps (10 cases)**: 8 of them are caps on native termini and can be refused (`terminal_cap_on_native_terminus`).
- **Ligand charge (3 cases)**: `ligand_chemistry._select_protonation_state` regards the first Dimorphite state as dominant (9V2 and AMH became −1). If there are multiple candidates, refuse as ambiguous, and allow the expected charge to be passed via the CLI.
- **Other**: number ranges of fusions (2 cases), missing residues could not be built from a source with no sequence (3 cases), a non-matching `--exclude-ligand-ids` was silently ignored (1 case), etc.

**B. MD execution failures (qwen 59, glm 1, kimi 3)**

Most occur in the same pattern. Submission succeeds, the first MD inside the job fails immediately, and the successors are cancelled by afterok. submit_job's preflight only looks at run_production's conditions.
1. `--script` arguments become invalid in the argparse inside the job (14 cases). The `next` command was printed with `...`, and there are 3 cases of pasting it. Add an argparse pre-check for all tools (`script_arguments_invalid`, suggesting close flags), and make `_envelope.py` not print `...`.
2. Paths not present on compute nodes (11 cases): `/data1/$USER`, `/tmp`, outside the workspace, etc. On the sandbox's tmpfs, even mistyped paths end up existing. Return `submission_path_not_shared` in submit_job.
3. Disagreement between eq's declared conditions and the actual values (6 cases as final failures; 36 nodes in qwen's CLI + skills). Extend the preflight to eq and min too. Do not seal a node in which nothing has run as failed.
4. Condition keys that the tools do not report are accepted at creation time (5 cases). Refuse them in `create_node`. Do not ambiguously match aliases with different units (`_ps` and `_ns`).
5. **Bug (4 cases)**: `(\S+)` in `_base.py:167` puts paths containing quotes into binds. Split with shlex.
6. **Bug (4 cases)**: the generic `except` in eq / prod / min turns a duplicate-run `NodeAlreadyRunningError` into fail_node.
7. GPU allocated but no `--nv` (3 cases). No dependency or a wrong dependency (2 cases, including glm's 026): `parent_not_submitted`, `parent_dependency_missing`.

**C. Things that waste the agent's time**
- **The biggest item: running MD directly on the login node**
  - 97 attempts in qwen, about 52,400 s in total. 19 of qwen's 35 timeouts. Also the cause of OOM.
  - Specifying `--platform CUDA` sealed the node as failed with `unhandled_error` (21 cases).
  - Proposed fix: refuse min / eq / prod outside a Slurm allocation (`md_outside_allocation`, next is submit_job). For an unusable platform, return `platform_unavailable` without sealing the node.
- **preflight reasons are lost**: `preflight.py:308` discards argparse's message and returns only "Cannot validate … : 2" (28 attempts).
- **id mode**: when `--output id` fails, it just prints an empty string (about 36 attempts).
- **`tool_not_available`**: 113 attempts. The suggestion list is empty, and invocations prefixed with the server name and aliases are not supported.
- **Malformed `--conditions` is let through at creation time** (56 attempts).
- **The default water model for membrane and solvation is `opc`** (`water.py:232`, `membrane.py:2027`): refused as a mismatch at topo (13 attempts). If the membrane patch cache misses, building takes 1,100–1,400 s.
- **`| tail` cuts off the head of the envelope** (441 attempts). Put a one-line summary at the end too.
- **`bootstrap_md_workflow` does not refuse the workspace root or the HOME that `--containall` gives** (6 cases created the DAG outside the contract).

**Proposed priority** (from case count, actual harm, and ease of fixing)
1. The chain-resolution bug for S–S bonds and the invariant checks
2. Refusing MD outside an allocation, and handling of platforms
3. Making the submit_job preflight cover all tools (return argparse's reason, refuse `...`, check conditions, paths, and dependencies) and the bind-extraction bug
4. Swallowing of `NodeAlreadyRunningError`
5. Default water model
6. Choice of ligand protonation state
7. Terminal caps
8. Improved error display (`tool_not_available`, id mode, one line at the end of the envelope)

## 2026-10-27 — Conclusions on the 2 uninvestigated v5 items: qwen's 2 `execution_evidence_unavailable` and SIF only's `scorer_error` (qwen 42, glm 7, kimi 0) are both submissions that did not follow the contract's location or format. Pass/fail is unchanged

User request: "Investigate the 2 cases that failed with empty details, and why there are so many scorer_errors."

- **2 `execution_evidence_unavailable` cases** (qwen, CLI + skills):
  - All 3 MD jobs were COMPLETED in both. The scorer could not find `nodes/` at the contract location `workspace/study/jobs/main`, and all 20 checks failed with `no nodes directory`.
  - 080_soluble_1ez3 r3 created the DAG at `workspace/jobs/main` (set `--study-dir` to the workspace itself).
  - 070_soluble_1bgf r2 created it with `--job-dir /home/$USER/study/jobs/main`. HOME inside the sandbox is `sandbox/home`, so the DAG remains there.
  - The prompt states "submission at study/jobs/main", so this is an agent error. Pass/fail is unchanged.
  - However, the harness's classification (stage `unknown`, empty detail) is hard to understand. Turning it into a code like `submission_not_at_contract_path` is an improvement candidate on the MDDataBench side.
- **SIF only's `scorer_error`**: in every case the scorer exited 1. Two kinds of cause.
  - 43 cases (qwen 38, glm 5): `system_signature` in `production.json` was written as a string (a hash, e.g. `"054f61318bb30f53"`). The contract (the SIF only description in `experiments.py`) is "`system_signature` with `ensemble` and `pressure_bar`", asking for an object. `signature.get("ensemble")` at `scoring.py:979` failed with AttributeError. kimi wrote an object and had 0 cases.
  - The remaining 6: 3 with no `trajectory.dcd`, 1 where lines of `energy.dat` were not numeric, 1 IndexError, 1 with no `system_signature`.
  - pass_rule is `all_weighted_checks_pass`, and if ensemble cannot be read, `thermodynamic_conditions_match_reference` does not hold. Even if the scorer did not crash, all would fail, so the SIF only numbers do not change.
  - The scorer should not crash on malformed submissions but return check failures (treat `signature` as empty if it is not a dict, make a missing trajectory a check). A fix candidate on the MDDataBench side, not yet fixed.
- Wrote this conclusion into the "not investigated" line of the qwen section in `RESULTS-v5.md`.
- **Addendum (same day)**: fixed and pushed in MDDataBench `9bd2b96`. The scorer now scores malformed submissions without crashing; exceptions become `evaluation/submission_unscorable`, and a DAG outside the contract location becomes `agent/submission_not_at_contract_path`. Rescoring the 49 cases with the new scorer: all could be scored and 0 passed. The campaign numbers do not change (details in MDDataBench's `docs/memo.md`).

## 2026-10-25 — qwen's dispatcher stopped again (06:16 JST, SIGKILL). Resumed at 07:11 with a watcher (oom-shield) that makes the agent side the preferred OOM victim

- **What happened**:
  - The dispatcher of unit `mddb-qwen-20261024-2004` ended at 06:16 with status 137 (SIGKILL). Before the stop, 681/882 finalized, 339 passed.
  - The unit's peak memory was 8.8 GB. Meanwhile the user slice (limit 64 GiB) recorded `oom_kill 25` in `memory.events`. Read as: the slice as a whole hit its limit and the kernel picked the dispatcher. Who used the memory cannot be confirmed, because there is no permission to read the journal.
  - The previous day's `OOMPolicy=continue` prevented the whole unit from stopping, but cannot prevent the dispatcher itself from being targeted.
- **Fix**:
  - Run `runs/prep/oom-shield.sh <E>` in a separate user unit (`mddb-qwen-oomshield-*`). Every 20 seconds it sets the `oom_score_adj` of the dispatcher's descendants (from the agent's `timeout` down) to 1000. It only raises values, so no privileges are needed. Descendants forked later inherit the value too.
  - The dispatcher stays at 200 (the systemd user default), so on OOM the agent side is killed first. An attempt whose agent is killed is finalized as the agent's own failure.
  - Reset the 6 in-flight attempts (078 sif_only r1–r3, 079 cli_sif r1–r3, no jobs) with `_reset_attempt`.
- **Resumed**: unit `mddb-qwen-20261025-0711`. Confirmed the 6 children have adj 1000.

- **What happened**:
  - At 19:10 a process in unit `mddb-qwen-20261024-1056` was killed by the OOM killer, and with systemd's default `OOMPolicy=stop` the whole unit stopped.
  - The user slice (`user-$UID.slice`) has MemoryMax 64 GiB. The login node itself had 1.5 TB free.

The solvent species is cross-checked among the trajectory's system signature, topology metadata, and build provenance.
- Temperature etc. are not borrowed from equilibration, earlier prod segments, dependent nodes, or declared-but-unexecuted conditions. Contradictions in build records or solvent species stop the export; if temperature/timestep records contradict the signature, it stops unless runtime XML resolves it. The same retrieval is applied to concatenated trajectories, keeping the all-segment consistency check.

## 2026-10-24 — Fixed missing simulation conditions for MDDB concatenated trajectories

These can be filled with explicit metadata applicable to all segments, but contradictions with known values or mixing between segments cannot be hidden by overriding.

## 2026-10-24 — Reproduced and worked around conda-pack's hard-link tar corruption

- Packing a minimal environment containing 2 hard links with conda-pack 0.9.2 makes GNU tar return `Skipping to next header` and exit code 2. Normal copies / symbolic links succeed, and only hard links fail even without gzip. The cause is that `TarArchive._add_bytes` attaches a content size and data to a hard-link-type header; it is not a lack of disk space. The old path can be reproduced by the regression check with `python container/scripts/test-env-relocation.py tar.gz /path/to/gtar`.
- Changed Stage 1 to `conda-pack --format no-archive --dest-prefix /opt/mdclaw`. Stage 2 COPYs the finished directory, abolishing tar generation, intermediate copies, extraction, and conda-unpack. Everything from installation to cache deletion is combined in the same RUN, so the original environment and download cache are not left in earlier layers.
- The real regression check of the new path succeeded for both names of a hard link, symlinks, execute permissions, path replacement, and preservation of binary content and original files. The same check is run inside the build. 10 deployment/doc tests, ruff, actionlint, diff and shell syntax checks passed. The real container build and behavior tests will be confirmed after push.
- Added to Actions a space log every 30 seconds and a protection that stops the builder below 5 GiB free. The published latest is not updated.

## 2026-10-23 — Added a LICENSE file and third-party license notices

User request (research how to write up the licenses of dependent software and put it at the end of the README).

- **Conventions** (Apache / Linux Foundation / OSPO guidance): the LICENSE file contains only the project's own license. NOTICE/THIRD_PARTY lists **only what is actually bundled and redistributed**, not dependencies the user installs themselves. The MDClaw repository vendors no third-party code at all, so LICENSE is pure MIT only, and the dependency list is written as an informational section of the README (the container image counts as redistribution, so this is stated along with where the license texts are).
- **Finding**: the repository had no LICENSE file at all (the README only declared MIT) → added the full MIT text, and added `license = "MIT"` / `license-files` (PEP 639) to pyproject.toml. Confirmed pip's metadata build succeeds.
- **Measured dependency licenses** (the pixi environment's conda-meta and importlib.metadata are authoritative): OpenMM LGPL-3.0+, AmberTools a combination of GPL-3.0+ AND LGPL-3.0+ AND BSD-3 AND MIT, MDAnalysis LGPL-3.0+ (not GPL), MDTraj LGPL-2.1+, ParmEd LGPL-2.1+, propka LGPL-2.1, SST2 GPL-2.0 (already isolated by running as a subprocess), RDKit/PyTorch BSD-3, PDBFixer, the OpenFF packages, pymbar, e3nn, hpacker (checked on GitHub), BioEmu, Boltz-2 MIT, dimorphite-dl and HOLE2 Apache-2.0, gemmi MPL-2.0, PyMOL its own OSS license, MODELLER proprietary (free for academics; the user supplies the key). Listed as a table at the end of the README.
