## 2026-10-23 — Introduced GitHub Actions: pixi-environment CI and automatic container build / GHCR push

User approval (1A: ci.yml, 2A: container.yml supports both automatic on tags and manual, 3A: GPU smoke stays manual). This repository's first CI.

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** (push/PR): on `macos-latest` (Apple Silicon = osx-arm64) and `ubuntu-latest` (linux-64, `CONDA_OVERRIDE_CUDA=12.9`): `setup-pixi` (with lock cache) → `pixi install --locked` (fails if the lock is stale) → ruff → standard test set + deployment/docs/wrapper tests.
- **`.github/workflows/container.yml`** (`v*` tags + `workflow_dispatch`): disk cleanup (frees about 25–30 GB) → check that the tag matches the plugin.json version → buildx (layer cache in GHCR's `:buildcache`; Stage 1 reused if the lock is unchanged) → `test-container.sh` (CPU; GPU checks SKIP by design) → on tags push `:X.Y.Z` + `:latest`; dispatch pushes the versioned tag only when `push_image` is specified.
- Replaced steps 3–4 of release.md (manual build + push) with a tag push, keeping only the GPU smoke as a manual gate. 2 caveats before the first run: (1) the existing `mdclaw` package on GHCR was created with a PAT, so unless the package settings grant write to this repository's Actions, the `GITHUB_TOKEN` push will be refused. (2) `CONDA_OVERRIDE_CUDA` on a GPU-less builder and `conda-pack` on a pixi prefix are unverified, so run it once via dispatch (no push) before the first tag (Release gates in deploy-v2-plan updated).

## 2026-10-23 — Deploy v2: unified dependencies via the pixi lock and standard Agent Skills distribution (deploy-v2-plan)

User approval (1A: unify on pixi from the dev environment through the amd64 container, 2A: standard skills distribution, 3B: one-liner deferred). Design and remaining risks are in `docs/developer/deploy-v2-plan.md`.

- **Settled by investigation**: uv alone is not possible (AmberTools, hole2, pymol-open-source, and openmm-torch are conda-only; OpenMM itself has been officially distributed on pip since 8.2). pixi resolves conda-forge + PyPI into one multi-platform lockfile (using uv internally) and handles both git pins and editables. For skills distribution, vercel-labs/skills (`npx skills add`, supports 17 harnesses) has become the industry standard and uses the same symlink mirror approach as `install-agent-skills.sh`.
- **Existing bugs that surfaced**: the committed `environment.yml` was unresolvable (every conda-forge openmm-torch build pins openmm<8.5; already recorded by conda-env-parity-plan on 9/11) → removed the line. hpacker's `biopython==1.81` pin only worked because pip silently overwrote conda's 1.88 → pixi.toml now explicitly pins 1.81 on the conda side too.
- **R1 (dev environment)**: `pixi.toml` + `pixi.lock` (673 packages, linux-64 / linux-aarch64 / osx-arm64; linux declares __cuda=12.9 to select CUDA 12.9 builds; hole2 linux only; MODELLER via the salilab feature on linux-64 / osx-arm64). Verified on osx-arm64: `pixi install` about 17 s, the tool set from `--list` exactly matches the hand-built conda environment, standard tests + wrapper/deployment/docs tests 391 passed, ruff clean. `bin/mdclaw` auto-detects the checkout's `.pixi/envs/default` with top priority (can also be explicit with `MDCLAW_RUNTIME=pixi`), `setup-container.sh` skips the pull if a pixi environment exists, and a pixi block was added to doctor.
- **R2 (container)**: replaced Stage 1 of `container/Dockerfile` with `ghcr.io/prefix-dev/pixi` + `pixi install --locked` (a stale lock fails the build immediately = no re-resolution). The separate installation steps for MODELLER, SST2, hpacker, and openff-pablo were absorbed into the lock and disappeared. Stage 2 (OpenMM 8.5.1 cu118 source build, openmm-torch pinned commit, PLUMED) and Stage 3 are unchanged. **Unverified gates**: this Mac has no Docker, so the build was not run. At the next release, on a Docker host, pass (1) `CONDA_OVERRIDE_CUDA` on a GPU-less builder, (2) `conda-pack -p` on the pixi prefix, and (3) `test-container.sh` before replacing GHCR latest / the shared SIF. Fallbacks on failure are pixi-pack or the same-path approach (see the plan doc).
- **2A (skills)**: added `skills/common/SKILL.md` to make the shared pages a proper skill (`name: common`, installed with the same sibling layout as the mirrors). Confirmed with `npx skills add ./ --list` that 14 skills including common are discovered. Changed the README / deployment.md onboarding for generated-skill agents to prefer `npx skills add matsunagalab/mdclaw` (the old script without Node).
- **Positioning**: the environment layer of conda-env-parity-plan (§1, §3) is replaced by this work. The source-build layer (openmm-torch / PLUMED / packmol fixes, §2, §4, §5) remains valid and unimplemented. `environment.yml` is kept for conda users and the rikyu-arm64 Dockerfile (the canonical source is pixi.toml). ambertools is 24.8 in the lock (floor stays >=24.0; bumping to 25/26 is a separate matter).
- Changed the development defaults in AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md to `pixi run` (conda listed alongside). Updated `configuration.md`, `container.md`, and `deployment.md`. Lockfile updates are recorded in history via `pixi update` + committing the `pixi.lock` diff.

## 2026-10-02 — CTLA-4 plain MD control (3 runs × 300 ns per start) finished: the apo start never reaches holo-type H3 (0 %, 0/3 runs, Thr103 never flips), clearly different from SST2 (3.7 %, 6/8 runs). The difference between the 2 starts' distributions (JSD) at about 900 ns per start is SST2 0.37 vs plain MD 0.75. The holo start drops from 89 % to about 45 % even in plain MD

- **Run and cost**. MPS 152390 (c232) COMPLETED (ExitCode 0:0, elapsed 19:46:37, 10/1 11:14 → 10/2 07:00 JST). prod_025–027 (md_s1–3) are all completed in every job, final_step 75 million (300 ns). Each task's `.err` has only heartbeats and separator lines. **4.94 node-h (19.78 GPU-h) = 5,933 yen (6,526 yen incl. tax)**, as estimated (cap 6 node-h). Cost per ns is almost the same as SST2 (plain MD 0.0110, SST2 0.0109 GPU-h / walker-ns). CTLA-4 cumulative total is 18.0 node-h (72.0 GPU-h), 23,751 yen incl. tax.
- **Analysis**. Added an md mode to `analyze_ctla4.py` (`run_adapter_md.sh` → `analyze_ctla4.py <study> md`). It reads the trajectories of each job's `md_*` nodes directly, with equal weights, walker = node, time = (frame + 1) × output interval, and only the 300 K rung, and aggregates with the same definitions as SST2 (60° from the crystal φ/ψ, simultaneous pattern of 3 residues, 25 ns windows, walker bootstrap, RMSD, JSD). Rungs without frames are skipped in the per-residue table (SST2 has frames on every rung, so it is unchanged). The md mode's figure title is "plain MD (300 K)". Re-ran SST2's `ext2` and confirmed `analysis_ext2.{txt,json}` match exactly. The comparison figure is `compare_sst2_md.py` → `ctla4_sst2_vs_md.png` (per-window holo pattern, and JSD vs aggregate time). Figures sent to the user.
- **Results** (300 K. SST2 is 8 walkers × 300 ns with MBAR weights; plain MD is 3 runs × 300 ns with equal weights).

| | SST2 apo start | plain MD apo start | SST2 holo start | plain MD holo start |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| joint holo H3 % [95 % interval] | 3.72 [0.88, 8.05] | **0.00 [0.00, 0.00]** | 52.9 [28.6, 74.1] | 66.5 [47.8, 87.6] |
| joint apo H3 % | 20.4 | 75.3 | 12.7 | 2.6 |
| walkers reaching the holo pattern (300 K) | 6/8 | **0/3** | 8/8 | 3/3 |
| walkers reaching the apo pattern (300 K) | 8/8 | 3/3 | 3/8 | 1/3 |
| per-residue Gly101 / Thr103 / Asn104 % (holo-like for apo start, apo-like for holo start) | 53.2 / 8.85 / 10.1 | 22.9 / **0.00** / 0.19 | 16.1 / 24.8 / 31.7 | 2.7 / 8.5 / 24.3 |
| H3 RMSD < 2 Å (apo crystal / holo copy) % | 53.9 / 16.0 | 80.2 / 2.4 | 17.6 / 46.7 | 5.2 / 72.7 |

- **Time course**. Joint holo for the plain MD holo start, in 25 ns windows: 88.9, 88.5, 87.2, 88.1, 78.3, 66.9, 68.5, 52.2, 45.1, 44.1, 44.5, 45.3 % (holds until 100 ns, then drops). Walker 2 reached the apo pattern around 225 ns (apo pattern 22.3 % in the 225–250 ns window). In the holo start, apo-like Thr103 rises to 19.2 / 28.6 % in 200–250 / 250–300 ns, and apo-like Asn104 to 40.1 / 51.6 % (unweighted). The plain MD apo start has 0.0 % holo pattern in every window. Holo-like Thr103 is 0.0 % throughout, Asn104 is at most 0.4 %, and only Gly101 becomes holo-like at 23 % (300 K).
- **JSD** (H3 RMSD distributions of the 2 starts). Plain MD at 90, 180, …, 900 ns per start: 0.982, 0.977, 0.965, 0.962, 0.935, 0.921, 0.925, 0.835, 0.780, 0.747. SST2 is 0.371 at 960 ns (the `analysis_ext2` grid) and 0.446 at 800 ns (`analysis_final` at the 100 ns point). At the same aggregate time (about 900 ns per start, with almost the same cost per ns), SST2's 2 starts are much closer.
- **Interpretation**. (1) The comparison with plain MD shows the effect of SST2. In the apo start, 6 of 8 SST2 runs reached the holo pattern vs 0 of 3 plain MD runs. The rate-limiting Thr103 flip never occurs in the plain MD apo start over 900 ns (3 runs × 300 ns). The difference between the 2 starts' distributions is about half at the same aggregate time. (2) However, compared at the same aggregate time (about 900 ns per start), the fraction of holo pattern in the apo start cannot be statistically distinguished between SST2 (100 ns × 8 runs: 0.67 % [0.00, 2.18], 1/8 runs) and plain MD (0 %). The joint-pattern difference becomes clear at 300 ns per walker (SST2 aggregate 2.4 µs, 2.7× plain MD). The metrics to claim the effect in the paper are JSD, the Thr103 flip, and the number of walkers that reach the pattern, not the 300 K fraction itself. (3) The plain MD holo start also loses the holo pattern without the antigen (89 % → about 45 %, 1/3 runs go to the apo pattern). Unlike plain MD of TPP-3077 (holds about 95 %, a kinetic trap), with this force field CTLA-4's holo H3 is not stable without the antigen. (4) Population shift (agreement of the 2 starts) is not shown even with SST2 (3.7 % vs 52.9 %). That it is not claimed is unchanged.
- **Records**. `inputs/ctla4/analysis_md.{json,txt}`, `ctla4_{joint,raster,landscape}_md.png`, `ctla4_sst2_vs_md.png`, `run_adapter_md.sh`, `compare_sst2_md.py`.

## 2026-10-01 — `--ligand-charge-method {nagl, am1bcc}`: a CLI option to switch ligand charges to AM1-BCC (default stays NAGL)

User approval ("I agree with the proposed fix; implement and test it"). The trigger was T4L's indole. NAGL (`openff-gnn-am1bcc-1.0.0`) gave N1 −0.583 e, whereas AM1-BCC with AmberTools sqm gave −0.196 e. Until now there was no way to choose AM1-BCC; it was used only as the automatic fallback when NAGL failed (`am1bcc_fallback`).

- **Implementation**:
  - Added `ligand_charge_method` (default `nagl`) to `build_amber_system` and `build_decoupled_system`.
  - With `am1bcc`, NAGL is not called; the charges carried by the molecule (from the SDF etc.) are cleared, and the GAFF template generator computes AM1-BCC for all ligands (`_request_am1bcc_partial_charges`). No persistent template cache is used (a new `SystemGenerator` per build), so even building NAGL → AM1-BCC in the same process switches charges correctly.
  - Records: the request goes in `forcefield_provenance.ligand_charge_method`, the result in `ligand_charge_assignment[]` (`method: am1bcc`, `charge_engine: ambertools_sqm` (`openeye` in environments where OpenEye is available), `status: success`).
  - Invalid values are refused with `invalid_parameter_value` (with the list of accepted values), and the node stays pending. Also added to the node's condition validation.
  - `build_decoupled_system` records the charge model actually applied to the decoupled ligand in `hybrid_manifest.ligand_charges.model` (`nagl:<model>` or `am1bcc`; requested AM1-BCC and the NAGL fallback are the same fit, so they count as the same model). `estimate_binding_dg` refuses with `abfe_legs_incompatible` if the two legs' models differ.
  - Citation selection picks Jakalian 2000/2002 for requested `am1bcc` too.
  - Docs updated: tool-reference, the md-abfe option table, md-prepare/explicit-water.
- **Error caught along the way**: inserting `_ligand_charges` right before `def build_decoupled_system(` attached `@node_tool(node_type="topo")` to the new function instead (the tool would no longer require topo). It surfaced as a diff when regenerating the CLI contract in a temporary tree with only this change on top of HEAD. Reverted, and the contract diff became 0 (the contract pins only node requirements and required arguments).
- **Tests**:
  - New `tests/test_ligand_charge_method.py`. Contents: an AM1-BCC request does not call NAGL and clears charges; invalid values are refused by both tools and the node stays pending; recording of the charge model (fallback = request); a slow real build (indole in vacuum: NAGL N1 < −0.5, AM1-BCC between −0.35 and −0.1, total charge 0, records match).
  - Added to `test_abfe.py`: refusal of legs with mismatched charge models, and that the combination of requested AM1-BCC and the fallback passes. Added to `test_evidence_server.py`: Jakalian is selected for requested `am1bcc`.
  - In a temporary tree of HEAD + only this change: ruff and the fast suite 585 passed / 1 skipped, slow 2 passed.
- **Confirmed on real data**: rebuilt both indole legs with AM1-BCC from the same solv (`l99a_ind` topo_004 / topo_005, 56,057 / 7,192 particles, endpoint validation pass, N1 −0.196, N–H H +0.298). GPU computation on Slurm 152817–152823 (`branch_run.py ind_am1bcc`).
- **Indole AM1-BCC results (3 replicas × 5 ns per window, from the same solv)**:
  - ΔG_bind is −0.89 / −0.61 / −0.78, **mean −0.76 kcal/mol**. Almost the same as NAGL's −0.57, and does not reach the experimental −4.89.
  - Leg totals: solvent leg 17.68 → 12.00 (−5.68), complex leg (excluding the analytic restraint term) 18.25 → 12.76 (−5.49); the differences nearly cancel.
  - Hydration free energy −8.39 → −6.67 kcal/mol (−9.38 → −7.66 including the LJ long-range correction). The gap to 3-methylindole's −5.88 shrank from 3.5 to 1.8.
  - Minimum overlap 0.072–0.095. Elapsed time fepc0 3:11, fepc1 1:56, feps 1:16. Boresch is Ala97 backbone ↔ C8/C9/C7, no rotation.
  - Per-phase values (e.g. NAGL complex steric phase 11.2 vs AM1-BCC 9.7) depend on the path and restraint atoms, and the restraint atoms differ between the two calculations (NAGL Ile100, AM1-BCC Ala97), so they cannot be compared. Only the leg totals are comparable. The pose (RMSD 1.2–1.9 Å, contact with Ala99 O) and Val111 (nearly trans) were the same in both calculations.
  - **Overturned**: the inference in the same day's root-cause entry that "about 80 % of indole's weak binding is explained by over-hydration" was wrong. Charges that strongly polarize N–H strengthen the interactions in the cavity (e.g. the hydrogen bond with Ala99 O) as much as the hydrogen bonds in water, and switching the charges to AM1-BCC weakens both by the same amount, leaving binding almost unchanged. Reading a hydration error as a binding error assumes the complex side is not affected by the same parameter error, and for indole that assumption does not hold (the same caution applies to other points in the figure `fig_hydration_vs_binding.png`, such as N-methylaniline).
  - The remaining ~4 kcal/mol of binding weakness does not move with the charge model and likely lies in the description of the complex side. The bicyclics (benzofuran +1.6, indene +1.7) are weak in the same direction, and in Mobley 2007 (AMBER96 / GAFF) indole was also −1.37.

## 2026-10-01 — Investigating the causes of the large T4L ABFE misses (indole +4.3, 2-nitrothiophene −4.3 kcal/mol)

User request ("explain the large misses"; also approved additional calculations for the nitrothiophene altloc B system). Working location `/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/abfe-t4l` (`diag_outliers.py`, `charges_compare.py`, `vacuum_leg.py`, `hydration_vs_binding.py`, `confb_run.py`).

- **Structure (final State of each λ window, superposed on the crystal CA)**:
  - Nitrothiophene (started from altloc A of 2RBO) stayed in crystal pose A in all 3 replicas in the bound-state windows (RMSD 0.3–1.1 Å; 1.9 Å to pose B). It does not move to B within 5 ns. The nitro O sits 3.1–3.5 Å from the Tyr88 backbone N. In the crystal the two poses have occupancy 0.5/0.5, and Met106, which lines the cavity, also has A/B conformers.
  - In the crystal (185L), indole has no polar atom within 3.6 Å of its N–H, but in MD it shifted by about 1.4 Å and hydrogen-bonded to the Ala99 backbone O (2.7–3.0 Å).
  - In neither case does water enter the cavity in the decoupled windows.
- **Per-phase contributions**:
  - For indole, the cost of discharging is 5.1 larger in water (18.8 kcal/mol) than in the cavity (13.7). It is 2.7 for indene and 1.6 for benzofuran, so indole is 2.5–3.5 larger than these.
  - Nitrothiophene comes out 2.9 kcal/mol stronger in the calculation than thienothiophene, which binds about equally strongly in experiment (−4.67 vs −4.85). The breakdown of that difference: sterics (LJ) −2.2, electrostatics −1.2, restraint and σ +0.5.
- **Charges (NAGL vs sqm AM1-BCC, same conformer)**:
  - Only indole deviated strongly. N1 is −0.583 vs −0.196, and the N–H hydrogen is +0.449 vs +0.298 (maximum difference 0.39 e).
  - The other 7 ligands (nitrothiophene, benzofuran, indene, N-methylaniline, thienothiophene, phenol, 3-chlorophenol) differ by ≤ 0.05 e.
  - However, NAGL was trained on OpenEye AM1-BCC (ELF10), and with FreeSolv's GAFF / AM1-BCC (OpenEye) 3-methylindole is also over-hydrated at −8.16 vs experiment −5.88. The difference from sqm may be an implementation difference of AM1-BCC, and cannot be pinned on an error specific to NAGL.
- **Hydration free energies of this model**: obtained by adding to the solvent leg (mean of 3 replicas) an FEP in vacuum that sets the ligand charges and intramolecular 1-4 charge products to 0 (11 windows × 0.4 ns, MBAR, cut out of `coupled.system.xml`). The LJ long-range correction was estimated analytically (−0.7 to −1.2 kcal/mol).
  - For the 16 ligands with FreeSolv experimental values, the corrected MUE is 0.95 kcal/mol and the mean error is −0.27.
  - Indole is −9.38, 3.5 more hydrated than 3-methylindole's −5.88. This explains 3.5 of the binding error of +4.32.
  - N-methylaniline is −6.57 vs −4.69, over-hydrated by 1.88. This explains almost all of the binding error of +1.91.
  - The phenols are 0.86–1.84 under-hydrated, in the same direction as over-binding in a polar cavity. However, 2-methylphenol is an outlier in the opposite direction.
  - 2-nitrothiophene is −2.53. There is no experimental value, but it is about 2 kcal/mol less hydrated than about −4.6 estimated from analog additivity (thiophene −1.40 + nitrobenzene − benzene), which is about half of the 4.3 over-binding.
  - The correlation between the binding error and "the binding error caused by the hydration error alone" is R = 0.64 (16 cases). Figure: `fig_hydration_vs_binding.png`.
  - In conclusion, the main cause of the large misses is ligand hydration in the GAFF2 / AM1-BCC family (aromatics with N–H are over-hydrated; phenols, nitro and thiophene are under-hydrated), not an error on the ABFE protocol side.
  - **(Partly corrected by later verification on the same day)** For indole, recomputing with AM1-BCC charges improved hydration by 1.7 kcal/mol, but binding barely changed, −0.57 → −0.76. This item's "explained by over-hydration" does not apply to indole (see the `--ligand-charge-method` entry).
- **Nitrothiophene altloc B system** (`m102q_ntp_b`, the full B conformer set of 2RBO, same protocol as the main calculation, Slurm 152463–152473): it kept pose B after equilibration (RMSD 0.86 Å). Boresch is Cys97 backbone ↔ CAG/NAH/CAE, with no rotation. Combining the contributions of multiple poses always moves binding toward the stronger side, so the B value cannot cancel the over-binding of nitrothiophene. What this calculation tells us is whether the over-binding is specific to pose A.
  - **Result**: ΔG_bind is −8.39 / −8.54 / −9.03, **mean −8.65 kcal/mol** (pose A is −9.18, experiment −4.85).
    - In the bound-state windows all 3 replicas stayed in pose B (RMSD 0.3–1.2 Å), so the two calculations sample two poses separately, which do not interconvert.
    - The per-phase contributions are almost the same as A (complex-side sterics 12.0–12.7 vs 12.9, discharging 4.7 vs 4.5, the solvent leg also equal). Minimum overlap is 0.056–0.076.
    - **The over-binding does not depend on pose**. In the model A is 0.53 kcal/mol more stable than B (about 7:3 at 283 K), which agrees with the crystal occupancy 0.5/0.5 to within about 0.5 kcal/mol. The value combining the two poses is −9.36.
    - Elapsed times were fepc0 3:04, fepc1 1:52, feps 1:16, about 6.4 GPU-h including the eq stages.
  - **GAFF version**: from GAFF1 → GAFF2, the LJ of the nitro N/O actually became shallower (no: ε 0.17 → 0.086, o: 0.21 → 0.146 kcal/mol). Meanwhile aromatic C (0.086 → 0.099) and ss (0.25 → 0.28) became deeper. It is not the case that "the GAFF2 nitro group is too sticky". The 3.5 kcal/mol difference from Boyce 2009's −5.73 (AMBER96 / GAFF1 / AM1-BCC / TIP3P) cannot be narrowed down to a single cause with the present data.
- **Summary**:
  - The weak binding of indole and N-methylaniline is almost entirely explained by ligand over-hydration (AM1-BCC-family charges that strongly polarize N–H + GAFF).
  - The over-binding of nitrothiophene does not depend on pose; about 2 kcal/mol is ligand under-hydration (estimated from analogs), and the rest is the treatment of the nitro group on the complex side.
  - Both are force-field-side errors, with no sign that the ABFE protocol (restraints, λ, sampling) is the cause.
  - Single-variable confirmation experiments (indole with sqm AM1-BCC charges, nitrothiophene with GAFF1) require adding charge-method and GAFF-version options to `build_decoupled_system` (currently NAGL-first and gaff-2.11 are fixed).

## 2026-10-01 — Updated the shared amd64 SIF to main `a70d16b`, and bumped the SST2 pin to `ba48461` along the way (only the mdclaw side had advanced)

main advanced 3 commits from `87e1bd1` (`fbb2496` generate report citations from each stage's record, `b011b80` leave charges of specified solute atoms unscaled in SST2, the rest docs). None of the build inputs moved, so I did an incremental build on top of `87e1bd1e7cf1` and widened the verification from `.py` only to all 226 files except `__pycache__` (this time `evidence/references.bib` grew by +157 lines, so `.py` alone is not enough).

One new failure in that candidate's suite: `test_run_sst2_charge_unscaled_subset` with `SST2 driver exited with 2`. The cause is that only the mdclaw side had advanced — `run_sst2` passes `--charge-unscaled-indices` to `SST2.driver`, but the baked SST2 is `5590f4f`, whose `driver.py` does not even contain the string `charge`, and argparse exits 2 on an unknown argument. The required commit `ba48461` "rest2: charge_unscaled_index" (9/28) had already been pushed to the fork's `mdclaw` branch; only the pins in `environment.yml` and the two Dockerfiles (+ `MDCLAW_SST2_REVISION`) had been left behind. This is exactly the spot where the repo's own comment says "bump all three together".

On the user's decision, I bumped the pin and rebuilt. Changed 3 source files (`environment.yml`, `container/Dockerfile`, `container/Dockerfile.rikyu-arm64`) from `5590f4f` → `ba48461` (**uncommitted**). The fork's `requirements.txt` is identical in both revisions, so `--no-deps` is safe. The conda git inside the image has no https remote helper, so I cloned `ba48461` on the host, pip-installed from the local path, and layered `ENV MDCLAW_SST2_REVISION=ba48461` on top. A from-scratch build gets the same revision via the git URL in the Dockerfile.

Artifact: `/data/mdclaw/mdclaw-amd64-a70d16b8a183-sst2ba48461.sif`, 5,977,489,408 bytes, sha256 `d1e9352b…` (image `sha256:6821b4eb…`). Switched over at 10/1 18:32 JST with the usual atomic relink; `mdclaw-amd64-87e1bd1e7cf1.sif` is kept for rollback. At switch time no process was holding the shared SIF.

Acceptance: `test-container.sh` 26 passed / 0 failed for both image and SIF. The 226 package files match `a70d16b` (rechecked via the shared path after the switch). `python -m SST2.driver --help` shows `--charge-unscaled-indices`, and `MDCLAW_SST2_REVISION=ba48461`. Suite: 2,637 passed / 3 failed. The remaining 3 all fail the same way with the old image + the same checkout overlay, so they are not products of this build, but all 3 need fixing on the main side (see "3 items to fix" below).

**Correction** — in the 9/29 entry just before this and in `known_failures` of `/data/mdclaw/mdclaw-amd64-87e1bd1e7cf1.manifest.json`, I wrote that the `test_pdb_writefile_inventory_is_pinned` mismatch was "EXPECTED lacks `simulation/tempering.py`"; that was wrong. That was correct only up to the 9/18 (661a80c) build; from `87e1bd1` on, the raw write in tempering.py was fixed to go through `render_simulation_pdb_preserving_resnames` and EXPECTED was updated, and the mismatch is **`simulation/metadynamics.py`**. Because the place to fix is different, I correct it here rather than overwriting. I also fixed the manifests of both images.

3 items to fix (all source-side, unrelated to the image):
1. **Raw `PDBFile.writeFile` at `simulation/metadynamics.py:771`** — not a missed pin update but a bug with real impact. `run_metadynamics` writes `final_structure.pdb` directly from `simulation.topology`, so the normalized Amber/PTM/water residue names (HIE/HID→HIS, GLH→GLU, CYX→CYS, WAT→HOH) are lost at the point where the run stage reads `topology.pdb` with OpenMM. `production.py` / `equilibrate.py` / `minimize.py` / `platform.py` / `tempering.py` all go through `render_simulation_pdb_preserving_resnames`; metadynamics is the only exception. The guard test is working correctly. The fix is to go through the same helper and add `"simulation/metadynamics.py": (1, "restore")` to EXPECTED (or remove the raw write).
2. **Tolerance in `tests/test_metadynamics.py:136`** — this one is a test-side problem. `free_energy_range_kj_mol` is computed from the double-precision `F` (`metadynamics.py:709`), but `free_energy.csv` is written with `f"{f:.6f}"` (line 715 of the same file). The test requires `f_range <= F_csv[:,1].max() + 1e-9`, so it always fails whenever the maximum rounds down (measured 13.62274711745013 vs 13.622747, difference 1.17e-7). Either match the tolerance to the file's precision (1e-6) or reconstruct F from the total bias in `.npy` and compare.
3. **Unguarded `mdtraj.Topology.find_molecules()` at `mdclaw/simulation/restraints.py:264`** — the periodicity-detection path introduced in `6d7cdcc`, `load_distance_restraints` → `distance_cv_periodicity` → `groups_share_molecule`, lets mdtraj's raw `ValueError: Cannot identify molecules because this Topology does not include bonds` pass straight through for a topology without bonds. This violates the CLAUDE.md design principle (a tool refuses with a stable `code`). The trigger condition is "the whole topology has not a single bond, and there is a residue with 2 or more atoms", so the practical reach is narrow (a solvated system always has bonds), but with no bonds it should fall back to `False` or refuse with a structured error.

Not pushed to GHCR (`:latest` remains `661a80cedc05`).

## 2026-10-01 — `generate_md_report` citations: choose preparation, solvation and ligand-parameter methods from the records, and read the OpenMM version from State/System XML

In the T4L ABFE Methods draft (9/27), I investigated the methods whose use remains in the records but for which no citation came out, and the cause of the per-min/eq-node "OpenMM version not recorded", and fixed them with user approval (remedies 1 and 2).

- **Cause 1 (gap in the registry)**: the selector (`mdclaw/evidence/citations.py`) and the bundled bib (24 entries) only covered OpenMM-side methods and FEP theory, so GAFF, NAGL, PDB2PQR/PROPKA and packmol-memgen could not be selected even when present in the records. The audit document (`docs/research/citation-audit-2026-09-06.md`) already had the mapping table and Crossref-verified records.
- **Cause 2 (wrong place to read)**: the OpenMM 8 citation was selected only from `openmmVersion` in a production node's `runtime_system` (System XML); min/eq (State XML) and topo (System XML) have `openmmVersion` but were not read.
- **Changes**:
  - For nodes without `runtime_system`, the reporter (`reporting.py`) reads only the root start tag of `state` / `system_xml` and records it in `runtime.openmm_serialization`. The hash is taken over the whole file and cached once by size and mtime.
  - Newly supported by the selector:
    - `protonation_baseline_method` (`pdb2pqr+propka` → 3 PDB2PQR + 2 PROPKA, `pdb2pqr_no_prediction` → PDB2PQR only)
    - solv `backend` / `membrane_backend` = `packmol-memgen` → SchottVerdugo 2019 + Martinez 2009 (PACKMOL). For older nodes without this record, it is detected from the `Packmol Memgen` REMARK at the top of `solvated_pdb`.
    - topo `forcefield_provenance`: when there is a ligand that went through the GAFF template generator, select Wang 2004 GAFF, Wang 2006 Antechamber and Case 2023 AmberTools. If the charges are NAGL's `openff-gnn-am1bcc-1.0.0.pt`, the AshGC working paper; if `am1bcc_fallback`, Jakalian 2000/2002. I confirmed in the openmmforcefields 0.16 source that the generator runs antechamber and parmchk2 without charges. Even for protein-only systems `small_molecule_forcefield = gaff-2.11` is written as a fixed value, so the decision is based on whether a ligand is present.
    - PDBFixer, openmmforcefields, the GAFF2 version and the NAGL model have no dedicated paper, so they became versioned documentation items.
  - I also fixed the recording side. `clean_protein` records `pdbfixer_version` in its provenance on success, and the normal path of `solvate_structure` records `backend: packmol-memgen` and `backend_version` (both via `_common.installed_version`). In existing DAGs PDBFixer stays unrecorded (it is a documentation item, so it does not affect BibTeX).
- **Bibliography**: copied 12 entries from the audit bib into the bundled bib, which now has 37 entries. Re-verified title (with publisher markup removed), first author, year, volume and pages against Crossref; all matched. AshGC was verified against DataCite. PDB2PQR 3.7.1 itself asks at runtime for citations of Jurrus 2018 and Dolinsky 2007, and the official page lists the same 2 plus 2004 and Unni 2011 (web server, out of scope), so I verified Dolinsky 2007 against Crossref and added it to the audit bib (120 keys, 119 DOIs). Added a 2026-10-01 addendum to the audit document.
- **Tests**:
  - Added 2 tests to `tests/test_evidence_server.py`: the OpenMM version from State/System XML (7.x is unresolved with a value), and the mapping for preparation, solvation and ligands (including the old solv REMARK and a protein-only topo). Updated the bundled count to 37.
  - Added a test to `test_guardrails.py` that a solv node records `backend: packmol-memgen` (using a fake packmol-memgen). Added the recording of `pdbfixer_version` to `test_protonation_states.py`.
  - Broader fast suite: 677 passed. The 1 failure is due to another session's uncommitted `sst2_charge_unscaled_invalid` (golden file not updated).
  - Also confirmed with the real CLI (prep → solv of 181L left both records, and the report selected using the metadata as evidence).
- **T4L results**: in the benzene 3-replica report, selected citations went from 12 → 24 and unresolved `OpenMM_version` to 0. For the 25 ligands (replica 1 each, `report/study_r1`) there are 25 citations, and Mobley 2007 is also included from the 14 ligands with σ > 1. The only remaining unresolved item is the uniform per-node note `remaining_stage_methods`. I put the 25 keys into the body of `report/METHODS.md` and made them match `references.bib` exactly. Still to be cited by hand: the data sources (benchmarksets and 4 original ITC sources), Mobley 2006, MDClaw, and software without dedicated papers (cited by version and URL). OpenFF Toolkit (Mobley 2018) is in the audit bib but not yet selected automatically.

The criterion is that "joint holo H3 is significantly present in the 300 K ensemble from the apo start and agrees with the holo start". **Presence is satisfied**: the lower end of the interval is 0.88 %, and 6/8 walkers reached it at 300 K. **Agreement is not satisfied**: 3.7 % vs 52.9 %; even at 300 ns per walker (2.4 µs aggregate per start), a difference of nearly 50 points remains, and 21 points remain even at the hottest 600 K rung. The apo-pattern fractions are approaching (24.5 / 5.5 → 21.7 / 10.0 → 20.4 / 12.7 %), but the intervals are wide. There are few transitions per walker, and the population estimate is determined by events in a few walkers. **A population shift is not shown, and we do not claim it.** Even if extended with the same design, the apo-start fraction did not rise over the last 100 ns, so the time to agreement cannot be estimated.

Gly101 is 59.6, 51.9, 49.9 % (plateau, slight decline), Trp105 76.6, 80.6, 72.0 %, Gly106 78.1, 85.2, 85.5 %. Apo-like from the holo start: Gly101 6.7, 21.1, 17.2 %, Thr103 19.9, 28.6, 21.7 %, Asn104 26.0, 29.9, 33.8 %. The joint holo of the holo start does not keep falling after 75–100 ns, fluctuating at 38–56 % (within the spread of 8 walkers per window; cannot conclude it has bottomed out).
- **Rung dependence** (unweighted, fixed λ). joint holo is nearly flat from the apo start, 3.1 → 5.1 % for 300 → 600 K, and from the holo start 55.4 → 31.6 %, higher at lower temperature. At equilibrium the per-rung fractions should agree regardless of start, so the difference of about 52 points at 300 K and about 27 at 600 K is an indicator of non-convergence (hotter rungs mix faster).
- **Convergence indicators**. JSD (H3 RMSD distributions of the 2 starts, bit, every 160 ns of aggregate time = every 20 ns per walker; 160, 320, …, 1600 ns) is 0.896, 0.752, 0.603, 0.575, 0.445, 0.371, 0.329, 0.303, 0.301, 0.285. The decreases in the extension (from 800 ns on) are 0.074, 0.042, 0.026, 0.002, 0.016, slowing down (the 800 ns value is almost the same as stage 1's 0.446). The decrease is mainly due to the holo start moving toward the apo side (below 2 Å from holo copy 68.7 → 52.1 %, below 2 Å from apo crystal 7.8 → 16.2 %). The RMSD distribution of the apo start has barely moved. It cannot yet be called a plateau. PCA is PC1 49 %, PC2 27 % (stage 1: 51 / 25 %).
- **analyze_tempering verdicts**. All 4 nodes `sampling_verdict = not_converged` (same as stage 1). The weight verdicts are all 4 `weights_drifting` (in stage 1, the 2 in the apo job were `weights_converged`), because of between-walker disagreement of f_k (up to 2.7 kJ/mol in the apo job, up to 6.4 kJ/mol in the holo job; stage 1's holo job was 5.3), and because in the holo job the on-the-fly weights of prod_012, 014, 016 deviate from the MBAR f_k by 3.2, 2.8, 3.6 kJ/mol. `runs_disagree` (difference of the 300 K distributions per run) is flat: 11.8 / 12.3 → 10.7 / 11.9 in the apo job and 11.2 / 11.2 → 13.8 / 12.2 kJ/mol in the holo job (in order of apo, holo reference), about 4–5.5 times the threshold 2.5, and RMSD regions not visited by all walkers remain. The first-half vs second-half distribution difference went 4.0 / 6.5 → 2.3 / 1.5 kJ/mol in the apo job, below the threshold 2.5, but the holo job is 13.0 / 6.4 → 3.9 / 3.7 kJ/mol, still above.
- **How to read (against the criteria fixed in advance)**. The criterion is that "joint holo H3 is significantly present in the 300 K ensemble from the apo start". **Arrival was confirmed**: the lower end of the walker bootstrap interval exceeds 0 (0.73 %); 4/8 walkers at 300 K (stage 1: 1/8) and 6/8 walkers at some rung (stage 1: 2/8) adopted the holo pattern, and the 25 ns windows of the most recent 100 ns rose monotonically, 1.7, 6.7, 8.7, 10.8 %. **But a population shift has not been shown**: 3.5 % is a minority (the holo start is 55 %), it is still rising in the most recent window with no plateau in sight, the verdict remains not_converged, and the between-run disagreement is not shrinking. Whether both starts head to the same equilibrium ensemble cannot be determined at this length. That the holo start loses the holo pattern from 82 % to 38–56 % without antigen is consistent both with the interpretation that the apo state is favored and with the interpretation that it is a consequence of the force field and the solute definition (H3 only, 90 atoms) (not distinguished). The possibility that the apo H3 of 5E03 is stabilized by the crystal lattice remains untested.
- **Relation to the stage 1 description**. Stage 1's "the apo start is 0.67 % (1/8 walkers)" was an underestimate because 100 ns was too short, and I correct this point (this time 3.45 %, 4/8 walkers). Stage 1's "the holo start is decaying" did not continue after 100 ns, fluctuating at 38–56 %, so I weaken that assertion. Stage 1's conclusion "does not satisfy the criterion, draw no conclusion" still stands. The 0 % for TPP-3077 / Nb.X0 (9/29) is a different system, so this neither strengthens nor weakens it. However, it is now known that there are systems in which the apo start takes more than 100 ns to acquire the holo pattern.
- **Next candidates (all unapproved and not launched; to discuss with the user)**. (A) Another +100 ns of the same 16 walkers (about 17.4 GPU-h = 4.35 node-h, about 5,750 yen incl. tax, no code changes. **Recommended**: the cheapest way to see whether the joint holo from the apo start (1.7 → 10.8 %) plateaus or keeps rising, and whether it approaches the holo start (38–56 %)). (D) The Level 3 main run of TPP-3077 (16 walkers × 100 ns, about 23–33 GPU-h), a 3rd run of Nb.X0 apo copy B, plain MD of ctla4, Level 3 indices for ctla4. In the Level 3 hot-λ confirmation run the H3 holo pattern was 0 % at every λ from the apo start, so expectations for (D) are low.

Per residue is the same: holo-like from the apo start is Thr103 2.2 % (300 K) → 4.2 % (600 K), Asn104 4.8 → 7.7 %; apo-like from the holo start is Thr103 13.6 → 12.7 %, Asn104 19.5 → 17.4 %. These two ψ keep the memory of the starting point even at the λ = 0.5 rung (by the fork's rule, with the H3-only solute, Thr103 ψ has all 4 atoms hot and scales as λ^1, and Asn104 ψ scales as λ^(3/4) because N105 is not hot).
- **Time course** (unweighted, all rungs, walker-time windows 0–1, 1–5, 5–20, 20–50, 50–100 ns). Holo-like fractions from the apo start: Trp105 0.0, 21.2, 37.7, 68.6, 76.6 % and Gly106 0.0, 21.0, 38.2, 70.3, 78.1 % keep increasing to the end (these two torsions are outside the solute, and their ψ / φ are not scaled); Gly101 21.0, 29.2, 44.0, 63.3, 59.6 %, nearly flat after 20 ns; Thr103 0.0, 2.6, 0.0, 1.8, 5.1 % and Asn104 1.0, 4.7, 8.1, 7.7, 6.2 % barely move. Apo-like fractions from the holo start increase in the second half: Thr103 0.0, 1.5, 0.6, 5.4, 19.9 %, Asn104 3.0, 3.8, 7.8, 12.9, 26.0 %. That is, the ψ flips of Thr103 and Asn104 occur on a timescale comparable to the run length (~100 ns) and have not reached equilibrium in either direction.
- **Convergence indicators**. JSD (H3 RMSD distributions of the 2 starts, bit) keeps decreasing from 0.915 at 80 ns aggregate time to 0.446 at 800 ns (80, 160, …, 800 ns: 0.915, 0.896, 0.826, 0.752, 0.651, 0.603, 0.582, 0.575, 0.513, 0.446) and has not plateaued. `analyze_tempering` gives `sampling_verdict: not_converged` all 4 times (runs_disagree 11–12 kJ/mol, distribution_drifting 4–13 kJ/mol). The weights are `weights_converged` for the apo-start job and `weights_drifting` for the holo-start job (difference between on-the-fly weights and MBAR up to 2.8 kJ/mol, between-walker f_k deviation up to 5.3 kJ/mol). Cartesian PCA (H3 backbone, superposed on framework CA, fitted with the 2 starts weighted equally) is PC1 51 %, PC2 25 %, and the 300 K landscape of the apo start has a continuous path up to near the holo crystal at a height of about 8–12 kJ/mol. Per walker, walker 2 of the holo start transitioned completely holo → apo at 44–82 ns, and walker 8 of the apo start went in and out of the holo pattern at 50–70 ns.
- **Verdict**. It fails the reading fixed before the runs (joint holo H3 significantly present from the apo start) (0.67 %, upper end of the 95 % interval 2.2 %, 1/8 walkers at 300 K). The positive control did not succeed. However, we do not conclude "it does not appear with H3 only": (1) transitions occur in both directions, but the 2 starts have not yet reached the same distribution (the holo pattern of the holo start keeps falling per 25 ns window, 82 → 40 %, and the apo start is at 1/8 walkers at 300 K). (2) Even at the hottest rung it is 1 % vs 37 %, and the memory of the starting point remains. (3) JSD keeps decreasing. (4) What does not move is the ψ of Thr103 and Asn104, whose flips are on a timescale around 100 ns, so 8 walkers × 100 ns does not reach equilibrium. Whether these two are slow because of the solute definition (the shell, side chains and solvent are barriers) or simply because the length is insufficient cannot be separated from this run alone. The possibility that the apo H3 of 5E03 is a shape held by the crystal lattice (contacts with symmetry copies) (the positive-control preparation entry, "crystal facts") was also not tested with this data. That Trp105 and Gly106 become holo-like in about 70–78 % from the apo start is consistent with the C-terminal side of the apo crystal H3 being hard to maintain in solution, but that alone does not show a lattice effect. The 0 % for TPP-3077 / Nb.X0 (9/29) is neither strengthened nor weakened by this result.
- **Next candidates (all unapproved and not launched; to discuss with the user)**. (A) Extend the same 16 walkers by 100 ns each (`create_node --node-type prod --continue-from prod_00N`, no code changes, rung, averages and state inherited from the sidecar. About 17.4 GPU-h, about 5,700 yen incl. tax). If the time course above continues, the value of joint holo H3 from the apo start and the agreement of the 2 starts (JSD) will be settled. (B) An H3 + 5 Å shell 319-atom solute (about 17–28 GPU-h, about 5,700–9,200 yen incl. tax. Determined by the number of MPS clients per walker: lower bound for the plain type with 8 walkers per GPU, upper bound for the charge-unscaled type with 4 walkers). It changes the solute definition, so measure the client count and speed of 1 walker before the run. (C) Keep H3 only and widen the ladder to about 1000 K (about 17 GPU-h, about 5,700 yen incl. tax). Recommended is (A) (cheapest, and it directly shows whether it is unconverged without changing the solute definition).

## 2026-09-29 — SST2 nanobody demo: revisiting the solute definition (Level 3 = loops hot, sheets cold), based on per-rung starting-point memory, the hot-λ diagnosis and the fork's scaling rules

User: "SST2 isn't working on CDR-H3 as well as I expected" → hot-λ diagnosis (approved) → "you should think a bit more about the solute definition". The study is `/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/sst2-trials/nb-apo-holo`; scripts and figures are under `inputs/` (outside the repository).

- **Rules of how it acts (fork `~/SST2/src/SST2/rest2.py`)**: to accelerate backbone φ/ψ, the atoms of that dihedral must be hot. Proper torsions scale as λ^(n/4) (n = number of hot atoms among the 4), CMAP as λ^(n/8), impropers are unscaled, and 1-4 pairs across the hot/cold boundary as √λ. The Level 1/2 shell (side chains only, charges not tempered) helps only χ, and the backbone φ/ψ of neighboring loops stay at 300 K. Only H3 has a hot backbone; H3's neighbors (CDR1, N-terminus) are cold.
- **Per-rung starting-point memory M** (`inputs/rung_flips.py`, `rung_flips.png`): M(rung) = P(holo-like | apo start) − P(holo-like | holo start), per rung for each switch dihedral (φ or ψ differing by more than 60° between apo crystal copy A and the circular mean of the holo crystal). Rung 0 is 300 K (λ = 1), the same Hamiltonian in all designs, so M(rung 0) ≠ 0 means "that design has not converged yet" (flips visible at hot rungs are meaningless unless they come down). For TPP-3077 in Level 2, H3 mixes (Q99 +0.03, E101 −0.13, G104 −0.01, G105 −0.03), but CDR1's I28/S29/I32 are frozen at −0.99/−1.00/−1.00. Even in block 2 (all shell atoms), I28 −0.72, S29 −0.69, I32 −1.00. For Nb.X0 in Level 2, the 9 H3 dihedrals are −0.35 to −0.99, and P26/G27 −0.83/−0.82. In block 2, G99 mixes down to −0.08 (G100 −0.70, R102 −0.66, Y108 −0.90 remain). H3 dihedrals start to mix from rung 4–5 (463 K and above). **Making the backbone of neighboring loops hot makes H3 mix**.
- **Hot-λ diagnosis (Level 2 solute, `inputs/level2/submit_hotlambda.sh`)**: each walker is fixed at one λ (ladder `[300, T_hot]`, with `--weights-file [0, 1e6]` so that the first Gibbs move goes to T_hot and never returns), 30 ns, apo and holo starts, λ = 0.5 / 0.3 / 0.2 (600 / 1000 / 1500 K). The between-start JSD of the H3 RMSD distributions (bits, second half) is 0.28 / 0.27 / 0.73 for TPP-3077 and 0.99 / 0.26 / 0.34 for Nb.X0. Switch dihedrals (`level2/torsion_hot.py`): TPP-3077's H3 (Q99, E101, G104, G105) enters the opposite basin 13–63 % of the time from λ = 0.5 even from the apo start. CDR1's I28.ψ, S29.ψ, I32.ψ are 0–0.6 % in the apo → holo direction at all λ; in the holo → apo direction, I28/S29 are 31–40 % at 600 K and 1500 K (0 at 1000 K), and I32 is 0. Nb.X0's P26.ψ and G27.φ are 4 % or less at every λ (backbone cold in Level 2). **The apo → holo CDR1 flip does not occur** (the reverse does: the holo start has no antigen, so the holo-side CDR1 relaxes).
- **MPS limit**: a Level 2 walker holds about 10 CUDA contexts (REST2 4 + charge splitting 6), and MPS allows 48 clients per GPU, so **up to 4 walkers per GPU**. At 6 walkers/GPU (149797/149798), 9 of 12 walkers died with "No compatible CUDA device" (at Context creation); resubmitted at 3 walkers/GPU (149808–149810, 1 h 25 m–2 h 17 m, 30 ns × 3).
- **Crystal differences** (`inputs/crystal_diff.py`, `inputs/torsion_switch.py`): in TPP-3077 the CA of CDR1 27–33 moves 1.3–4.3 Å, and the switch dihedrals are I28.ψ, S29.ψ, I32.ψ (I32 is paratope) and H3's Q99.φ, E101.ψ, G104.ψ, G105.φ/ψ. H3 loses contact with R27/I28/S29 and contacts S30/R53. In Nb.X0 the H3 CA moves 7–14 Å over 99–106 (from contacts with V2/S29/T33/Y94/C95 to contacts with F47/Y58), and P26.ψ and G27.φ differ only from apo copy A. Nb.X0's paratope is T33, Y37, F47, A50, T52–G55, L56, Y58 + H3.
- **Level 3 (loops hot, sheets cold)** (`inputs/level3/make_level3_indices.py`): the fully scaled set F = all atoms of H3 + all atoms of runs of 3 or more consecutive residues whose DSSP in the apo start is C (coil) and that contain 2 or more residues of the shell (union of the 5 Å shells of the apo and holo crystals). The charge-unscaled set U = the side chains of the remaining shell (excluding N/H/CA/HA/HA2/HA3/C/O). solute = F + U; with no loops it reproduces the Level 2 file exactly (checked in the script; along the way I forgot to put Gly's HA2/HA3 in the backbone and got a mismatch → fixed). TPP-3077: hot loop 27–32, F 295 (H3 192 + CDR1 103), U 178, solute 473 (block 2 was 564). Nb.X0: hot loops 1–3 and 25–33, F 402 (H3 207), U 146, solute 548 (block 2 was 538). The size is similar to block 2, so exchange should work with 9 rungs over 300–600 K. The framework β strands are side-chain-only even in the shell, and their backbone stays cold (the cause of melting in blocks 1/2). No changes to the fork (generative reuse).
- **Dependence on holo information (disclosure)**: the shell is a union that includes the holo crystal, so when redefined from apo only (`scratchpad/apo_only_shell.py`), TPP-3077's hot loop is the same 27–32 (U goes 178 → 147, dropping the side chains of R53 and T78), while Nb.X0 drops the N-terminal 1–3 and keeps only 25–33 (F 350, U 108; T3 enters the shell only for holo, a 1-residue difference). The backbone made hot can be regarded as determined by the apo structure alone (exception: Nb.X0's N-terminus). If the paper says "the solute is from the apo structure's DSSP and 5 Å shell", a rerun with the version defined by the apo-only shell is needed.
- **Confirmation runs (`inputs/level3/submit_screen_l3.sh`)**: same procedure as the Level 2 hot-λ, T_hot 600 / 1000 K (λ 0.5 / 0.3), apo and holo starts, 30 ns, 8 walkers (tpp3077_apo prod_030/031, tpp3077_holo prod_021/022, nbx0_apo prod_030/031, nbx0_holo prod_024/025, seeds 201–208). MPS 150026 (TPP-3077), 150027 (Nb.X0), 4 walkers per GPU, 6 h, about 4.8 GPU-h (about 1,600 yen). What to look at: (1) whether CDR1's I28/S29/I32 (TPP-3077) and P26/G27 (Nb.X0) flip in both directions at λ = 0.5 or 0.3, (2) whether the framework β strands stay intact (CA RMSD, DSSP), (3) compare the H3 JSD with Level 2. Note: even in block 2 with all shell atoms hot, TPP-3077's I32 did not flip, so if it does not flip in Level 3 either, regard this CDR1 flip as antigen-induced (or needing λ ≤ 0.2) and narrow the TPP-3077 claim to "H3 mixing". Next: if it passes, start SST2 Level 3 with 16 walkers × 100 ns (about 32 GPU-h, about 10,500 yen), but this is unapproved, so ask the user. For analysis, run `inputs/level2/torsion_hot.py` and `hotlambda.py` with `HOT_LEVEL=level3`, and use `inputs/level3/framework_integrity.py` to put the DSSP E fraction and CA RMSD (relative to the starting frame, self-superposed) of the cold strands (58 residues for TPP-3077, 54 for Nb.X0) side by side with Level 2. The Level 2 30 ns reference values are E fraction 0.90–0.97 (minimum 0.74–0.85) and CA RMSD mean 0.63–0.94 Å (95th percentile 0.74–1.26 Å).
- Provisional (holo-start plain MD 148084 not yet finished): the JSD (bits) of the H3 RMSD distributions of the 2 starts is 0.75 for TPP-3077 and 0.79 for Nb.X0 with plain MD; with SST2, 0.10 / 0.53 for block 2, 0.45 / 0.57 for Level 1, 0.13 / 0.92 for Level 2. For TPP-3077 the 2 starts are closer with SST2, but Nb.X0 Level 2 is worse than plain MD (in a system where H3 moves a lot, shell side chains alone are not enough). To be finalized after 148084 completes (`inputs/efficiency.py`).
- Uncommitted (until the user asks). The fork commit ba48461 is local only. Do not rewrite `~/mdclaw/mdclaw` or `~/SST2` while runs are in progress (compute nodes read them). The tracked bug "CANCELLED by <uid>" was fixed in 0528df5 (included in the 09-26 image).

## 2026-09-29 — Closed the 4 cli_skill_sif failures of MDDataBench v4 in the CLI (parent type checks at creation and submission, a marker for unknown submission results, refusal of double runs, stopping before the time limit, chain_ranges)

The plan is `docs/developer/cli-skill-sif-v4-fix-plan.md` (history and evidence locations for 04 / 010 / 015 r1 / 015 r2, implementation status at the end). The principle is "a check that happens only at run time is invisible to the agent" (004 r3 ended at 462 s of 1800 s), so the same checks were also placed in `create_node` and `submit_job`. The MDDataBench-side session independently reached the same conclusion (screenshot 2026-09-28).

- **§1 Parent type**: `create_node` applies `_ALLOWED_PARENT_TYPES` at creation (`parent_type_invalid`, `next_action` is the correct open parent). An eq under a topo that has a min gets `eq_parent_should_be_min`. `submit_job` / array / MPS return `node_execution_context_invalid` before sbatch via `node_structure_preflight` (parent type, failed parents, tool-to-stage mapping). An existing bug found at the same time: since `run_metadynamics` was added (6941312, 9/22), `_STAGE_PREFERENCE` had no prod, and `next.run_command` of a completed eq recommended `run_metadynamics` (the campaign v4 image 0528df5 too). `test_envelope.py::test_alchemical_routing_is_decided_per_branch` was failing on main.
- **§2 Unknown submission result and double runs**: `#SBATCH --comment=mdclaw:<intent>`. For failures where the sbatch response was lost (Socket timed out, etc.), look for the marker in squeue (`find_marked_job`, up to 30 s); if found adopt it, otherwise keep the reservation with `slurm_submit_uncertain` (resubmission is refused). `check_job --job-dir J --node-id N` resolves it (adopt / release with `slurm_submit_not_found` / hold if unknown). Other sbatch failures are `slurm_submit_failed`. `begin_node` claims the node with the rounds owner record (moved to `mdclaw/node/owner.py`), and if another live executor exists returns `node_already_running` (the CLI does not fail the node). The sync side also does not seal as FAILED/COMPLETED a running node held by another live job (the path by which the losing job of 010 r3 broke the winning one).
- **§3 chain_ranges**: `inspect_molecules.chain_ranges` (first / last / count / gaps / insertion_codes per chain, kept even with `--output brief`), put into metadata and results when source completes, showing `next.inspect_command`. `prepare_complex.kept_residue_ranges`, and warnings when a range extends beyond the structure / spans a gap.
- **§4 Time limit**: `run_production` stops at a frame boundary 120 s (or one output interval) before `SLURM_JOB_END_TIME` (or `MDCLAW_JOB_END_TIME`) and completes with the actual length (`requested_simulation_time_ns` / `remaining_simulation_time_ns` / `stopped_reason`), with `next` being an extension via `--continue-from`. eq records `ns_per_day`, and `submit_job` refuses a production that does not fit via `production_time_budget` with `production_exceeds_time_limit` (015 r2's 3 ns / 20 min gets the suggestion 2 runs × 1.5 ns).

## 2026-09-28 — SST2 does not currently look more efficient than plain MD (user's observation) → holo-start plain-MD control first

User: "The sampling doesn't look any more efficient than plain MD." I agreed. For apo → holo (this paper's question), plain MD (apo start, 300 ns) gives a closest approach to holo of 1.92 Å for TPP-3077 with P(holo < 2 Å) 0.1–0.17 %; SST2 block 1 gives 1.64 Å / 0.15 %, and Level 2 (100 ns) 1.78 Å / 0 %, so there is no difference. For Nb.X0, plain MD alone moves over the same range as SST2, apo A → apo B → up to 12 Å from holo (in contrast to 1KXV, where 200 ns of plain MD could not cross the H3 basin while SST2 crossed it 48–105 times: the loops of this nanobody are intrinsically mobile). Where SST2 is clearly better is temperature cycling and weight convergence. SST2's crossing from the holo start to the apo side (TPP-3077 0.8 %, Nb.X0 0.3 %) may be an effect, but there is no holo-start plain MD to compare against.

Hypotheses: (1) the slow degrees of freedom are not the terms being tempered (in TPP-3077, H3 shifts in position more than in shape; the pivot is at the base of H3 or on the framework side, outside the solute), (2) holo is genuinely rare in solution (if induced fit, it barely appears even with a correct method; the only test is agreement of the distributions from the 2 starts), (3) the time is too short (Liedl et al. use metaD + tens of µs).

User decision: the control first (option 1). Cancelled the Level 2 +200 ns extension (148060/148061) after 17 min, and `--abandon`ed 8 nodes (tpp3077_apo prod_022–023, tpp3077_holo prod_013–014, nbx0_apo prod_022–023, nbx0_holo prod_013–014). Submitted holo-start plain MD: from eq_001 of tpp3077_holo and nbx0_holo, seeds 1–3 × 300 ns (prod_015–017, 50 ps output), MPS 148084 (6 tasks/1 GPU, image). `inputs/submit_md_holo.sh`. Next, put side by side for SST2 and plain MD "how fast per GPU hour the 300 K distributions of the 2 starts agree" (option 2).

User's observation: "the dPCA and RMSD plots aren't consistent". Checking with block 1 apo-start frames, for TPP-3077 the correlation of H3's RMSD to apo with the all-dihedral distance is 0.03, and with the 2D dPCA distance −0.15. ## 2026-09-28 — SST2 Level 2 for CDR-H3: shell side chains do not have their charges tempered (fork ba48461 + run_sst2 `--charge-unscaled-indices-file`), pilot submitted

Implemented and ran Level 2 at the user's request. The solute is the same as Level 1 (all H3 atoms + shell side chains), with only the shell side chains' charges unscaled (LJ ε and torsions are scaled). Only H3 has its charges tempered, and the solute net charge is H3's −1 e (the non-integer charges of Level 1, +2.53 / +0.66 e, disappear).

SST2 fork (`~/SST2` branch mdclaw, local commit ba48461, not pushed): `REST2(charge_unscaled_index=...)`. The per-atom factor is √λ for charge (charge-scaled atoms) / 1 (others), and ε is λ over the whole solute. Pair dependence: Coulomb λ between charge-scaled atoms, √λ between charge-scaled and others; LJ λ within the solute, √λ solute–solvent; these fit directly into SST2's 2 buckets (λ and √λ). The nonbonded decomposition is built by subtraction, evaluating at each exchange 6 System copies with Coulomb-only / LJ-only original parameters (all, C, not-C / all, S, O) (no updates needed as λ changes). Exceptions (1-4) automatically land in the correct bucket via the product of factors. CHARMM NBFIX/LJ14, RF and subsystems other than copy are NotImplemented. `--charge-unscaled-indices` in the driver, `charge_unscaled_atoms` in the sidecar.

Verification: the new test `test_rest2_charge_unscaled.py` (2HPL, λ = 1, 0.7, 0.5, 0.35, 1) passes on particle parameters, λ-invariance of the unscaled components, closure (difference between the context's ΔE and the ΔE assembled from the decomposition ≤ 0.003 kJ/mol), and round trip. All fork tests: 21 pass, 2 fail, the known 2 that failed before the change (confirmed with stash). On a real system (Nb.X0, 56k atoms, including OPC virtual sites), λ-invariance 0.0002 kJ/mol, closure error 0.07 kJ/mol (against ΔE ~1500 kJ/mol, due to single precision in the main computation). One decomposition takes 17 ms (vs 169 ms for 500 steps, about 10 % at every 2 ps).

MDClaw (uncommitted): `run_sst2(charge_unscaled_indices_file=...)`; `sst2_charge_unscaled_invalid` if it is not a subset of the solute / if there is no nonbonded scaling / for a continuation whose count differs from the parent walker. Artifact `charge_unscaled_indices.json`, `tempering.charge_unscaled_atoms`. Added "loops + partner side chains only, do not include the shell backbone" and the new option to the skill `md-production/sst2.md`, updated tool-reference, regenerated golden codes. Tests: test_tempering 12 pass (2 new), 164 pass including guardrail/registry/cli. Along the way, inserting a helper right before `run_sst2` stole the `@node_tool` decorator and made `test_registered_as_prod_tool` fail (fixed).

Pilot: same design as Level 1 (from eq_001, 2 seeds 41/42 × 4 starts × 100 ns, 9 rungs). Indices are `inputs/level2/{tpp3077,nbx0}_charge_unscaled.json` (245 / 209 atoms = solute − H3). Analysis: `inputs/run_analyze_set.sh {pilotsc,b2}` (analyze_003/004 = pilot, analyze_005/006 = block 1+2 chain, apo reference / holo reference), `inputs/join_frames.py` → `{pilotsc,b2}_populations.json` and `_2d_maps.png`, dPCA with `inputs/dpca_landscape_set.py` (projected onto block 1's PCA axes with `BASIS=block1`), shell β with `inputs/dssp_trap_check.py <S> pilotsc`.

Level 1 pilot (compared with block 1 over the same 100 ns):
- Temperature cycling: 28–67 round trips/run (block 1: 3–33), rung exchange 0.38–0.46 (0.31–0.39), nearly uniform rung occupancy. Weights `weights_converged` in 3 of 4 starts (block 1: 0).
- The shell β of Nb.X0 was maintained at 0.58–0.60 independent of rung (block 1's trapped run went 0.59 → 0.46). TPP-3077 drops over time 0.53 → 0.48, but the same at rung 0, and the framework outside the solute also drops slightly, so it is not high-temperature melting.
- Structural crossing not yet within 100 ns: closest approach to holo from the TPP-3077 apo start 1.95 Å (block 1: 1.64 Å), Nb.X0 apo start 3.63 Å. However, in dihedral PCA the Nb.X0 apo start spreads continuously from apo A to apo B (the other copy of the apo crystal), and the holo start also spreads from holo toward apo B, so the 2 starts began to overlap near apo B (completely separated in block 1).

block 2 (current solute, 300 ns chain):
- TPP-3077: the holo start reached the apo crystal form to within 0.78 Å (P(apo < 2 Å) = 0.4 % at 300 K). The 300 K populations of the 2 starts approach each other (within 2.5 Å of holo 8.9 % vs 16.7 %, within 2.5 Å of apo 3.4 % vs 2.4 %). The closest approach to holo from the apo start remains 1.64 Å. Weights drifting at 16–17 kJ/mol between seeds.
- Nb.X0: worse. Some runs reach a 300 K-reweighted mean RMSD of 10–11 Å, with H3 collapsed. The holo start has a between-seed f_k difference of 1394 kJ/mol, with runs that do not return to low temperature. Consistent with the trap due to shell β melting seen in block 1.

Dihedral PCA of block 2 (`inputs/b2_dpca_landscape.png`, block 1's axes, including 300 ns of plain MD): for TPP-3077 the holo start spreads to the apo crystal region, but the apo start does not reach holo. For Nb.X0 the apo start goes apo A → apo B → toward holo (dPC1 ≈ 1.3), and the holo start also spreads toward apo B, so in dihedral space the 2 starts began to overlap near apo B. However, in Cartesian RMSD of the same runs H3 is collapsed (some runs with a 300 K mean of 10–11 Å); the dihedrals connect, but the loop's position relative to the framework is broken. Plain MD (Nb.X0) also moves from apo A to (−0.5, −1) in 300 ns.

Conclusion: the current H3 + all shell atoms causes a high-temperature trap in Nb.X0, getting worse with extension. Level 1 greatly improves temperature cycling and weight convergence and does not break the shell. The logical next step is to make Level 1 the main series and extend it (awaiting the user's decision).

## 2026-09-27 — Investigating the cause of the SST2 high-temperature trap, and submitting a pilot of a CDR-H3-oriented solute (Level 1: all H3 atoms + shell side chains only)

Preparation for the user's question "Can we make an SST2 suited to the CDR-H3 loop?". Investigated the cause of Nb.X0's high-temperature trap with block 1 data.

- It is not cis/trans: 12 runs × 5,000 frames, 0 cis peptide bonds within the solute at every rung (`inputs/cis_scan_block1.py` → `block1_cis_scan.json`).
- The β sheet of the framework backbone included in the shell melts at high temperature: in the trapped nbx0_apo prod_003, the β content of shell residues is 0.59 in the first 10 ns → 0.46 in the last 20 ns, 0.59 at rungs 0–3 and 0.51 at rungs 5–8. The framework outside the solute is nearly unchanged at 0.49 → 0.45. The untrapped prod_001 has shell 0.59 → 0.57 as well (`inputs/dssp_trap_check.py` → `block1_dssp_trap.json`).
- Interpretation: the barrier to H3 rearrangement is the side-chain packing of the shell, and there is no need to temper the framework backbone. With H3 alone the shape does not change at 300 K (1KXV), so the shell is needed.

The proposed 3 levels: Level 1 = solute as all H3 atoms + shell side chains only (backbone N/H/CA/HA/C/O unscaled), no code changes. Level 2 = choose terms per region (all terms for H3; for shell side chains only LJ and side-chain torsions with charges unscaled, gREST-style) in the fork, made into a tool as `--solute-preset vhh_cdrh3` determined from IMGT numbering. Level 3 = weak WT-metaD on a fold-over CV.

Submitted Level 1 (user-approved): the solute is 437 atoms for TPP-3077 (net +2.53 e) and 416 atoms for Nb.X0 (+0.66 e). Cutting at the backbone makes the solute net charge non-integer, and the total system charge changes with rung (a problem common to REST2 that also happens with the current +2 e; needs checking). CMAP is scaled only for H3's part (driver log: shell CMAP in the 1/8 bucket). From eq_001, 2 seeds (31, 32) × 4 starts × 100 ns, ladder the same 9 rungs as block 1, MPS 4 tasks/GPU: 146233 (TPP-3077: tpp3077_apo prod_016–017, tpp3077_holo prod_007–008), 146234 (Nb.X0: nbx0_apo prod_016–017, nbx0_holo prod_007–008). Indices `inputs/{tpp3077,nbx0}_solute_h3_shellsc.json`, submission `inputs/submit_pilot_shellsc.sh`. Compare with block 1 over the same time: retention of shell β, high-temperature trapping, shape transitions at 300 K, how the distributions of the 2 starts approach each other.

## 2026-09-26 — Production takes its temperature from the node it restarts from; rounds pin one temperature per scheme

Why: MDDataBench glm-5.3-flash-3cond-full, `010_membrane_6kux` cli_skill_sif r3. The prompt asked 310 K, the agent ran `run_equilibration --temperature-kelvin 310` and then `run_production` without the flag (a Slurm chain, afterok), so production ran at the 300 K default and failed both temperature checks. The eq -> prod temperature change had been a hard error until 17afe45 (2026-09-10), which relaxed timestep, temperature and friction together to warnings because of a timestep case (011_membrane_6kuy: eq recovered at 2 fs after a NaN, the default 4 fs production was refused); no reason specific to temperature, and none from the enhanced-sampling work (run_sst2, run_metadynamics and run_fep build their own integrators and never pass that check), was recorded. This narrows only the default, not 17afe45: an explicit different temperature from an eq still runs with a warning.

Surveyed first (five lenses plus a critic, then an adversarial review with per-finding verification, 32 agents). Inheriting alone was not free of side effects: the Slurm preflight filled an omitted flag from the signature default and would have refused every declared-temperature prod command once the default became None; the value has to come from the node whose state is loaded (a continuation after an explicit 300 K production from a 310 K eq must stay at 300 K, so the eq-ancestor rule `pressure_bar` uses is wrong here) and be resolved before the declared-condition check; and rounds/WE schemes would mix temperatures (a 310 K start ran every segment at 300 K before; after naive inheritance, continued walkers of a running scheme would keep 300 K while recycled ones took the basis's temperature).

What changed:
- `mdclaw/node/inputs.py` `_resolve_restart_temperature(job_dir, restart_node_id)`: the restart node's `integrator_signature.temperature_kelvin` (what the restart check compares, so an inherited value never trips it), else `metadata.temperature_kelvin` (SST2 nodes); never a further ancestor, never state.xml. `resolve_node_inputs` for eq and prod returns it, so `explain_node` shows it.
- `run_production`: `temperature_kelvin: Optional[float] = None`. In node mode the restart node and the temperature are resolved before `validate_node_execution_context`; omitted -> inherited from the restart node, else 300 K with a warning saying why (no recorded temperature, or an explicit restart file matching no ancestor); standalone 300 K. `temperature_kelvin_source` (`inherited` / `explicit` / `default`) and `temperature_kelvin_inherited_from` in the result and node metadata, and a warning naming the source node. An explicit temperature or timestep different from a prod parent's signature is now refused after the node-context check and before anything runs (`production_restart_integrator_mismatch`); it used to fail the node after it began, with no code, and `run_rounds` retried it into `rounds_replica_unstable`. A node run directly stays pending; a submitted (queued) one is recorded failed and must be replaced, which the envelope says (the registered text no longer claims either).
- `run_metadynamics`: the same inheritance (a new walker takes the eq's temperature, a continuation its parent walker's), resolved before kT-dependent parameters and the manifest.

## 2026-09-26 — Reworked the SST2 convergence verdict into "temperature cycling + agreement of 300 K structural distributions", and compared 3 solute conditions on 1KXV

The verdict decided in discussion with the user (same day): SST2 convergence is judged by (1) the temperature time series (all rungs visited, round trips, weights) and (3) the change of the 300 K structural distribution, and (2) the connection between the two (does the shape change only at high temperature, or does it interchange at 300 K too) is shown in a figure. `analyze_tempering` computes an observable (solute backbone RMSD by default) every time and compares the MBAR-reweighted 300 K distributions run against run and first half against second half (over bins within 3 kT of the minimum of the pooled distribution and with expected effective frames ≥ 5, the per-bin maximum |ΔF| < 2.5 kJ/mol, and every run visits that bin). `sampling_verdict` = `converged` when both temperature cycling (weight verdict) and distribution agreement hold, `converged_single_run` for 1 run, `not_assessed` if there is no observable. The figure `tempering.png` shows on the left each run's rung time series colored by RMSD, and on the right the 300 K distributions per run and per half. The 2-state dF(t) was demoted to a question-specific number only for `--state-a/--state-b` (`delta_f_verdict`).

Fixes along the way: (a) counting a bin "visit" with the Kish ESS within the bin made even 1 frame with weight 1e-25 at a hot rung count as 1, giving a spurious between-run difference of 142 kJ/mol for H3 + shell. Changed to count with bin probability × overall ESS (expected effective frame count), giving 15.9. (b) `--rmsd-selection "resSeq 98 to 110 and name N CA C O"` picked up water O with the same numbers, making RMSD over 3 nm and NaN in all conditions (an MDTraj DSL trap the user had warned about before). If the selection includes water or ions, it is refused with `tempering_observable_invalid` (248c010).

Results for 1KXV 50 ns × 2 seeds (RMSD in all 3 conditions is the backbone of the 13 H3 residues, superposed on the framework): the maximum between-run difference of the 300 K distribution is 9.6 kJ/mol for H3 only (only seed 1 occupies 3.2–3.6 Å), 15.9 for H3 + shell (though the distributions of both seeds spread to 4.5–6 Å), 5.9 for dihedrals only (both seeds never leave the vicinity of the crystal). The first-half vs second-half differences are 9.0 / 4.5 / 2.8. All 3 conditions are `not_converged`. Looking at the RMSD-colored rung time series, H3 only and dihedrals only cycle temperature well (48–418 round trips) but do not change shape at 300 K; H3-only seed 1 entered another shape at high temperature (the Tyr101–Gly102–Leu103 backbone rearranges, Gly102 φ −65°→149°, not a Pro104–Gly105 flip), brought it back to 300 K after 38 ns and stayed. H3 + shell interchanges shape even at 300 K, but the ladder is coarse with rung exchange 3–5 % and 7–13 round trips. Next: H3 + shell with an 8–9 rung ladder, 2 seeds. The 300 K distribution of plain MD (prod_014/015) rises just before 3 Å, and occupancy of B (2.5–6 Å) is 0–0.4 %.

## 2026-09-25 — Added an SST2 sampling convergence verdict (dF(t)) to `analyze_tempering`

User request (a figure that judges sampling convergence as for metadynamics, with a method suited to SST2). Replaced the "2-state dF(t) and second-half drift" of `analyze_metadynamics` with an SST2 version. SST2 has no CV, so the observable is the solute backbone RMSD (default: solute N/CA/C/O, superposed on protein CA outside the solute, reference the topo's topology.pdb = starting structure; all overridable). Given 2 RMSD ranges (nm) via `--state-a/--state-b`, MBAR is re-solved using only the rows recorded up to each time, giving the 300 K dF(A − B) as a function of time (both for the pool of all runs and for each run alone, 20 points by default). Verdict `sampling_verdict`: `converged` when the second-half drift of the pooled dF < 2.5 kJ/mol, the difference of final values between runs < 5 kJ/mol, and the 300 K effective frames of both states ≥ 10. Artifacts `tempering_delta_f.csv` / `.png` (left dF(t), right the 300 K RMSD profile, pooled and per run), and an `rmsd_nm` column in the frames table.

Terminology correction (user's observation): SST2 is a single-walker method in which one trajectory traverses rungs; there are no coupled walkers as in metadynamics. "walker" in the output keys means "independent run (seed)", and the figure and skill say run.

Handling 1 run (user's observation "sometimes there's only one"): checking with 1KXV H3 only, seed 2 (prod_011) alone is flat at dF ≈ −11 kJ/mol after 17 ns with small second-half drift, passing the time-direction check, but seed 1 (prod_008) ends at +6 (the pool is −1.3, second-half drift 6.8, run difference 17.2 → `not_converged`). When a single trajectory stays in one basin it looks self-consistent in time, so when 1 run passes the check it now returns `converged_single_run` rather than `converged` (the skill says "report as unconfirmed, add another seed if needed").

Verification: on a DCD in which RMSD is tied to the coordinates of a synthetic Gaussian model (ALA of alanine dipeptide translated by x + 5 nm, superposed on the caps), dF is −0.92 kJ/mol against the exact value −0.94. A bug found along the way: in direct mode the 2 runs had the same node_id (the name of the report's grandparent directory), and since the observable cache was looked up by node_id, run 2 was using run 1's trajectory. Fixed to look up by trajectory path. 17 tests pass. 33 s on 1KXV (2 runs × 50 ns, 10,000 frames), results in analyze_004–006.
