## 2026-09-18 — Collapsed aromatic rings in MODELLER loop models: added a check and excluded them from selection (b6b7721, pushed), shared image is `modgeom-28f5e4a4f461`

While rebuilding the 9 systems of the T1R bundle from prep (`/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/t1r/systems_v2/`), the topo of hum-ecd-9opw-apo stopped with `built_system_energy_implausible` (1.4e11 kJ/mol). Tracing it, the cause was in the model returned by prep's missing-residue completion: the rings of PHE A53 and A373 were folded onto themselves (ring diagonal atoms 0.34 Å). Of MODELLER's 4 output models, the initial loop model had collapsed PHE A29 / TRP A317 / TYR A333, loop model 2 had collapsed PHE A53 / A373, and loop model 1 had VAL B364's CG1/CG2 at 0.89 Å. DOPE does not rank these last, so mdclaw had been picking collapsed models. The 9OPW topo made on 2026-09-10 (6.2e10 kJ/mol, PHE A373 in the same shape) came through the same path.

Fix: added `_model_geometry_issues()` to `genesis/modeller.py`, which lists heavy atoms within a residue closer than 1.0 Å, between residues closer than 0.5 Å (threshold lowered because templates assembled from rigid parts can have contacts around 1 Å), and Phe/Tyr/Trp ring diagonals shorter than 2.0 Å. All models are checked and the lowest DOPE among those that pass is chosen (`_among_geometry_valid_models` in `selection_reason`); dropped models are listed in a warning, and if all fail it fails with `modeller_models_geometry_invalid`. Prep completion in `structure/clean_protein.py` retries once with 8 models and a different seed when all fail. Worked in practice: for 9OPW both models failed → 4 of 8 passed on retry → completed with a sound model, no collapse in merged. Tests `tests/test_modeller_geometry.py` (planar ring, folded ring, an inter-residue contact of 0.97 Å is allowed); 251 MODELLER/prep/genesis tests pass.

Image: `mdclaw-rikyu-arm64-cuda130-cufft121-modgeom-28f5e4a4f461.sif`, 3 files layered onto tempering-de7d17bb7ec5 (main 7ee4be8) (7,438,577,664 B, sha256 `fa683b6a…`, 197 files match `b6b7721`). Acceptance on c287 (job 123440, 4 min 47 s): 3WD5 cell 58 s, water rigid, 500 iterations normal, fast suite 2,279 passed / 2 skipped. Switched the shared path at 06:40 JST; rollback is `…pre-modgeom-20260918.sif`. Updated both copies of RIKYU.md. Another session's SEUS work (`simulation/expanded_ensemble.py` etc.) is still uncommitted and was included in neither the push nor the image.

## 2026-09-18 — Pablo-path water was never rigid: fixed (8c0f83f, d11f8ed, a500ac8, pushed), shared RIKYU image switched to `water-011cf9894d92`

Found while auditing the T1R ECD bundle for Rikyu (`/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/t1r`, `run/rikyu_check_20260917.md`): hum-ecd-9opw-apo's shipped topo had OPC water with 2 constraints per water, an H–O–H angle term and hydrogens at 4 amu (O 10.016), while the other eight systems had rigid OPC. The one difference was the loader: 9opw was the only ligand-free system Pablo could parse, the others fell back to `PDBFile`. Mechanism, verified in OpenMM 8.5.1 `forcefield.py` (line 1300): `createSystem` recognises water by `res.name == 'HOH'` for both the rigid-water constraints and the `hydrogenMass` exemption; `PDBFile` rewrites WAT→HOH on read, Pablo keeps the file's names and the solvent fast path (b648068) copied them verbatim. Not water-model specific: sampled Pablo-built topos across the campaigns — v2 2axf (09-12, TIP3P), v4 1ewf (09-16, TIP3P, 581k atoms), sst2-trials 1kxv (09-16, OPC), seus-trials cln025 (09-17, OPC), and the 1AKE study of 08-01 (OPC) — all show 2 constraints per water, one angle term per water, O 10.015/10.016 and H 4.0; fallback-built 1dpt (09-16) is rigid. Of 1,505 completed topo nodes on disk, 702 built on or after 09-14 went through Pablo. The O–H constraints kept 4 fs stable, so nothing crashed; the water just ran with a flexible angle and heavy hydrogens. Any study whose topo node has `topology_validation.loader.used_pablo: true` should rebuild its topo node.

Fix in three commits on main, pushed: `_topology_pablo.py` names water `HOH` after every load path (fast path block and pure Pablo), taking the name set from PDBFile's own replacement table plus `WATER_NAMES`, guarded by composition (one O, ≤2 H, massless extra points allowed); a residue that is water by composition under a name nobody knows is reported as `unrecognised_water` and `build_amber_system` / `build_openmm_system` refuse with `water_residue_name_unrecognised` (user request: stop, never build such water silently). Tests: fast-path expectation now HOH, name-set and unknown-name tests added; loader, registry, CLI suites pass (registry files staged hunk-wise around the uncommitted SEUS entries). Verified the pure-Pablo branch too: cln025 rebuilt on a scratch DAG copy gives 3 constraints per water, O 16 / H 1.008, no angle terms.

Image: source overlay of the 4 changed packaged files on `protonation-7c66c59d41fe` → `mdclaw-rikyu-arm64-cuda130-cufft121-water-011cf9894d92.sif` (7,438,520,320 bytes, sha256 `e86b9179…`, all 196 packaged files equal `a500ac8`, evidence in `.validation/water-20260918/`). Acceptance on c179 (job 122757, 4.5 min): the 343k-atom WAT-named TIP3P 3WD5 cell through the Pablo fast path on the GPU gives 3 constraints per water, no water angle terms, masses 15.999/1.008, protein HMR intact; 500 iterations clean; fast suite 2267 passed / 2 skipped with the stale `test_pdb_writefile_inventory_is_pinned` deselected (unchanged since the SST2 commit). A first candidate (`dd3455f3faa7`, 8c0f83f only) also passed acceptance (job 122743, c149) and was discarded when the two follow-up commits landed. Shared path switched 00:32 JST with the usual atomic relink; rollback link `…pre-water-20260918.sif` → the protonation image. RIKYU.md (both copies) updated. Members need `git pull` because their clones overlay the image on the login node.

## 2026-09-18 — `analyze_tempering`: MBAR reweighting of SST2 walkers and weight-convergence verdict as an analyze node

SST2 analysis existed only in hand-written scripts outside the DAG (`analysis_interim/`), which agents could not reproduce, so added `analyze_tempering` (`@node_tool(node_type="analyze")`) to `mdclaw/analyze/tempering.py`. Parents are `run_sst2` prod leaves (one walker = one parent; with `production_chain` the `continue_from` chain is bundled oldest first, with `segment` only the leaf; `comparison` is refused with `tempering_scope_unsupported`). From each row of `tempering.csv` (one per exchange attempt, 2 ps), it builds u_m(x) = β_ref [Σ_f λ_m^f E_f + √λ_m E_pw] for every rung (E_ww and the unscaled solute terms cancel between rungs) and solves pymbar 4.2's MBAR over the pool of all walkers. Outputs are `weights.json` (f_k as a list in kJ/mol, passed as is to the next stage's `run_sst2 --weights-file`), `tempering_frames.csv` (per DCD frame: walker, node, frame, chain_frame, step, time_ns, rung, temperature, log_weight, weight; a λ-tagged data format for the surrogate), `tempering_mbar.json`, and `tempering.png` (per-walker rung time series, and the deviation of the on-the-fly weights and per-walker MBAR from the pooled f_k). `verdict` is `weights_converged` if all of the following hold: every rung visited, each walker's on-the-fly weights and standalone MBAR within 2.5 kJ/mol (1 kT at 300 K) of the pooled f_k, 5 or more round trips, and a rung change rate of 0.1 or more; otherwise `weights_drifting` with `verdict_reasons`. Has `discard_ns`, `fixed_weights_only`, and `row_stride`. Frame rows are identified as multiples of step from `output_frequency_ps` / `timestep_fs`, and the DCD frame count is cross-checked by reading the header directly without mdtraj (mdtraj's dcdplugin writes to stdout and breaks the CLI's JSON; it actually broke, so this was fixed). Error codes are not picked up by the registration scanner unless written in `code=` keyword form (the same pitfall as last time).

Validation: on a 1D Gaussian model where f_k is known in closed form (E_pw = a·x, rung k's distribution is N(−c_k, 1), f_k = −c_k²/2), MBAR reproduces f_k within 0.1 kT; frame-table alignment, `segment` / `fixed_weights_only` / refusal of mixed ladders / refusal of non-SST2 parents are pinned in `tests/test_analyze_tempering.py` (9 tests). Results from running the real 1KXV data through the DAG: H3 only (analyze_001, prod_008 + prod_011) f_k = 0 / 255.7 / 466.2 / 643.4 / 787.9 kJ/mol (matches the hand-computed MBAR), frame ESS 2,465 / 10,000, verdict `weights_drifting` (difference from the on-the-fly weights 9.4 kJ/mol; the top rung of per-walker MBAR is 779.6 vs 795.1, a 15.5 kJ/mol difference). In other words, writing last time that they "agree within a few kJ/mol" was too lenient; the top rung differs by 6 kT between seeds. Not converged at 50 ns; extension is needed. H3 + shell (analyze_002) is the same. Dihedral only (analyze_003): seed 1 is trapped with 1 round trip and weights 25 kJ/mol off; seed 2 has 418 round trips. On the `run_sst2` side, the `sst2_sst2.pdb/.cif` that SST2 leaves behind is now deleted. Skill: created `skills/md-analyze/tempering.md`, linked from `md-analyze/SKILL.md` and `metrics.md`, rewrote `md-production/sst2.md` as a 2-stage procedure (adaptive → `analyze_tempering` → fixed weights), and removed the old statement that `MDCLAW_SST2_HOME` is required. The `sst2_not_installed` guidance text was also changed to assume bundling.

Rollout to the shared image (same day 01:34 JST): `.validation/tempering-20260918/build-tempering-candidate.sh` source-overlaid 4 files (`analyze/tempering.py` new, `analyze/__init__.py`, `guardrail_codes.py`, `simulation/tempering.py`) onto the water image `011cf9894d92` (main a500ac8 + SST2 5590f4f) → `mdclaw-rikyu-arm64-cuda130-cufft121-tempering-de7d17bb7ec5.sif` (7,438,561,280 bytes, sha256 `70d911f5…`, 197 files match 7ee4be8). GPU acceptance (job 122840, c179, 4 min 19 s, `/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/mdclaw-validation/tempering-20260918/`): `analyze_tempering` appears in the baked package's CLI, CUDA present, on a copy of the 1KXV job (without DCDs) `analyze_tempering` through the DAG reproduces the same f_k as on the login node (top rung 787.9) and 10,000 frames, `run_sst2` 20 ps on CUDA completes as a prod node with no leftovers, fast suite 2276 pass / 2 skip (`test_pdb_writefile_inventory_is_pinned` excluded as before). Switched the shared path with the usual atomic relink; rollback link `…pre-tempering-20260918.sif` → the water image. Updated RIKYU.md (both copies). ## 2026-09-17 — Dataset generation policy for the VHH surrogate: ensemble only, all SST2 rungs as λ-tagged training data, 3-tier sequence set at 10,000–15,000 GPU hours

Estimated from the numbers after the 1KXV 50 ns block completed. Packing 6 SST2 walkers onto 1 GPU with MPS, 300 ns takes 4 h 21 min (aggregate 1,650 ns/GPU-day, 0.0145 GPU hours/ns, 275 ns/day per walker). The user's proposal of "1,000 VHH × 3 replicas × 1 µs" is 3.0 × 10⁶ ns → about 43,600 GPU hours (1,820 GPU days, about 14.4 million yen at 330 yen/GPU hour). With a 10 Å buffer + 8 per GPU, an estimated 30,000–36,000 (not measured). When packed, the extra cost of SST2 is almost the same as packing ordinary MD; the 2× slowdown seen when running alone does not appear because the wait at exchange steps is hidden by MPS.

User decision: the surrogate can target the ensemble (p(x | sequence) at 300 K) rather than dynamics. The generation policy that follows (written in `docs/research/sst2-seus-plan.md` §7 "Dataset generation policy"): (1) Save frames from all SST2 rungs with λ and MBAR weights, as training data for a temperature-conditioned generative model (300 K reweighting alone gives an ESS of 25 %). (2) Start from predicted structures (Boltz-2), with the solute defined by Kabat positions. (3) The sequence set has 3 tiers, breadth (1,000–2,000 × 1 × 200–300 ns), depth (100 × 3 × 1 µs), and mutational neighborhood (20 parents × 30 variants × 300 ns), totaling 10,000–15,000 GPU hours. (4) An active loop that trains the model partway through the breadth tier and sends sequences with low reweighting ESS next. Swarm MD at 300 K for dynamics is no longer needed.

## 2026-09-17 — `protonation_method` "standard" renamed to "no-prediction"; the CLI listing and the prep receipt now say what the method did

Why: in the kimi-k3 v4 and glm-5.3-flash campaigns four cli_skill_sif attempts (008 r2, 013 r1, 069 r2; glm 025 r2) translated the prompt's "standard state at pH 7" into `--ph 7.0` and left propka running, and propka moved an ionisable residue off the fixed state in about 1 of 10 such attempts (36 of 39 `--ph`-only attempts passed; 214 of 214 with the fixed-state method). ## 2026-09-16 — Scorer recalibration: what the two campaigns say the prep and md axes should tolerate

Background: MDDB project metadata (80 fields per project, checked live on A01M3, A0001, A002J) has no pH or protonation field; the only protonation record is the reference topology's residue names, from which the task builder derives `stated_protonation` (6 tasks name protonated histidines: 007, 009, 014, 088, 096, 100). The other 92 references are all-standard because that is how they were built (MoDEL entries with Amber 8 / Parm99, the newer ones with pdb2gmx defaults), not because anyone chose pH 7. So the v0.4 sentence "every ionisable side chain in its standard state at pH 7" encodes a build convention, and the four propka failures (kimi v4 008 r2, 013 r1, 069 r2; glm 025 r2) measure convention-matching. Decision with the user: dataset v0.5 drops the blanket sentence ("neutral pH; ionisation states of the side chains are your choice"), keeps the six named-residue sentences (with the residue name, e.g. HIP, so it maps onto `--protonation-states`), and the scorer tolerates ±1 H on ASP/GLU/LYS/HIS/CYS the task does not name; named residues stay strict. mdclaw keeps `propka` as the default; `standard` is to be renamed (`no-prediction`), described in `--list-json`, and reported in the receipt with the residues propka moved.

Prep axis, second change: the metal-ligand exemption is read from `minimized_structure.pdb` at 3.5 A, so 062 r3's zinc leaving two thiolates during minimisation turned CYM224 into a composition failure while r1/r2 with identical flags passed. Derive the exemption from prep's declared `metal_sites` instead.

md axis: no loosening warranted. Over the 588 skill attempts of kimi-k3 v4 and glm-5.3-flash, 586 radius-of-gyration checks and 562 fluctuation-magnitude checks were parsed against their calibrated bands (reference 1 ns windows, n=30, widened by 4 window SD; the lower fluctuation bound is diagnostic). Only 2 checks failed, both just outside the upper edge: 048 r2 Rg over by 1.5 % of the band width, 040 r3 fluctuation over by 1.0 %; both were the shortest-equilibration replicate of their task. Inside the band the median distance to the nearest edge is 43 % of the width, the 5th percentile 16-27 %, and 2-3 checks per axis sit within 5 % of an edge. A false-fail rate of about 2 in 1,150 is consistent with the calibration's intent (an unwidened band was measured to reject a correct submission 7-16 % of the time), so the bands stay; the two failures are the price of cutting equilibration, which the skill's default protocol avoids. Twelve fluctuation values fell below the lower bound (nucleic tasks 047, 053, 056, 057, 059), all reported as diagnostic and passed, which is the intended behaviour for stiff DNA/RNA runs.

## 2026-09-16 — kimi-k3 v4 cli_skill_sif: 289 of 294; the five failures by cause, and the propka question

v4 finished 21:14 JST (882/882; cli_sif 282/294, cli_skill_sif 289/294, sif_only 32/294). All five skill-condition failures are 19/20 evaluation failures; none is a timeout, a CLI error or a gateway loss. By cause:

**A. propka assigned a non-standard ionisation state although the prompt asks for standard states (3).** 008_membrane_6i53 r2 (GLH303, HIP56), 013_membrane_6ps2 r1 (ASH79), 069_soluble_1aol r2 (HIP112). Each ran `prepare_complex` with `--ph 7.0` (or `--ph 7`) and without `--protonation-method standard`; the passing replicates of the same tasks used `standard` (013 r2 even re-ran with it after a first `--ph 7.0` prep; 069 r3 patched HIP112 with `--protonation-states '{"A:112":"HID"}'`). The reasoning is the same in all three and in glm's 025 r2: "propka at pH 7 would give the standard states anyway; to be safe pass --ph 7.0". Two of the three had read `prep-chemistry.md`, whose lines 100-108 say to pass `--protonation-method standard`; the rule was read and rationalised away. Across both campaigns' skill attempts: with `--protonation-method standard` 214 of 214 passed; with `--ph` only, 36 of 39 passed, and all four campaign failures of this kind (kimi 3, glm 1) are in that group, so propka moves an ionisable residue off its standard state in about 1 attempt in 10. The scorer has no tolerance for it by design (`residue_atom_counts_match_reference` is tautomer-blind but counts every ionisation variant; the only exemptions are metal ligands and catalytic dyads), and every v0.4 prompt carries the sentence "Simulate every ionisable side chain in its standard state at pH 7". Whether that sentence and the strict count stay is a dataset decision (see below).

**B. Equilibration cut short, MD statistic lands just outside the reference window (1).** 048_nucleic_1h9t r2: Rg 20.564 A against [19.436, 20.547] A, eq NVT 0.1 + NPT 0.5 ns and prod 1.0 ns; r1 and r3 ran the skill's 1 + 1 ns and 1.1-1.2 ns prod and measured 20.22 and 19.91 A. Same shape as glm's 040 r3 (0.740 vs 0.736 A with the shortest protocol of its three).

**C. Zinc site came apart at minimisation and the scorer's distance-based exemption then exposed a thiolate (1).** 062_metal_6w9c r3: prep, topo and min were flag-identical to r1 (chains C + I, ZN C402 `ZN-Cys3` site established, CYM189/192/224, ff14SB non-bonded zinc, `run_minimization --restraint-atoms solute_heavy --restraint-force-constant 100`), but in the minimised structure r1 keeps all three SG at 1.9 A from the zinc while r3 keeps only CYM192; the ion (not covered by the solute-heavy restraint) left two thiolates. The scorer reads metal ligands from `minimized_structure.pdb` with a 3.5 A cutoff, so r3's exemption set fell from 6 to 5 residues and CYM224 (10 atoms) was compared against the reference's CYS224 (11). Two fix candidates: mdclaw should restrain or bond an established metal site through min/eq (and the topo receipt should state the metal model used; today `applied.facts` has no metal entry); MDDataBench's exemption should come from the declared site (prep `metal_sites`) rather than a frame.

Pattern across kimi-k3 v4 and glm-5.3-flash (10 failures in 588 skill attempts): 4 propka-vs-standard, 2 shortened equilibration, 2 membrane build choices (glm only), 1 zinc-site collapse, 1 infrastructure segfault. No failure came from the CLI being hard to operate.

**The propka question (user, 2026-09-16: "unless specified, propka variance was meant to be tolerated").** As shipped it is not tolerated, and the prompt does specify: the standard-state sentence is in all 98 tasks, and the MDDB references were built with standard states. If the benchmark should instead accept any ionisation the agent's pKa predictor chooses for residues the prompt does not name, two things change together: the sentence is rewritten to say so, and `compare_monomer` gets an ionisation tolerance (±1 H on ASP/GLU/HIS/LYS/CYS not named in the task) alongside the existing tautomer tolerance; the four failures above and qwen's 023 would then pass (kimi-k3 v4 skill 292/294, glm 291/294). Recommendation: keep the sentence and the strict count. The reference is at standard states, a HIP or ASH changes the charge and the dynamics the md axis compares, and following an explicit protonation instruction is part of what the prep axis measures; the 1-in-10 propka deviation is real chemistry the agent is asked to override, and the skill already says how. Decision pending with the user.

## 2026-09-16 — Root causes of every glm-5.3-flash cli_skill_sif failure (5 of 294), from the transcripts

All five read the skills (36-39 files each); none is a CLI-operation error. Each failure is one decision, and for four of them the transcript shows the reasoning.

1. **002_membrane_5zk3 r1, timeout at the solv node.** Thinking: "Default example uses dist 15, dist-wat 17.5 — that creates a big box (long build time and big system). For speed, smaller box is better: dist 10.0, dist-wat 10.0." The agent did not know `dist_wat` is part of the patch-cache fingerprint; the miss started a CPU patch equilibration on the login node. `membrane.md` mentions `dist_wat` only in the Packmol-race retry paragraph ("keep leaflet and dist_wat unchanged unless the user explicitly asks") and says "common compositions are pre-built" without naming them or the parameters that select them. The agent read the page 11 times and still optimised the wrong variable. Fix: state next to the embed example that lipids, ratio, water model, salt, `dist_wat`, `leaflet` and `patch_side` select the cached patch and that changing them rebuilds it on the host; list the bundled compositions; CLI refusal on a CPU-host miss (known-issues).

2. **010_membrane_6kux r3, timeout at the solv node, detached script.** Thinking: "The patch-tile cold build runs MD (OpenMM equilibration of the patch) ... strictly, the patch equilibration inside embed_in_membrane is MD computation [that must go through Slurm] ... is DPPC pre-built in the bundled cache? If not, the cold build happens ... 3. Use packmol-memgen legacy backend: no patch cold-build." The agent chose the legacy full-box backend to avoid a cold build that would not have happened (DPPC/TIP3P at the default geometry is bundled; r1 and r2 embedded in about 70 s), and the legacy path ran packmol for 25+ minutes on the CPU. Two gaps: there is no way to ask the CLI whether a composition is cached (`probe_patch_cache` exists in `patch_membrane.py` but is not a tool), and `membrane.md` lists `--membrane-backend packmol-memgen` as a plain option without saying it is slower and CPU-bound. Fix: expose the cache probe (or report it in `explain_node` for a solv node), and mark the legacy backend as a debugging path in the skill; CLI warn/refuse on CPU hosts (known-issues).

3. **025_complex_1akj r2, 19/20, HIP3 and HIP151.** Thinking: "prepare_complex presumably runs protonation via PDBFixer/PDB2PQR at pH 7. Default. His neutral ... At pH 7.4, propka would still usually assign neutral HIS (pKa ~6.5). But to be safe, pass `--ph 7.0`." The rule "when the request asks for standard states pass `--protonation-method standard`" lives in `prep-chemistry.md` (lines 100-108); r1 read that page and passed, r2 read 36 skill files including `defaults-and-guardrails.md` but not `prep-chemistry.md`, and the spine (`SKILL.md` step 4) only says to read it "for the protonation baseline". The receipt then reported nothing about histidine states, so the propka result went unnoticed. Fix: put the one-line standard-state rule in the spine (or in `defaults-and-guardrails.md`, which every agent reads), and add the histidine/ionisable-state tally and the method used to the prep receipt facts.

4. **040_ligand_3n2u r3, 19/20, fluctuation 0.7400 A against the reference window [0.3398, 0.7360].** The three replicates ran the same system (1,269 solute heavy atoms, 4 fs HMR, 298 K) with different protocols: r1 NVT 1 ns + NPT 1 ns, prod 1.25 ns, fluctuation 0.62 A; r2 0.1 + 0.15 ns, prod 1.2 ns, 0.67 A; r3 0.1 + 0.1 ns, prod 1.0 ns, 0.74 A. The value rises as equilibration and production shrink, so this is the shortest protocol landing 0.004 A above the window's upper edge; r1 shows the 20-minute MD limit allowed the skill's default 1 + 1 ns. Not a defect anywhere; a budget shortcut that cost the margin.

5. **090_soluble_1aa3 r3, `production_incomplete`.** eq job 114913 died 14 s into `singularity exec --nv` on c165 with a bare "Segmentation fault" before any OpenMM output; min on the same node had completed 10 s earlier; the only segfault in this week's Slurm logs across all campaigns. Reset with `--force true` and rerun: 20/20 in 302 s.

Pattern: 3 of 5 are the model trading the skill's defaults for speed or caution (smaller box, legacy backend, shorter equilibration), 1 is a routing miss inside the skill (the rule sat on a page the agent did not open), 1 is infrastructure. Skill-side fixes recorded in `roadmap-and-known-issues.md` under "Skill Text Fixes from the glm-5.3-flash Campaign".

## 2026-09-16 — Interim analysis of the 1KXV SST2 trial run (at 38 ns): the H3 + shell walker found an H3 basin absent from 200 ns of ordinary MD

Interim analysis outside the DAG (`sst2-trials/1kxv-h3/analysis_interim/`, mdtraj). Using cos/sin of H3 (residues 98–110) φ/ψ as features, fit a PCA on frames from all conditions (PC1 32 %, PC2 14 %) and plotted the 2D −kT ln P per condition (`h3_fes_interim.png`). On the SST2 side, only frames that were at the 300 K rung (an approximation, since this is the adaptive stage). The 2 ordinary MD runs, 200 ns, show only 2 basins at PC2 ≈ 0. SST2 H3 only (14 ns at 300 K) visited those same 2 basins plus states at PC2 ≈ −1 and −2.3, and H3 + 5 Å shell (33 ns likewise) additionally visited a broad basin at PC2 ≈ −3. That basin is not a proline cis state (cis fraction 0 for H3's Pro104/107/110) but a flip of the Pro104–Gly105 peptide plane (ψ104 and φ105 differ by about 170°, a backbone flip of Gly105). It was found by shell seed 1 (920 of 1398 300 K frames) and H3-only seed 1 (25 frames); the two seed 2 runs never visited it. The long residence is because the walker stayed stuck in that basin, so the free-energy difference cannot be trusted yet. Rung statistics: H3 only has 45–83 round trips at 38 ns, and the weights are stable within each run but differ by 20 kJ/mol at the top rung between seeds. H3 + shell has an exchange rate of 3–4 % and 7–10 round trips; the ladder is coarse. Dihedral-only seed 1 never visited the bottom 2 rungs (adaptive-weight trap); seed 2 had 303 round trips. The 2 ordinary-MD negative controls (prod_014/015, 100 ns each, 823 ns/day) are complete. Counting the number of 120° bin changes between frames 10 ps apart as "transitions" saturated at 95/ns for all conditions and was meaningless as a metric (next time, count inter-basin transitions).

A version using frames from all rungs via MBAR (`mbar_fes.py`, pymbar 4.2): from the fractional terms E_t and E_pw in the report CSV, build u_m(X) = β[Σ λ_m^f E_t + √λ_m E_pw] for all rungs and run MBAR with rung occupancy counts N_k. ESS at 300 K is 1903 / 8790 frames for H3 only (1402 with rung 0 alone), 3732 / 8806 (3293) for H3 + shell, and 766 / 8920 (353) for dihedral only. MBAR's rung free energies agree with SST2's on-the-fly weights within a few kJ/mol (H3 only: MBAR 256/466/643/788, seed 1 253/460/635/777, seed 2 257/469/648/795), falling in the middle of the seed-to-seed spread. For dihedral only, MBAR matches seed 2's weights exactly, while seed 1's weights are 25 kJ/mol off at the top rung, confirming that the weights of the walker that could not return to the lower rungs were biased. Figure `h3_fes_interim_mbar.png` (crystal structure overlaid as a star: PC1 0.59, PC2 −0.04, inside the deepest basin).

## 2026-09-22 — `analyze_metadynamics`: reduced the convergence verdict to a single quantity, "late-half drift of ΔF(t) between 2 states"

At the user's request (a simple quantity that can be written in a paper and understood by people, rather than many verdict quantities), added `mdclaw/analyze/metadynamics.py::analyze_metadynamics` (`@node_tool("analyze")`, parents are `run_metadynamics` prod nodes sharing the same bias, `production_chain` / `segment`). It takes `--state-a LO HI --state-b LO HI` (nm, disjoint, within the bias range), sums the hills of all walkers in time order, reconstructs F(s, t) = −γ/(γ−1)·V(s, t) at `n_time_points` (50) times, and writes ΔF(t) = −kT ln[∫_A e^{−F/kT} / ∫_B e^{−F/kT}] to `metadynamics_delta_f.csv` / `.png` and `metadynamics.json`. The verdict is `converged` if "drift over the second half < `drift_tolerance_kj_mol` (2.5 = 1 kT) and both states visited", and the reported value is `delta_f_kj_mol ± drift_second_half_kj_mol`. Only two diagnostic warnings: `walkers_unequal_residence` (difference in A-residence fraction > 0.5 between walkers sharing the same bias, a sign of an orthogonal slow variable) and `gaussian_height_not_decayed` (final height over 10 % of the initial). 6 codes; tests `tests/test_analyze_metadynamics.py` 4 tests (agreement with the analytic solution for 2 plateaus, the 3 verdict cases, refusal of state specifications, walker inconsistency, node mode with 2 toy walkers); registry / cli / guardrail 154 tests; golden regenerated (98 tools, 474 codes). Skill `skills/md-analyze/metadynamics.md`, routing from md-analyze / md-production, tool-reference.

Analyze nodes for the 3 systems (`analyze_001` each): Ala3 (compact 0.55–0.95 vs extended 1.05–1.5) ΔF = −1.2 ± 2.6 kJ/mol → not_converged (drift 2.55, right at the threshold); deca-alanine (helix 1.0–1.8 vs extended 2.4–3.4) ΔF = −3.3 ± 2.7 → not_converged; chignolin (folded 0.45–0.8 vs unfolded 1.2–2.3) ΔF = −3.2 ± 4.1 → not_converged + `walkers_unequal_residence` (A-residence fractions 0.00 / 0.03 / 0.79 / 0.06). This agrees with the manual conclusion (Ala3 converged at the 1 kT level, the other 2 systems have hidden variables), and the warning automatically points out chignolin's hidden variable. The `run_metadynamics` / `analyze_metadynamics` set was committed as 6941312 and pushed to origin/main (2 commits together with the minimum-image fix in 6d7cdcc). The memo and another session's rounds / WE changes remain uncommitted.

## 2026-09-22 — `run_metadynamics`: OpenMM's built-in well-tempered metadynamics as a prod node

`mdclaw/simulation/metadynamics.py::run_metadynamics` (`@node_tool("prod")`). The CV is the same centroid-to-centroid distance as `distance_restraints` (`resolve_centroid_groups`; raw coordinates within a molecule, minimum image between molecules with `cv_max_nm` up to half the box). With `openmm.app.metadynamics.Metadynamics` + `BiasVariable` it deposits hills on a grid over `[cv_min_nm, cv_max_nm]` (default 5 points per width), well-tempered via `bias_factor`. Outside the grid, a harmonic wall (`wall_force_constant_kj_mol_nm2`, force group 30). **Multiple walkers** use OpenMM's mechanism as is: they share `--bias-dir` (outside the node, under the study), and every `save_interval_ps` (default 100 ps) each writes its own bias `.npy` and reads other walkers' new files. No synchronization; communication is only reading and writing files of a few KB. The first walker writes `metadynamics_manifest.json`, and a walker with different settings is refused with `metadynamics_shared_bias_mismatch`. A single walker's `--continue-from` places the parent's total bias in the child's directory as `bias_0_1.npy` and continues depositing from there (different settings give `metadynamics_restart_mismatch`). Artifacts: in addition to the ones with the same names as production, `metadynamics.csv` (ξ, bias, height per hill), `metadynamics.json`, `metadynamics_total_bias.npy` / `_self_bias.npy`, `free_energy.csv` (F = −(T+ΔT)/ΔT·V, minimum 0). 6 codes. Tests `tests/test_metadynamics.py` 8 tests (toy 2-particle system: standalone, bias accumulating across node continuation, total of 2 walkers in a shared directory, refusal of different settings); registry / cli / guardrail 158 tests; golden regenerated (96 tools, 466 codes). Skill page `skills/md-production/metadynamics.md` (parameter guideline table, limits of applicability, how to read convergence), routing in SKILL.md, tool-reference.

On the first submission (134514), 2 of 4 died immediately with `metadynamics_shared_bias_mismatch`: walkers launched simultaneously under MPS read the manifest, mid-write by another walker, as an empty file (a race). Fix: the manifest is created atomically with a temp file + `os.link` (only the first one can create it), the reader retries every 0.5 s for up to 30 s, and the comparison uses canonical JSON independent of key order. `free_energy_range_kj_mol` is also taken within the visited range (the unvisited grid edge had become the maximum with F = 0). 9 tests. The remaining 2 (prod_056/057) continued as a 2-walker validation. With the fixed version, also submitted 4 walkers each for deca-alanine (grid 0.9–3.5, σ 0.1, γ 8, 4 × 100 ns) and chignolin (0.4–2.3, σ 0.05, γ 12, 4 × 150 ns) (user instruction "also test the ones done with SEUS").

Validation 1 (Ala3, 9/22): 4 walkers × 50 ns from eq_001 of `seus-trials/ala3-e2e`, shared bias (`study/metadynamics/e2e_v1`), grid 0.5–1.55 nm, σ 0.05, h 2.5 kJ/mol, γ 8, every 1 ps (`launch_metad.sh`). Compared against the existing umbrella 20 windows × 20 ns and the unbiased 400 ns PMF (`analysis/pmf_from055.json`).

Validation 1 results (13:10, `analysis/pmf_metad.png`): 2 walkers × 50 ns (the survivors of 134514). F from the total bias has RMS 1.3–1.5 against umbrella over 0.55–0.9 nm and 0.7–0.9 kJ/mol over 0.9–1.5 nm, and 1.1–1.2 kJ/mol against unbiased (F<10). Umbrella vs unbiased is 0.7, so this is nearly within error. Difference from F reconstructed from only the first half of the deposited hills: 0.4–0.9 kJ/mol. Hill height went 2.2 → 0.002 kJ/mol (1/1000). Speed is 760 ns/day each with 2 packed (15 % slower than SEUS's 905, the cost of the GPU round trip for hill deposition). **Edge artifact**: the minimum of F appeared at 0.5 nm (the grid edge = the wall position). Gaussians deposited outside the wall (down to 0.39 nm) pile up on the grid-edge point (OpenMM's `_addGaussian` contributes to the edge even for centers outside the grid). Fix: extend the grid to 4σ beyond the wall (`GRID_MARGIN_SIGMAS`), have `free_energy.csv` report only inside the walls, and set the minimum to 0 within that range. Resubmitted Ala3 with the fix at 4 walkers × 50 ns (`launch_metad2.sh`, bias `e2e_v2`). The running deca-alanine / chignolin use the old grid, so comparisons exclude 1σ at the edges.

Validation 1 v2 (4 walkers × 50 ns, fixed grid, 134605, 15:08, `analysis/pmf_metad_v2.png`): all 4 launched simultaneously without problems. F's minimum at 1.18–1.19 nm (umbrella 1.17). RMS against umbrella is 0.42 over 0.55–0.9 nm, 0.42 over 0.9–1.2, 0.65 kJ/mol over 1.2–1.5, and 0.57–0.60 against unbiased (F<10). Equal to or below umbrella vs unbiased's 0.69, and the 4 walkers' F agree within 0.05 of each other (naturally, since they share the total bias). Difference from the first half of the deposited hills alone: 0.7–1.0 kJ/mol. 50 ns per walker × 4 = 200 ns gives precision equivalent to 400 ns of umbrella.

Validation 2 (deca-alanine, 4 walkers × 100 ns, old grid, 134532, 16:26, `ala10-e2e/analysis/pmf_metad.png`): all 4 shuttle across 0.80–3.65 nm, h goes 2.4 → 0.0004 kJ/mol. RMS excluding 1σ inside the walls (aligned over 1.4–2.6 nm): metadynamics vs umbrella is 1.19 over 1.0–1.6 nm, 0.47 over 1.6–2.4, 0.48 over 2.4–3.0, 0.81 kJ/mol over 3.0–3.4; vs unbiased (F<10) 0.26 / 0.17 / 0.54 (middle to extended side), 1.25 (helix side); vs pooled SEUS 0.47 / 0.29 / 0.53, helix side 1.31. For reference: umbrella vs unbiased 0.35–0.52, pooled SEUS vs umbrella 0.41–0.87. First half of the deposited hills vs all 0.5–0.8 (1.7 over 3.0–3.4). So from the middle to the extended side the 4 methods agree within 0.5 kJ/mol, and only on the helix side (1.0–1.6 nm) does a 1.2–1.3 kJ/mol difference remain (the slow helix-content variable seen with SEUS is at work here too). The minimum of F appearing at the old grid's edge of 0.9 nm is the edge artifact (already confirmed with Ala3 v2 to disappear in the fixed version). Speed is 515 ns/day each with 4 packed (on par with SEUS's 536).

Validation 3 (chignolin, 4 walkers × 150 ns, old grid, 134533, 18:10, `cln025-e2e/analysis/pmf_metad.png`, reference `pmf_ref.json`): hills went 2.3 → 0.0006 kJ/mol; 3 walkers shuttle across 0.45–2.4 nm, only prod_052 reaches just 1.86 nm. RMS excluding 1σ inside the walls and aligned over 0.5–0.9 nm: metadynamics vs umbrella is 2.4 on the folded side 0.5–0.8 nm, 2.1 in the transition 0.8–1.3, 0.5 on the denatured side 1.3–1.8, and 0.8 kJ/mol over 1.8–2.3; vs unbiased (folded side only) 2.1. First half of the deposited hills vs all is 3.4 on the folded side and 0.2–0.6 on the denatured side. On the reference side, umbrella vs unbiased is also 1.8, and umbrella itself has a long within-window correlation time of 1.1 ns. Walker contents: walker 3 is 62 % compact (< 0.7 nm) (native 97 %), the other 3 are 0–2 % compact (1–9 native ↔ unfolded transitions). The total bias is shared among the 4, yet their residence is completely different; that is, a bias that is a function of d alone cannot simultaneously flatten the "native hairpin" and "misfolded/denatured" manifolds. The same hidden-variable diagnosis as SEUS (register): switching to metadynamics gets nothing beyond agreement on the denatured side (0.5–0.8 kJ/mol).

**Summary across the 3 systems (9/22).** Well-tempered metadynamics agrees with the references in all 3 systems in regions where an orthogonal slow variable is not at play: 0.4–0.65 kJ/mol against umbrella and unbiased for Ala3 (400 ns-level precision at 200 ns), 0.2–0.5 on deca-alanine's middle-to-extended side, and 0.5–0.8 kJ/mol on chignolin's denatured side. In regions where it is at play (deca-alanine's helix side 1.2–1.3, chignolin's folded side 2–3 kJ/mol), it has the same limit as SEUS. Operationally it is simpler than SEUS (no windows and no weight learning, 4 walkers launched together communicating only through files, 2–15 % slowdown), so `run_metadynamics` becomes the standard route for distance PMFs. The next step is extending the CVs (angles, dihedrals, 2D) and combining with SST2. GPU time: Ala3 2 × 1.6 h + 4 × 1.6 h, deca-alanine 4.7 h, chignolin 6.4 h ≈ 21 GPU hours.

The replacement is OpenMM's built-in well-tempered metadynamics (`openmm.app.metadynamics.Metadynamics` + the existing centroid-distance force). Reasons (discussion on 9/21–22): it is the standard method for getting a distance PMF from a single walker, needs no windows, weight learning, or Gibbs moves, has positive feedback driving exploration, and multiple walkers only need a shared `biasDir`. ABF is not in OpenMM; the image's PLUMED 2.9 has the `drr` module disabled (no eABF) and no `OPES_METAD` either, but has `METAD` / `ABMD` / `EXTENDED_LAGRANGIAN`. The premise that the limit from orthogonal slow degrees of freedom remains regardless of method is unchanged.

## 2026-09-16 — Intramolecular distance CVs were evaluated with the minimum image: found when deca-alanine's umbrella "stuck fully extended", fixed `distance_restraints` and `run_seus`

Running SEUS vs umbrella on the end-to-end distance of deca-alanine (ACE-Ala10-NME, OPC, 12 Å buffer → 6.6 nm box), the mean distance of all 25 umbrella windows (centers 1.0–3.4 nm) stuck at 2.62–3.30 nm, and the 1.0 nm window did not move while carrying a bias energy of 330 kJ/mol (= 0.5·250·(2.62−1.0)²). The cause was that `load_distance_restraints` always set `usesPeriodicBoundaryConditions=True` on the `CustomCentroidBondForce` for periodic systems. The minimum-image distance wraps at half the box (3.3 nm), so a peptide fully extended to 4.0 nm becomes "real distance 3.98 = minimum image 2.62 nm", and when the umbrella tries to shrink the minimum-image distance, in real space it pulls the two ends apart toward the neighboring image. The peptide was pulled until its bonds were fully stretched and got stuck. `run_seus` broke above 3.3 nm through the same path, and the fixed stage of the 4 walkers had windows with 0 occupancy and was meaningless (scancelled 118257). Ala3 (box 4.85 nm, max 1.5 nm) and the unbiased trajectories are unaffected.

Fix (`restraints.distance_cv_periodicity`, shared by both routes): if the 2 groups are in the same molecule (mdtraj `find_molecules`), the minimum image is not used. OpenMM does not wrap coordinates inside the Context, so intramolecular distances are always correct with raw coordinates. Intermolecular distances keep the minimum image, and if the target (the umbrella target, SEUS's largest window center) exceeds half the shortest box vector, it is refused with `distance_restraint_exceeds_half_box`. `minimum_image` is recorded in the signature of `collective_variables.meta.json` and in `run_seus`'s `groups`. Test `tests/test_seus.py::test_intramolecular_cv_ignores_the_minimum_image...`. Existing umbrella-route results that used "an intramolecular distance with window centers near half the box" should be treated with suspicion (memo 2026-08-26's TAS1R is intermolecular with a box over 100 Å, so it does not apply).

For deca-alanine, resubmitted the 25 umbrella windows and the 4 SEUS walkers from eq_001 with the fixed code (`launch_v2.sh`, labels `*_v2_*`, Slurm 119400/119409/119413/119414, 119428 → 119429). The unbiased 4 × 200 ns runs are kept as is.

**mean_force × 4 results (9/22 03:40, 100 ns each, `analysis/zeta_schemes.png`).** The learned ζ agrees with the MBAR f_k of its own data within 0.1–0.3 kT (self-consistent, better than WL's 0.5–3.4 kT). But all 4 walkers made only 1 end-to-end round trip, 3 of them spent 89 % on the denatured side (≥ 1.2 nm), with 1–13 folded ↔ unfolded transitions. ζ − (−f_umb) is +6 to +8 kT on the folded side and −4 to −7 kT on the unfolded side: in the transition windows (0.9–1.1 nm) the native structure resists stretching so ⟨ξ⟩ − c becomes strongly negative, and the integral of the mean force overestimates the barrier by more than 10 kT → the weights over-penalize the folded windows, and walkers are pushed out to the denatured side and cannot return (the same mechanism as deca-alanine walker 3: "it does not stay in a window, so orthogonal relaxation never finishes"). Only walker 4 had 59 transitions, with ζ at RMS 0.9 kT from umbrella's −f_k and 100 % native compact. Conclusion: mean_force does not overdrive, but in exchange it has no positive feedback driving exploration and gets dragged by the nonequilibrium mean force in the transition windows. WL drives but its weights drift. The practical form is a two-stage "earn round trips with WL, then finish with mean_force", or pooling Σξ across walkers as SST2 does. Either way the orthogonal-relaxation limit remains. Between-walker ζ RMS: sams 6.7, min_visits 1.8, WL 5.2, mean_force 3.5 kT.

**Porting SST2-style weight estimation to windows (9/21, user proposal).** In the same structure as SST2 deriving weights by the trapezoidal rule from per-rung running mean energies, for window center c we have d(βf)/dc = −βk(⟨ξ⟩_c − c), so the difference between adjacent windows follows from the per-window running mean of ξ by the trapezoidal rule (the mean-force version of umbrella integration, the "Park & Pande type" in plan §5). Retrospective check on the chignolin data at hand: umbrella 21 windows × 27 ns gives RMS 0.07 kT against MBAR, and 0.1–0.2 kT on the walker data too. For every walker, the estimate at 50 ns is within 0.4–0.9 kT of the final value. WL's learned ζ had a case deviating by 3.4 kT even from the MBAR f_k of its own data (s2), which cannot happen with the mean force. The manifold problem remains (the difference between the mean-force f_k and umbrella is still 3–4 kT). Implemented as `run_seus --weight-update mean_force` (`--mf-min-samples` 20), with `xi_sum` / `mf_counts` kept in the sidecar so it can continue; passes the stepped-potential toy test with all 4 schemes (169 tests). Submitted mean_force × 4 on chignolin (seeds 31–34, 100 ns, 131340, `launch_adaptive_v3.sh`), to compare side by side with WL.

**Chignolin unbiased 4 × 500 ns (121561, 9/18 01:30).** All 4 are native in every frame of the 500 ns (backbone RMSD < 0.25 nm, Cα1–Cα10 0.43–0.99 nm), 0 unfolding events. CLN025 in ff19SB/OPC never unfolds at 300 K over 500 ns, and the PMF on the denatured side cannot be obtained at all from unbiased runs (as expected). All chignolin jobs complete. GPU time: umbrella 3 × 1.5 h, SAMS adaptive 2 h, umbrella fixed weights 8 h, new-scheme adaptive 4 h, new-scheme fixed 8 h, unbiased 16 h ≈ 43 GPU hours.

**Fixed stage with WL / min_visits's own weights (122197, 4 × 200 ns, 9/17 23:10).** Occupancy did not flatten (WL s1 0.003–0.36, WL s2 0.00–0.24). WL s1 refolded to native in the fixed stage (57 % compact, 90 % native) with a ζ + f_k spread of 1.3 kT; WL s2 was never compact in 200 ns, with a ζ + f_k spread of 9.7 kT (the manifold it learned on differs from the manifold it sits in during the fixed stage). As the summary said, weights flattened during the adaptive stage become meaningless with manifold switches that happen on 100 ns scales.

**Summary (9/17 20:00, answering the user's "does SEUS not work?").** On 3 systems (Ala3, deca-alanine, chignolin), the ξ-direction machinery of `run_seus` was validated (Gibbs moves, the closed-form expression for frozen ζ = MBAR, Wang–Landau weight learning). It beat umbrella at equal compute only on Ala3, where the orthogonal barrier is weak (2–9×). On deca-alanine and chignolin, walkers got caught by orthogonal slow variables (helix content, register), and SEUS-specific disadvantages appeared: weights are learned in that basin, so they break when the basin changes (umbrella is robust because MBAR solves it after the fact); a single walker walks all windows in sequence, so wall-clock time is multiplied by the number of windows; and Gibbs moves shift windows faster than ξ relaxes, so the "stay and wait" behavior never happens. Conclusion: single-distance SEUS has an advantage only for systems with fast orthogonal degrees of freedom, and the systems we want (binding, folding) are the opposite. The investment goes to SST2 (CV-free) as the main line, layering SEUS on SST2 if needed. Binding PMFs rely primarily on umbrella windows + MPS packing. `run_seus` stays as a tool, with the conditions of applicability stated in the skill. Umbrella has the same orthogonal problem, and chignolin's umbrella PMF is a result dependent on the initial condition "started from native", not an equilibrium (user remark 9/17).

**Fixed stage with umbrella-derived weights (121929, 4 × 200 ns, 9/17 19:00).** The 4 walkers continued from the end of the SAMS adaptive node (denatured state) with ζ = −f_k(umbrella) frozen had 0 % compact (< 0.7 nm) frames in 200 ns, occupancy concentrated at 1.3–2.0 nm, and 1 / 1 / 1 / 5 end-to-end round trips. If umbrella's f_k were right, occupancy should be flat, so the compact states walkers can reach (misfolded) are higher in free energy than the native hairpin the umbrella windows hold; that is, the rate-limiting step is refolding to native (µs scale). MBAR's f_k deviates from umbrella by RMS 4.4–6.6 kT, but this is the difference between 2 different conformational ensembles (with / without native), not an error in the estimator. Given the experiment (native most stable, Tm 343 K), the umbrella side (native vs denatured) is closer to the true equilibrium.

**New-scheme results (9/17 15:30, 100 ns each, `analysis/pmf_adaptive_v2.png`).** The gain problem is solved: both Wang–Landau walkers had 24 / 28 end-to-end round trips, γ reached 0.002 / 0.008 kT after 9 / 7 halvings, and occupancy over the last 30 ns was flat at 0.03–0.09. `sams_min_visits` had 4 / 14 round trips with occupancy 0.00–0.19, insufficient (it keeps the clock, but the gain shape is still SAMS). However, the learned ζ differs between walkers by RMS 5.2 kT (WL s1 vs s2), and relative to umbrella's −f_k, WL s1 is +13 kT on the denatured side and WL s2 ±4 kT. The cause is different conformations on the folded side: the umbrella windows at 0.5/0.6 nm started from the crystal structure and the unbiased runs are 100 % native (backbone RMSD 0.06–0.10 nm), but in the compact states of walkers that unfolded once and shrank again, native is 77 % for WL s1, 41 % for min_visits s2, and 19 % for WL s2 (median RMSD 0.32 nm, register-shifted misfolds). Each walker only flattened ζ for the conformational manifold it was in, and the umbrella side also does not leave the native basin in 30 ns, so it gives a "native-only folded ↔ denatured" PMF. Chignolin's refolding to native is µs scale, and with a single distance every method is blocked by the same hidden variable (register). Fixed stage: run 200 ns each with umbrella-derived weights (121929) and with WL / min_visits's own weights (122197, `launch_fixed_v2.sh`), and do the final evaluation with pooled MBAR and the misfolded fraction.

**Implementing SAMS improvements (9/17 11:40, user instruction).** Added `run_seus --weight-update sams|sams_min_visits|wang_landau`. `sams_min_visits` makes the SAMS clock t "visits to the least-visited window × number of windows" instead of the number of exchanges, keeping the gain until the whole ladder has been traversed. `wang_landau` is Rao–Blackwellized Wang–Landau (ζ += γ·p(m|ξ); γ is halved once every window's visit count since the last halving reaches at least `--wl-flatness` (0.8) times the mean; adaptation ends going from `--wl-gamma0` 1 kT to `--wl-gamma-min` 0.01 kT). `weight_update`, `wl_gamma`, `wl_halvings`, `wl_counts` are saved in the sidecar so it can continue. Test: for a ξ that relaxes slowly with short Metropolis moves on a 1D 5 kT stepped potential, all 3 schemes learn the window free energies within 1 kT and visit every window (`test_weight_updates_learn_a_stepped_ladder_with_slow_mixing`). Submitted 2 × 100 ns each of `sams_min_visits` and `wang_landau` on chignolin (121981, `launch_adaptive_v2.sh`), to compare against umbrella's −f_k.

**Chignolin interim (9/17 11:10).** Umbrella 21 windows × 30 ns (first 3 ns discarded): first-half/second-half difference RMS 4.4 kJ/mol, max 14 kJ/mol; in a system with a real barrier, windows do not converge in 30 ns (windows 0.4/0.5 nm are wasted because the hairpin does not shrink below 0.51 nm). MBAR's window free energies rise by about 6 kT from the folded side to the denatured side. Unbiased 4 × 31 ns never leave 0.43–0.99 nm (folded). **SAMS adaptation broke down**: at 50 ns, 3 of 4 walkers are still in stage 1 (the histogram does not flatten), with 1–3 end-to-end traversals, and the frozen ζ is scattered from −24 to +8 kT between walkers. The stage-1 gain t^−0.8 decays with the number of exchanges t (1 ps steps), so in a system where barrier crossing happens only once every few ns, the gain vanishes before exploration finishes (a known assumption of SAMS, which presumes fast mixing). Scancelled the fixed stage 121560, which had started from garbage ζ. Instead, built ζ = −f_k from umbrella's MBAR (`analysis/zeta_from_umbrella.json`) and submitted a fixed stage of 4 × 200 ns with `--weights-file` (`launch_fixed_umbweights.sh`): a test of the fixed-stage estimator and of "with correct weights, can it shuttle across the barrier". Ideas for improving SAMS: decay the gain by round trips or visits instead of exchange count, switch to a Wang–Landau style (halving on each flattening), set a minimum gain for stage 1.

## 2026-09-16 — Implemented `run_seus` (SEUS as a prod node) and submitted a SEUS vs umbrella validation on the end-to-end distance of capped Ala3

Decided to run SEUS (serial expanded-ensemble umbrella sampling) as a background test calculation behind the SST2 session, and wrote it on the MDClaw side under MIT as planned (`docs/research/sst2-seus-plan.md` §5). At the user's instruction it is a CLI that runs as a DAG `prod` node like `run_sst2`, and the CV is the same mass-weighted centroid-to-centroid distance as the existing `distance_restraints` (split out `restraints.resolve_centroid_groups` and shared it between both routes; COM for multi-atom selections, interatomic distance for single atoms).

**Implementation** `mdclaw/simulation/expanded_ensemble.py::run_seus`. A single walker carries `CustomCVForce(0.5*seus_k*(d-seus_r0)^2)` and every `exchange_interval_ps` picks a window by Gibbs sampling over all windows with `p(m|ξ) ∝ exp(-β w_m(ξ) - ζ_m)` (one `context.setParameter`). ζ is adapted with SAMS (Tan 2017, Rao–Blackwellized, two-stage schedule: stage 1 γ=min(π_min, t^-0.8), and once the histogram's relative deviation < 0.3, stage 2 γ=1/(t-t0+t0^0.8)), and the fixed stage uses `--freeze-weights` (the continue_from parent's sidecar) or `--weights-file`. Artifacts are the same names as production (trajectory.dcd / energy.dat / state.xml / final_structure.pdb / collective_variables.csv with a `seus_r0` column), plus a per-exchange `seus.csv` (ξ, window, next window, stage) and `seus.json` (ζ, visit counts, SAMS clock, rng state). `--continue-from` continues a walker (`seus_restart_mismatch` if the ladder, k, or CV differ). 5 codes. `tests/test_seus.py` 10 tests (standalone, node continuation, freezing, COM equivalence on a toy 2-particle system), `test_registry`/`cli`/`guardrail` 217 tests, golden regenerated. Skill page `skills/md-production/seus.md`.

**Validation system** `/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/seus-trials/ala3-e2e` (`launch.sh`). ACE-ALA3-NME built with tleap registered as a local source → prep (caps kept) → solv (OPC, 15 Å, 0.15 M NaCl) → topo (ff19SB/OPC/HMR, 14,478 atoms, box 48.5 Å) → min → eq (NVT 0.2 ns + NPT 1 ns). The CV is the distance between `resname ACE and name CH3` and `resname NME and name C` (1.465 nm fully extended). 23 windows from 0.40–1.50 nm in 0.05 steps, k = 1000 kJ/mol/nm².
- Reference: 23 window nodes of `run_production --distance-restraints`, 5.5 ns each (first 0.5 ns discarded), output 2 ps, 3 jobs packed 8/8/7 with `submit_mps_job` (117772–117774).
- SEUS: 2 walkers (seeds 1, 2), adaptive 30 ns (117775, 2 packed with MPS) → fixed 100 ns via `--freeze-weights` continuation (117776, afterok). Exchange interval 1 ps.
- Analysis: `analysis/pmf_mbar.py` (pymbar 4.2, MBAR on both routes with the same window biases, 0.02 nm bins, error from the first/second-half difference, also checks agreement between window free energies f_k and SEUS's ζ).

Speed (GB200, 4 fs, 14,478 particles, measured): SEUS packed 2 per GPU at 902/908 ns/day each (30 ns = 7.5 M steps in 48 min, ns_per_day in `seus.json`), umbrella packed 8 at 580 ns/day each (5.5 ns in 13.6 min, GPU total 4.6 µs/day), unbiased packed 4 at 930 ns/day each. Going from 2 → 4 packed does not change per-run speed, so at this size the ceiling is per-step latency (0.38 ms/step), not the GPU. A single run cannot be made faster; pack more runs to raise the total. Next time, make a 12 Å buffer and 8 per GPU the default.

A separate issue found along the way: `prepare_complex`'s receipt said `termini: charged termini (no caps)` even though it kept the ACE/NME that came with the input (`_receipt._caps` only looked at caps it applied). Fixed to print input-derived caps as `N ACE / C NME (caps kept from the input)`, pinned in `test_receipt`.

**Interim (17:35)**
- The 23 umbrella windows finished in 13 min. MBAR PMF: minimum 1.19 nm, a plateau of about 2.5 kJ/mol over 0.85–1.15 nm, 13.9 at 0.45 nm, 10.3 kJ/mol at 1.41 nm. The SD over 4 blocks (1.25 ns) is 0.6–0.9 kJ/mol (0.6–1.2 nm) but 1.6 kJ/mol for 0.3–0.6 nm. The 0.45 nm window has a statistical inefficiency of 244 ps and 20 independent samples, and the MBAR overlap of windows 0.40–0.45 is 0.024, so the short-distance side is not converged (backbone transitions of bent structures are slow).
- An interim PMF from running MBAR on (ξ, m) from partway through the SEUS adaptive stage (17 ns each, 6–10 ns into SAMS stage 2) has RMS 0.6–1.7 kJ/mol against umbrella over 0.6–1.5 nm (within umbrella's own block error), and is 2–3 kJ/mol lower over 0.3–0.6 nm. Occupancy is nearly flat at 0.032–0.084, with 5 and 9 end-to-end traversals in 17 ns.
- Two analysis caveats: (1) The correlation time of SEUS's whole ξ series (about 1.3 ns) comes from the random walk over windows, so thinning by it leaves only a few points. MBAR weights do not depend on correlation, so all exchange points are used and the error is judged from the first/second halves. (2) pymbar 4.2's `initialize="BAR"` crashes on sparse data with `BoundsError` → an exception whose `ConvergenceError` is undefined. Worked around by passing umbrella's f_k as `initial_f_k`.
- The ζ convergence criterion is ζ_m = −f_m + const (ζ_m = ln Z_m to even out occupancy). The closed-form F = −kT ln h + kT ln Σ_m exp(−βw_m − ζ_m) is exact only in the fixed stage with ζ fixed (no unknowns). With adaptive-stage data ζ moves, so MBAR is better (using the closed form with the final ζ worsens RMS to 3 kJ/mol).
- At the user's suggestion, added unbiased MD as a negative control: `run_production` 100 ns × 4 replicas from eq_001 (seeds 201–204, output 5 ps, 1 MPS job 117965). In the reachable region (F < 10 kJ/mol), the histogram PMF serves as an independent reference.

**At 30 ns of the fixed stage (18:43), and what the between-walker discrepancy really is**
- The 3 methods agree over 0.6–1.5 nm: SEUS 2 walkers vs umbrella RMS 0.73 / 0.71 kJ/mol, unbiased 162 ns vs umbrella RMS 0.68, SEUS vs unbiased (F < 10) 0.54 / 0.97. The closed form with frozen ζ and MBAR give RMS 0.1 kJ/mol on the same data (supporting that pymbar is unnecessary when ζ is fixed).
- Over 0.45–0.60 nm, walkers 1 and 2 differ by 2 kT. Record consistency is fine (checked collective_variables.csv's `seus_r0` and bias energy against the windows in seus.csv over 16,000 frames, 0 mismatches). The cause is a slow degree of freedom orthogonal to ξ: walker 1 forms the bent structures with residue 1 in α_R (φ < 0, 87 %), walker 2 with residue 1 in α_L (φ > 0, 72 %). Sign flips of Ala's φ are slower than ns and are not averaged out by the per-window residence (about 1 ns in 30 ns). In the same region, umbrella's 0.45 nm window also has a correlation time of 244 ps and 20 independent samples. The "orthogonal slow degrees of freedom" of plan §8 already show up in this toy system. The remedy is extending the fixed stage (100 ns running), and the real fix is combining with SST2.
- At the user's instruction, extended all 23 umbrella windows by 15 ns (continue_from, 118112–118114).

**The 20 ns umbrella version, and a comparison of convergence speed (20:30)**
- Even with umbrella at 20 ns, the first/second-half difference over 0.3–0.6 nm is 2.3 kJ/mol (0.3–0.9 above 0.6 nm). Compared at equal total compute, error × √ns is 26 for umbrella and 8.7 / 18 for SEUS, so SEUS converges 2–9× faster (a single walker's first/second-half difference underestimates when it sits in one basin, so these are upper-side values). The mechanism is φ₁'s α_R/α_L switching: umbrella windows switch 0–13 times in 20 ns, while SEUS walkers flip in extended conformations about 5 times per ns. However, the fraction of the long-lived α_L state is 38 % in umbrella's 0.40 window and 1 % / 25 % for SEUS; no method pins it down.
- The user's conclusion: 0.40–0.50 nm is a region accessible only to strained conformations with the termini pushed in, and should not be handled with a single distance coordinate. Limit the ladder to the reachable range (PMF ≲ 10 kJ/mol, 0.55 nm and above). The final comparison was narrowed to windows at 0.55 nm and above, and this was written into `skills/md-production/seus.md` as a caution on choosing the ladder.

**Next validation systems (user decision 20:20): deca-alanine → p53–MDM2.** As harder examples, proceed in the order (1) the end-to-end distance of ACE-Ala10-NME (cooperative helix ↔ extended transition, with helix nucleation as the orthogonal variable), (3) the centroid-to-centroid distance of peptide–protein dissociation (the real size from plan §6, motivating the combination with SST2). (2) chignolin is on hold. Angle and dihedral CVs are not supported by `run_seus` (a 1–2 hour extension with `CustomCentroidBondForce`'s `angle`/`dihedral`; for dihedrals, wrap the difference into [−π, π]). Deca-alanine is `/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/seus-trials/ala10-e2e` (`launch.sh`): 12 Å buffer, 25 windows from 1.0–3.4 nm in 0.1 nm steps, k = 250 (σ = 0.1 nm), umbrella 25 × 20 ns (MPS 7/7/7/4), SEUS 4 walkers (adaptive 40 ns → fixed 150 ns), unbiased 4 × 200 ns. Full extension is 4.0 nm, so the ladder stops at 3.4 nm (the lesson from 0.4 nm).

**Final results (20:45, all nodes complete).** Compared over windows at 0.55 nm and above (20 windows). Umbrella 20 windows × 20 ns = 400 ns, SEUS fixed stage 100 ns × 2 walkers (38 and 27 end-to-end traversals, occupancy 0.02–0.08), unbiased 4 × 100 ns = 400 ns. `analysis/pmf_from055.{json,png}` (the all-windows version is `pmf_full.*`). PMF: minimum 1.17 nm, a plateau of about 3 kJ/mol over 0.85–1.15 nm, F(0.61) = 7.2, F(1.41) = 9.9 kJ/mol.

| RMS difference kJ/mol (offset aligned over 0.8–1.3 nm) | 0.55–0.9 | 0.9–1.2 | 1.2–1.5 | 0.55–1.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| umbrella first/second half | 1.33 | 0.48 | 0.34 | 0.88 |
| SEUS walker 1 first/second half | 1.73 | 0.29 | 0.68 | 1.14 |
| SEUS walker 2 first/second half | 3.46 | 2.18 | 3.26 | 3.04 |
| walker 1 vs umbrella | 1.90 | 0.45 | 0.48 | 1.22 |
| walker 2 vs umbrella | 1.26 | 0.76 | 1.64 | 1.27 |
| walker 1 vs unbiased (F<10) | 0.97 | 0.30 | 0.32 | 0.67 |
| walker 2 vs unbiased (F<10) | 0.50 | 0.47 | 1.06 | 0.68 |
| umbrella vs unbiased (F<10) | 1.02 | 0.42 | 0.40 | 0.72 |
| walker 1 vs walker 2 | 0.73 | 0.52 | 1.05 | 0.79 |

The unbiased replica SD (F<10) averages 0.97 kJ/mol. Conclusions: (1) `run_seus` agrees with umbrella and unbiased MD within 0.3–0.5 kJ/mol over 0.9–1.5 nm and 1–2 kJ/mol over 0.55–0.9 nm, so the implementation is correct. (2) The closed form with frozen ζ agrees with MBAR at RMS 0.03 kJ/mol (pymbar is for cross-checking). ζ + f_k stays within 1 kT of variation over 100 ns, and ζ from 30 ns of SAMS is accurate to about 1 kT. (3) Walker 2 has a large first/second-half difference of 3 kJ/mol, with only a few entries into and exits from φ₁'s α_L state (25 %) even in the fixed stage. A single walker's first/second-half difference can be too small or too large depending on basin residence, so the error is better judged from the between-walker difference (0.8 kJ/mol). (4) The short-distance side (< 0.55 nm) is not determined by any method (φ₁'s α_R/α_L is a hidden slow variable). Do not put the ladder there. GPU time: umbrella 3 × 0.23 h + extension 3 × 0.6 h + SEUS 0.8 + 2.7 h + unbiased 2.7 h ≈ 9 GPU hours.

## 2026-09-16 — 1KXV SST2 trial run: why the min job died with `singularity: command not found`, and the CLI-side countermeasure

The study `/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/sst2-trials/1kxv-h3` was completed on the login node up through bootstrap → prep_001 chain C 119 residues → solv_001 OPC 80.2 Å → topo_001 ff19SB/OPC/HMR 71,013 atoms. Submitting min_001 to Slurm, it FAILED in 1 second, and the eq and 7 prod jobs in the afterok chain were all cancelled. The job's stderr was `slurm_script: line 14: singularity: command not found`. Cause: submission was done with the `mdclaw` inside the SIF (MDDataBench's prototype wrapper `runs/prep/bin/mdclaw`), and that wrapper does not pass `MDCLAW_SLURM_PATH`. The CLI builds the PATH of the environment passed to sbatch from `MDCLAW_SLURM_PATH` + the system defaults, so when unset it becomes the image-side PATH (`/opt/mdclaw/bin` …), and the generated script calls a bare `singularity` that is not found on the compute node. `skills/hpc-run/sif-slurm.md` instructs `--env MDCLAW_SLURM_PATH="$PATH"`, so this was my own procedural mistake in not calling it as the page says, but it is also a problem that the CLI silently submitted a "job that cannot run". With `export MDCLAW_SLURM_PATH="$PATH"`, resubmitted min_002 (117621, completed in 13 s) → eq_002 (117642) → 6 SST2 walkers in 1 MPS job (117647, `submit_mps_job`, 50 ns blocks, 10 h limit) and md_ref (117648, 100 ns) with afterok.

CLI-side countermeasure (same day, to be committed): added `resolve_container_runtime()` to `mdclaw/slurm/config.py`; before submitting, `submit_job` / `submit_array_job` / `submit_mps_job` resolve the runtime (`singularity` → `apptainer`, or what `configure_container --runtime` specifies) to an absolute path on `MDCLAW_SLURM_PATH` (or PATH if absent) and write it into the sbatch script. Responding to the user's "I'd like to get by without making people set variables", when `MDCLAW_SLURM_PATH` is absent inside the image, it reads the environment of the parent process that launched the container (the launcher) from `/proc/<ppid>/environ` and derives the host PATH automatically (`_base.host_search_path`; the PID namespace is shared, so it is readable). If still not found, it refuses with `container_runtime_not_found`; outside the image, only a warning. However, on RIKYU the parent process's environ could not be read because of the user namespace (the starter's cmdline is readable). The decisive fix is on the compute node side: `/etc/profile.d/apptainer-path.sh` restores PATH, so the start of container sbatch scripts gets a preamble that "reads `/etc/profile` (and module init) if the runtime is not found by `command -v`" (`_container_runtime_preamble`). Job 117688, submitted from inside the image with no variables as `submit_job --script "mdclaw --list"`, COMPLETED on a compute node (9 s). If it cannot be resolved inside the image, it warns rather than refuses; only a `--runtime` set as an absolute path that does not exist gives `container_runtime_not_found`. Tests: 309 pass inside the image, 156 outside. Commit 87f6862. The image with these 2 items (preamble + solvent-contamination guard) baked in is `mdclaw-rikyu-arm64-cuda130-cufft121-sst2-26406c5ca5c3.sif` (sha256 409f0517…6b50, 196 files match HEAD 87f6862). The user placed it in `/data1/$PROJECT` (sha256 match confirmed). The 1KXV study's `.mdclaw_cluster.json` has been switched to this image (the running 117647 / 117648 finish on 0a15ed1cf7d1). For the negative control (ordinary MD at 300 K), in addition to prod_014 (seed 1, 117648, about 820 ns/day alone), seed 2 was added as prod_015 (117769) at the user's suggestion. This submission was made from the new image with no variables, and the generated script was confirmed to contain the `/etc/profile` preamble. At the user's suggestion, also added a solvent-contamination guard to `run_sst2` (`sst2_solute_includes_solvent`: refuses if water, ions, or virtual sites are in the solute; easy to hit because `resid` in the mdtraj DSL is a global index). This time's index file is protein chain 0 only, with no contamination.

## 2026-09-16 — Packing small-system replicas onto 1 GPU with NVIDIA MPS: `submit_mps_job` implementation and GB200 measurements (2.24× with 4, 2.65× with 8)

Following NVIDIA's article "Maximizing OpenMM Molecular Dynamics Throughput with NVIDIA Multi-Process Service" (2025), added `mdclaw submit_mps_job`, which co-locates multiple DAG nodes in a single GPU job (`mdclaw/slurm/mps.py`, `_generate_mps_sbatch_script` in `sbatch.py`). RIKYU's Slurm has only `GresTypes=gpu`, no `gres/mps`, so the job itself starts the MPS control daemon within its `--gpus=1` allocation (a per-job pipe dir under `$TMPDIR`; Apptainer exposes the host `/tmp`, so clients inside the container connect there too; logs in `<job>_<id>.mps/`). `CUDA_MPS_ACTIVE_THREAD_PERCENTAGE = 200/N` (the article's recommendation, clamped to 1–100). Each task is launched simultaneously in the background, round-robin over the GPUs in `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`; the daemon is stopped after `wait` on all of them, and the job fails if any one fails. The N nodes share the same `slurm_job_id` and have a `slurm_mps_slot` and per-slot logs, and `check_job` propagates one job id to all nodes (`_find_records_by_job_id`; completed nodes are not demoted, failed nodes use their own slot's stderr as evidence). Requires an explicit `--platform CUDA` (`mps_task_requires_cuda_platform`); more than 16 per GPU is refused (`mps_tasks_per_gpu_exceeded`). Added 11 tests; 402 tests in the related suites pass. Skills: created `skills/hpc-run/submit-mps.md`, with routing from hpc-run / md-production / md-study (compute-budget) / run-loop saying "replicas of small systems (up to ~100k atoms) are packed with MPS by default". User instruction: run small-system replicas with MPS whenever possible to save GPU time.

Measurements (`/data1/$PROJECT/$USER/runs/mps-bench-20260916`, hen lysozyme 1AKI, ff19SB/OPC, 10 Å, 51,832 atoms, HMR 4 fs, NPT 300 K, 3 ns per replica, 1 GB200, timed from tool_started→tool_completed including container startup):

| Condition | Co-located | Job elapsed | Wall time per replica | Aggregate ns/day/GPU | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alone `submit_job` (117404) | 1 | 4:42 | 277 s | 919 | 1.00 |
| MPS 4 (117405, ATP=50) | 4 | 8:24 | 495–498 s | 2,057 | 2.24 |
| MPS 8 (117407, ATP=25) | 8 | 14:11 | 837–845 s | 2,437 | 2.65 |
| Control: 4 concurrent without MPS (117408) | 4 | 22:28 | 1,341 s | 769 | 0.84 |

Conclusions: (1) At this scale, packing 8 is best, 2.65× over alone and +18 % even over packing 4. Each run is 3× slower, so estimate `--time-limit` as N × time alone / speedup. (2) Concurrent execution without MPS (time slicing) is slower than running alone sequentially (0.84×). Merely "running multiple processes on the same GPU" is counterproductive; the daemon is essential. (3) The 4 jobs total 0.83 GPU-h (≈250 yen). 12 ns of sampling went from 18.8 GPU-minutes → 8.4 GPU-minutes (4 packed), 24 ns from 37.6 → 14.2 GPU-minutes (8 packed). Updated the default in `skills/hpc-run/submit-mps.md` to "8 up to ~50k atoms, 4 up to 100k atoms, 2 for 100k–400k atoms". md-study's budget derivation keeps 1.5× for 4-packed as the planning value (measured 2.24×, expected to drop near 100k atoms).

MLOPart (NVIDIA blog 2025-12; locality domains in MPS v3) is a feature that splits Blackwell's 2 dies into separate CUDA devices to improve memory locality, but it needs driver 590 (x86) / 595 (ARM, CDMM) + CUDA 13.1, and its support table lists only B200/B300. RIKYU is on 580.173, and trying `start_server -mlopart` on the login node silently starts a normal server (no MD sub-devices in `device_query`). After discussing with the user, not implemented; only noted in `docs/developer/roadmap-and-known-issues.md`.

The skill is not site-specific (user instruction: an LLM should be able to extrapolate on other GPUs to decide on MPS submission, and the text should say GB200 rather than RIKYU). `submit-mps.md` consists of a GPU class × atom count decision table (with NVIDIA's H100/L40S/A10 data and today's GB200 measurements as reference points, and an extrapolation rule: double the atoms, halve the co-location count, and step down one level on smaller GPUs), an MPS eligibility check (Volta or later, presence of `nvidia-cuda-mps-control`, compute mode, whole-GPU allocation, `--platform CUDA`), and a calibration procedure for unknown GPUs (compare aggregate ns/day between 2 short jobs, 1 alone vs 4 packed, and pack if it is 1.3× or more).

## 2026-09-16 — Revising the SST2/SEUS plan: 5 points found by inspecting the SST2 code in practice

Checked the SST2-based expanded-ensemble plan written by Opus against a clone of SST2 commit `31c76a4`, and revised it as `docs/research/sst2-seus-plan.md`. Findings that overturn the plan's premises: (1) `REST2` builds the solute / solvent sub-Systems with `forcefield.createSystem()`, so `app.ForceField` is required. This does not fit MDClaw's `system.xml` contract, and a sub-System builder based on System copying is needed. (2) With Amber-family force fields, 1-4 exceptions crossing the boundary are not scaled, while the decomposition treats them as √λ terms, so with a partial solute the acceptance energy is self-inconsistent at λ≠1. All upstream tests use whole chains as the solute, so this path is unverified. (3) The acceptance loop (shuffles 2 adjacent candidates and tests them in order with a single random number) does not satisfy detailed balance. Replace it with Gibbs sampling over all rungs. (4) The CLI flag is `-select`, and the console script points to a nonexistent `SST2.__main__`. (5) The Abl–abltide umbrella PMF that the plan used as its reference does not exist (confirmed by the user), so the SEUS reference is built with the existing umbrella route + pymbar. Since SEUS does not use REST2's decomposition, the policy changed to writing it on the MDClaw side under MIT, and corrected that the converged weights are window free energies, not a PMF, so the PMF comes from pymbar. Checked the boundary-term convention in the gREST paper (Eq. (3)): λ^(k/l), with l = 2 for bonds/LJ/Coulomb, 3 for angles, 4 for dihedrals, 8 for CMAP. SST2's dihedral k/4 and CMAP k/8 match, and boundary 1-4 at √λ is the same as the fix above. SST2 leaving bonds, angles, and impropers unscaled differs from gREST, so align `param_type` for GENESIS comparisons. The effort grows from 6–10 weeks to 7–11 weeks.

## 2026-09-15 — glm-5.3-flash full campaign launched beside kimi-k3 v4 (10:54 JST)

`runs/glm-5.3-flash-skill-full`: 98 tasks x cli_skill_sif x 3 replicates = 294 attempts on dataset v0.4, spec `runs/prep/experiment-glm-5.3-flash-skill-full.json` (copied from the v4 kimi-k3 spec: same image 6ecc1ad9, 1800 s budget, same task order; one cell, model `rikyu/glm-5.3-flash`, thinking high, skill_source user). Launched with `launch.sh` at `--max-agents 3 --max-seconds-per-call 30` because kimi-k3 v4 (6 agents, dispatcher 609351, 12.4 h in) shares the login node, whose load from other users was 120-135 at launch; pi checkout 17283b6, harness fdf9770. Dispatcher pid 3881654. Expected about a day at the pilot's pace (9.4 s/call, 4-11 min per attempt); monitor every 30 min with `campaign_status.py` and `sweep_dead_jobs.py --cancel`. First failure (11:54 JST status, 12 sealed / 11 passed): 002_membrane_5zk3 r1 timed out with `agent_no_submission` after 23 calls. The agent ran `embed_in_membrane --lipids DPPC --dist 10.0 --dist-wat 10.0 --water-model tip3p --salt --saltcon 0.15`; `dist_wat` is part of the patch-cache fingerprint (`patch_membrane.py::membrane_patch_fingerprint`), the image bundles DPPC/TIP3P only at the default 17.5, so the call logged `patch-tile: no cached membrane patch for lipids=DPPC ratio=1; building it once now` and spent the remaining 25 minutes equilibrating a lipid patch with OpenMM on the login-node CPU (heartbeats to 1460 s, `solv_001` left `running`, empty cache entry `~/.cache/mdclaw/membrane_patches/f6/`). The skill page `md-prepare/membrane.md` shows `--dist 15.0 --dist-wat 17.5` and says to keep `dist_wat` unchanged; every other membrane attempt so far (18 of 19, all 17.5) hit the cache and passed, so this is one model deviation, not a rerun candidate. Fix candidate recorded in `roadmap-and-known-issues.md`: an uncached patch build on a CPU-only host should be refused (or need an explicit flag) instead of running for half an hour on a shared login node. Second failure, 010_membrane_6kux r3 (13:25 status, 39 sealed / 37 passed): the agent passed `--membrane-backend packmol-memgen` (the legacy full-box packing; r1 and r2 used the default patch-tile and embedded in about 70 s), the call hit pi's 1500 s command timeout, and the agent then wrote and detached a `continue_attempt.py` under `$TMPDIR` that kept driving the DAG (a second embed on `solv_002`) after the attempt was sealed at 1786 s. At 13:35 JST the sealed attempt still owned a process tree on the login node: bash -> python3 continue_attempt.py -> apptainer starter -> mdclaw embed -> two packmol-memgen -> two `packmol` at 100 % CPU each for 26 minutes. Killed by PID (2454457 2454458 2677263 2677452 2677701 2713677 2713680 2731591 2732062) after verifying each command line named the r3 attempt; a one-pass scan found no other sealed attempt with live processes. Two fix candidates recorded: the harness must kill the agent's whole session/process group at timeout (a detached script survived), and a CPU-only host should refuse or warn on `--membrane-backend packmol-memgen`, which the skill never suggests. Known open defect carried into the run: the prep receipt hides `covalently_linked_glycan_chains_auto_included` (pilot 069), so the four glycan tasks (019, 020, 022, 069) may fail on it unless the agent passes `--include-types protein`; those attempts are rerun candidates once the receipt is fixed, not evidence about the model.

Final at 23:16 JST: **6 of 7 passed**. 015_antibody_1ahw PASS 20/20 (671 s, 41 calls, 16.1 s/call, 16 reads; the 413k-atom cell that timed out for qwen and passed 0 of 3 in kimi-k3 v2), 023_antibody_3wd5 PASS 20/20 (682 s, 45 calls, 15.0 s/call, 20 reads; standard protonation kept), 051_nucleic_1kx5 PASS 20/20 (648 s, 46 calls, 14.0 s/call, 18 reads; the v0.4 CL+MN sentence followed). Overall pace 9.7 s/call median (kimi-k3 v2: 21.7), no timeout, no gateway reset, every attempt read 14-18 skill files. The only failure, 069, is the receipt defect below. Recommendation: glm-5.3-flash goes first for the full 98 x 3 cli_skill_sif campaign on v0.4; at 6 agents it needs about 12 h, at 3 agents (beside kimi-k3 v4 on the loaded login node) about a day.

The 069 failure is the CLI's, not the model's. The agent planned "exclude glycan NAG chains B/C at ASN 12/168, exclude ZN" from the prompt, reasoned that label chain A holds the protein only, and ran `prepare_complex --select-chains A --protonation-method standard --solvent-type explicit`. `split` then applied `covalently_linked_glycan_chains_auto_included` (14 NAG on two chains), but the envelope `message` and `applied.summary` said "prepared: 1 protein chain(s) A (228 residues), 0 ligands, 6 disulfide(s), 3,484 atoms", `warnings_count` was 1 (the ASN168 HD21 - NAG B237 C1 close contact, the only trace of a sugar), `applied.options.select_chains` was `not_reported`, and the adjustment sits only in `result.json` under `split.selection_adjustments` and `applied.facts.glycans`. The agent's stage report said "glycan excluded" on the strength of the summary, and the scorer saw [3, 1, 155, 1, 68, 1, 1] backbone components (the same signature as kimi-k3's 069 failure in v2). qwen's passing 069 attempt saw the code only because it dumped the whole JSON with `2>&1` and re-ran with `--include-types protein` (3,456 atoms). Fix for mdclaw: a selection adjustment that changes composition must reach `message`/`applied.summary` ("2 glycan chain(s) auto-included: NAG x14; pass --include-types protein to leave them out") and `warnings`, and `select_chains` must not be `not_reported`. kimi-k3 avoids it by always passing `--include-types protein`.
