## 2026-08-20 — Missing residues were invisible inside prepare_complex; gaps are now repairable in place

Two problems, one fix. Started from the MODELLER ordering trap (fetching a
template completes the job's only `source` node, and a completed node is sealed,
so `modeller_from_alignment` cannot then write to it). Every CLI structure-
acquisition tool is `@node_tool("source")` — verified by running
`fetch_structure --output-dir` and getting `code=node_context_required` — so
inside one job there is no correct order to document. The workaround used for
9UWI left `studies/9uwi-popc` with three registered jobs (`main`, `modelled`,
`modelled2`) of which two hold nothing but a source node, and with `main` and
`modelled` recording `job_dir` against different path roots.

**The bigger finding: `prepare_complex` could not see missing residues at all.**
`split_molecules` builds each chain as a fresh `gemmi.Structure()` holding only
the modeled residues, so SEQRES stayed behind in the parent. PDBFixer finds
gaps by comparing coordinates to that reference; with none it reports zero.
Measured on 4AKE:

    source candidate (candidate_001.cif):  SEQRES chains=2   <- reference present
    split chain file (protein_1.pdb):      SEQRES chains=0   <- gone

So `pdbfixer_missing_residues_out_of_scope` could never fire from the
`prepare_complex` path, and internal gaps entered MD as silent chain breaks.
All three studies confirm it: `missing_residue_repair` was `None` on every prep
node of 4ake-apo-trial, 5l7d-popc and 9uwi-popc.

### What changed

`_carry_reference_sequence` (`mdclaw/structure/split.py`) copies the owning
entity's `full_sequence` onto the extracted chain. The recipe matters:
`setup_entities()` on the *new* structure first (gemmi writes SEQRES from an
entity whose subchains match the chain being written), then fill the empty
`full_sequence` it produced. Attaching the parent entity directly writes no
SEQRES at all — tried it, got 0 lines.

`missing_residue_method` on `clean_protein` and `prepare_complex`, default
`pdbfixer`, alternative `modeller`. With `modeller` the gaps are rebuilt before
PDBFixer runs, in the same prep node: the chain is its own template and its own
SEQRES is the target, so no template file, no target sequence, and no second
source node are involved. The DAG stays `source_001 -> prep_001 -> ...`, one
job, and `NodeSealedError` never appears.

Deliberately not done: no automatic escalation and no upper ceiling. Rebuilding
a 33-residue ICL3 is a scientific judgement, so it happens only behind an
explicit flag.

### Impact on existing studies, measured before shipping

    4ake  SEQRES=214  internal=0   -> unchanged
    5l7d  SEQRES=638  internal=0   -> unchanged
    9uwi  SEQRES=386  internal=40 in 3 segments, max 33, terminal 77
                                  -> now OUT_OF_SCOPE (was silent)

One of three studies changes behaviour, and it is the one that actually needed
MODELLER. 5L7D turned out to have no internal gaps — worth recording, since I
had assumed a cryo-EM GPCR would.

### Verified end to end on 9UWI chain A

Default path stops with the code unchanged (`pdbfixer_missing_residues_out_of_scope`
is a public contract) but the first recommended option is now
`repair_in_place_with_modeller` carrying `--missing-residue-method modeller`,
where it used to say "regenerate the source" and point straight at the two-job
trap. MODELLER path: 40 residues rebuilt in 3 segments, longest 33, seed -8123.

Residue numbering survives: all 269 observed residues keep both number and name,
model 309 residues total. The first attempt produced 386 — the whole SEQRES,
including a fabricated 67-residue C-terminal tail — because the full reference
sequence was handed to MODELLER. Fixed by modeling only the span between the
first and last observed residue, so unresolved termini are left alone exactly as
the terminal filter intended.

One bug found by running it end to end rather than at unit level: detection
originally ran on the post-repair file, which is a MODELLER model with no
SEQRES, so the node reported `status="not_detectable"` for chain A directly
under a line saying 40 residues had just been rebuilt. Detection now describes
the structure as it was before repair (SEQRES 386, modeled 269, terminal
excluded 77).

### Also now reported

A chain with no reference sequence reports `status="not_detectable"` rather than
zero gaps — "not checked" and "none present" were indistinguishable before.
Terminal segments excluded from repair are reported with segment *and* residue
counts (9UWI: 2 segments, 77 residues); the old message counted segments while
saying "residue(s)". The MODELLER random seed and the template's sha256 go on
the node, because a loop that cannot be reproduced makes the whole study
irreproducible. In a multi-chain structure each repair is tagged
`interface_context: chain_isolated`, since chains are repaired from separate
files and an interface loop never sees its partner.

`tests/test_missing_residue_handling.py` builds its inputs with gemmi rather
than downloading them, so it runs on a compute node with no network. The
two-chain fixture uses deliberately different sequences and lengths per chain: a
chain-to-entity mix-up survives a same-length check, and 4AKE and 5L7D both have
identical chains, so neither would catch it.

Not in the shared SIF. Members run the container's own mdclaw.

## 2026-08-20 — MODELLER now converts an mmCIF template instead of renaming it

Fixes trap 2 from the 9UWI entry below. `modeller_from_alignment` staged the
template into MODELLER's working directory with `shutil.copy2(template_path,
out_dir / f"{code}.pdb")` — extension change only. MODELLER picks its reader
from the file's contents, not its name, so an mmCIF under a `.pdb` name is not
degraded, it is unreadable: `read_pd_702E> ... file is probably corrupt` on the
first CIF line.

New `_stage_template_as_pdb` copies a PDB source and converts an mmCIF one via
gemmi (`make_structure_from_block` → `setup_entities` → `write_pdb`). The
conversion is reported as a warning, because PDB cannot hold everything mmCIF
can — residue names longer than three characters, more chains than single
letters. Failures return structured codes rather than a corrupt file:
`modeller_template_conversion_unavailable` (no gemmi) and
`modeller_template_conversion_failed` (unparsable input).

Verified against the file that produced the original failure: the full
`9UWI.cif` (562 residues, Atosiban included) passed straight to `--template-pdb`
with the 269-residue chain-A sequence now builds a model —
`selection_reason: lowest_dope_score`, DOPE -37149, CA RMSD after fit 0.748 Å —
where before it died in MODELLER's PDB parser. The staged `9UWI.pdb` contains
no `_atom_site.` or `loop_` lines. `tests/test_modeller_template_staging.py`
covers copy, conversion, the `.mmcif` suffix, and the unparsable case; 204 tests
and ruff pass.

The chain-A workaround written by hand for that run
(`studies/9uwi-popc/templates/9UWI_A.pdb`) is no longer needed for format
reasons. It is still the right input when the template should exclude the other
chains and the ligand — the tool converts the file it is given, it does not
subset it.

## 2026-08-20 — 9UWI chain A through MODELLER into POPC; three traps on the way

Second member target, and the first real exercise of the MODELLER path baked
into the SIF: 9UWI (human V1a receptor, cryo-EM 2.8 A), chain A only, Atosiban
and the cholesterols dropped, the three internal gaps rebuilt, POPC bilayer,
1 ns production. It works, and the run found three things worth fixing.

**The gaps.** Chain A is observed 43-351 (269 residues) against a 386-residue
SEQRES, with internal gaps 80-84 (3), 157-162 (4) and 247-281 (**33**, ICL3).
Author numbering is offset -32 from SEQRES, so the target sequence has to be
built by aligning observed residues rather than slicing SEQRES by author number
(269/269 match at that offset). The 33-residue gap is above the default
`--loop-max-length 30`, so it needs raising or ICL3 stays unrefined — the skill
does warn about this. Target span 43-351 only: modelling the unobserved 1-42 and
352-386 would invent 77 residues of terminus flapping in solvent.

Result: 4 loop models, best by DOPE (-3226, molpdf 213), 309 residues, **no gaps
left**. `--template-frame` reported `ca_rmsd_in_place: 13.552` / `after_fit:
0.823`, but measuring it directly over the 269 common CA gives mean deviation
0.28 A and a centroid shift of 3.5 A — the model *is* in the template frame.
Whatever the reported 13.55 is measuring, it is not the in-place deviation an
agent would read it as. Worth a look.

**Trap 1: the skill never says when to run MODELLER relative to
`fetch_structure`.** Node mode writes into the source bundle, so the source node
must still be open — but `fetch_structure` completes it, and loop refinement
needs a template structure, which is exactly what you would use `fetch_structure`
to get. Running MODELLER after it gives `NodeSealedError`.
`skills/modeller-predict/` does not mention `fetch_structure` anywhere. Worked
around by fetching in one job and running MODELLER on a fresh source node in a
second job registered with `add_study_job`.

**Trap 2: `--template-pdb` accepts an mmCIF and does not convert it.** The file
is copied to `<code>.pdb` and handed to MODELLER as-is, which then fails with
`read_pd_702E> ... file is probably corrupt` at the first CIF line it cannot
parse as PDB. Converting to a real PDB first fixed it. Restricting the template
to chain A also dropped Atosiban's `A1EQM`, whose 5-character residue name has
no PDB representation.

**Trap 3: a protonated aspartate renamed lipids, and nothing said it was
there.** Two aspartates (97, 112) came back protonated, but
`confirmation_needed.protonation_states` was `{"source": "auto_detected",
"states": []}` — empty. `embed_in_membrane` then failed at the net-charge step:

    No template found for residue 399 (ASH). The set of atoms matches PA, but
    the residue has no bonds between its atoms.

`--protonation-states '{"A:97": "ASP", "A:112": "ASP"}'` gets past it. 5L7D never
hit this, so it is structure-dependent — any member whose receptor has a buried
Asp will.

**First correction: ff19SB does have an ASH template**, so "no template found"
is not about the force field lacking one. OpenMM matches templates by atom
composition, not by name.

**Second correction — the loader was not at fault either.** `pdbNames.xml`
registers `ASH` as an alias of `ASP` (and `HID`/`HIE`/`HIP` of `HIS`), so
`openmm.app.PDBFile` normalises it and bonds fine; measured on a synthetic
ALA-ASH-ALA, `ASH` loads as `ASP` with 14 bonds whether written as ATOM or
HETATM. `LYN` and `CYM` have no alias and are the ones that would load bare.
So a residue arriving at template matching still *named* `ASH` never went
through that normalisation — which points at MDClaw's own code.

**The actual cause is in `mdclaw/amber/openmm_build.py`.** The topology path
deliberately rewrites ASH/GLH/LYN/CYM to their CCD names so Pablo can identify
them, then restores the Amber names on the loaded topology. The histidine
restore guards on `residue.name != "HIS"`; the variant restore had no such
guard and renamed on `(chain, residue number)` alone. **That key is not unique
in an assembled membrane.** In this system chain A carries both the protein
`ASP` 97/112 and POPC `PA` residues numbered 97 and 112, so lipid tails were
renamed to `ASH`. The force field's "no template for residue 399 (ASH), the set
of atoms matches PA" was reporting precisely that: a PA residue wearing the
name ASH.

Two defects, then, and neither is the force field or OpenMM:

1. **Restore.** Fixed: `_restore_amber_variant_names` now checks the recorded
   chain and that the residue still carries the base name that was substituted,
   before renaming it back. Extracted to a module-level helper with tests in
   `tests/test_amber_variant_restore.py` covering the lipid, water and ion
   collisions and all four variants. Verified on the failing system: the same
   prep that produced `membrane_neutralization_failed` now embeds cleanly with
   both aspartates kept as ASH and the lipids untouched.
2. **Reporting.** `confirmation_needed.protonation_states` only ever carried
   caller-supplied overrides, never what pdb2pqr assigned — while
   `histidine_states` reads the produced structure. Fixed: added
   `_extract_non_default_protonation_states` and `_merge_protonation_states`,
   wired into all three recording sites in `clean_protein.py` and into the
   operation records the summary aggregates from. Reported names are kept in
   step with what the topology path can round-trip (ASH/GLH/LYN/CYM; ff19SB has
   no TYM or ARN template, so promising them would promise an unbuildable
   system). The failing 9UWI prep now reports both aspartates with the state
   they replaced.

The workaround used during the run — forcing the aspartates back to ASP — was
therefore treating a symptom. It is no longer needed.

**The run.** Orientation came from OPM homolog **7QVM** (identity 0.60, fit_rmsd
2.29 A, hydrophobic thickness 31.8 A), not from 9UWI itself — so unlike 5L7D
this exercised the homolog transfer rather than an exact self-match. Box
116 x 77 x 104 A, rectangular in the membrane plane rather than square, but the
receptor keeps ~18 A of lipid to its periodic image against the 15 A requested.
`min` 21 s, `eq` (1.5 ns) 3 m 48 s, `prod` (1 ns) 2 m 51 s. Production held
300.99 +/- 1.03 K and 1.032 +/- 0.002 g/mL over 100 frames.

Final DAG: 8 completed, 1 failed (`solv_001`, the ASH failure, kept as evidence).

## 2026-08-20 — 5L7D in POPC end to end on Rikyu; the membrane fixes hold, and one analyze trap

Ran the v0.6.8 SIF through a real membrane system to check the fixes before
telling the group to pull: 5L7D (human Smoothened, a class F GPCR with a BRIL
fusion), chain A only, ligand CLR and the NAG glycans dropped, POPC bilayer,
0.5 ns NVT + 1.0 ns NPT, 1 ns production. Nine nodes, **0 failed**.

**The membrane fixes hold.**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Orientation backend | `opm-homolog`. 5L7D is itself in OPM, so identity 1.0, `fit_rmsd` 0.0, hydrophobic thickness 32 A, 10 candidates evaluated. No PPM3 fallback. |
| Ions in the bilayer | 301 ions, **0** within the middle 80 % of the lipid z-span. This is the `a6cad27` fix (patch salt no longer carried into the assembly) working on a real system. |
| Lipid headgroup restraint | `lipid_headgroup_restraint_count: 359` on both `min` and `eq` — the new flat-bottom restraint is applied. |
| Box fitted to solute | 116 x 116 x 173.5 A. The extracellular CRD sets the z height; nothing crosses the cell after NPT contracted it 10 %. |
| Equilibration | Density 0.917 -> 1.024 g/mL, volume 2416 -> 2164 nm3. |
| Production | 300.34 +/- 0.68 K, 1.025 +/- 0.001 g/mL, backbone RMSD rising to ~0.15 nm and flat after 40 frames. |

**Throughput:** ~300,000 atoms, one GB200. `min` 32 s, `eq` (1.5 ns) 7 m 58 s,
`prod` (1 ns) 6 m 09 s — about **270 ns/day**. The whole run cost ~15 min of GPU.

**The trap: `explain_node` says an analyze node is ready when its metric tool is
not.** Create an `analyze` node parented on `prod`, and `explain_node` reports
`ready_to_run: true`, no blocking codes, no missing inputs, and resolves
`topology_file` / `trajectory_chain` / `energy_chain`. Running `analyze_rmsd` on
that node then fails:

    Validation failed for 'trajectory_file / reference_pdb': Both are required.

The resolver exposes `trajectory_chain` (a list) and `topology_file`; the metric
wants `trajectory_file` and `reference_pdb`, which only exist after
`concat_trajectory` has run on that node and written `combined_trajectory` +
`reference_pdb`. `skills/md-analyze/metrics.md` states this ("After
`concat_trajectory` ... the combined trajectory and reference PDB are the common
inputs"), so an agent that reads the skill is fine. An agent that trusts
`explain_node` — which is what `run-loop.md` says to check before running a
stage tool — is not. Reproduced cleanly on a fresh node (`analyze_003`).

Either `explain_node` should report the concat prerequisite for metric-bearing
analyze nodes, or the metrics should accept the chain form the resolver already
hands them. Not fixed here.

**Not a finding, for the record:** `analyze_rmsd` does return its statistics —
`mean_rmsd_nm`, `std_rmsd_nm`, `max_rmsd_nm`, `n_frames` as flat keys. An
earlier read of this session looked for a `statistics` object that the tool
never promised.

## 2026-08-20 — The cause of the 21 failures in the full suite was the OpenCL driver's setlocale

21 tests that "pass when run alone and fail in a full run". **Not flaky but a real bug**, and there was
a single cause.

### How it was pinned down

`read_text()` was failing in the ASCII decoder, so the locale was suspected, but no matter how the environment variables were changed,
Python 3.12 forces the C locale to UTF-8, so it did not reproduce. Tracing the test modules' imports
one at a time did not knock it over either. **Collecting all files + running just 1 test did not reproduce it, but executing the tests did**,
so it was narrowed to "during the execution of some test", shrunk to 5 files reproducing in 22 seconds, and a binary search
reached `test_ap5_build_topology_smoke.py::test_step4_topology_via_gaff`.

Hooking all of Python's `locale.setlocale` / `ctypes.CDLL` / `subprocess.Popen` did not detect it
(because it went through a C-level dlopen); the moment was caught by **a sampler thread that reads LC_CTYPE every 2 ms and dumps
the main thread's stack**.

```
build_amber_system -> openmm_build.py:1555 Simulation(...) -> mm.Context(...)
-> no platform specified, so OpenCL is chosen
-> Apple's OpenCL driver initialization calls setlocale(LC_ALL, "C")
-> the process's default encoding gets pinned to US-ASCII
-> from then on all text I/O without an explicit encoding is ASCII, and dies on an em dash (U+2014)
```

### Not just a test problem

The 4 `render_structure_preview` failures were **MDClaw being unable to write its own output**, dying with `UnicodeEncodeError`.
Measured inside the Linux arm64 image:

| Environment | `utf8_mode` | After the driver sets LC_ALL=C | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| LANG unset (container default) | 1 | stays utf-8 | no effect |
| LANG=en_US.UTF-8 | 1 | stays utf-8 | no effect |
| **LANG=C.UTF-8** | **0** | **ANSI_X3.4-1968** | **UnicodeEncodeError** |

`LANG=C.UTF-8` is commonly set on HPC. **It is not macOS-specific.**

### Fix

Added `preserve_locale()` and `new_simulation()` to `_common.py`, and routed all 12 places where MDClaw creates a Simulation
through them. The driver still knocks the locale over, but it does not persist in the process. The bash 3.2 problem in `bin/mdclaw`
(empty-array expansion under `set -u`) was also fixed as a separate item.

`tests/test_locale_guard.py` checks restoration and restoration on exceptions, and in addition checks at the source level **that nothing outside `_common.py` calls `Simulation(`
directly** (the guard only means something once every call site uses it).
Confirmed that reverting one call site makes it fail.

```
before  21 failed, 1454 passed
after   1478 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed
```

Putting `PYTHONUTF8=1` into the image would also structurally eliminate the 3rd row of the table, but this has not been done.

## 2026-08-20 — Fixed the CLI not starting in a read-only CWD. SIF rebuilt. The existing 21 failures depend on the locale

### The actual fix

The 28 modules that declare `WORKING_DIR` called `ensure_directory(WORKING_DIR)` right next to it **at import time**.
`_cli._discover_tools()` imports every module, so **even a do-nothing
`--version` / `--list` digs `outputs/` into the CWD, and if it cannot, the CLI itself does not start**.
Every write site already calls `ensure_directory` / `create_unique_subdir` / `mkdir(parents=True)`,
so the import-time calls were never needed in the first place. Deleted all 28, along with imports that became
unnecessary. Added 2 regression tests to `TestSubprocessCLI`.

### Recording one mistake of my own

To check that the regression test was effective, I temporarily put the bug back into `pdb_client.py` and reverted it with `git checkout`.
**That restores from the index, so it rolled back not only the line added for the experiment but the fix as well.**
As a result I committed a state where only 27/28 were fixed, and baked and handed over a SIF in that state. Further, in the full suite
I misdiagnosed my own 2 failing regression tests as "flaky because I touched git during the tests".
**The tests were right; I was the one who misread them.** Two lessons: to roll back an experiment, use `git stash` / `git diff > patch`,
not `git checkout <file>`. If you judge a failing test to be flaky, the basis must be
identifying the cause, not "it passed on rerun".

### The existing 21 failures are unrelated to my changes; the cause is locale-dependent `read_text()`

Ran the same full suite in a worktree of the pre-fix commit `2daf6e4` and confirmed **the failure sets match exactly**
(pre-fix 21 failed / 1452 passed, post-fix 21 failed / 1454 passed;
the difference is the 2 added regression tests).

The cause is reading files in the repository with `read_text()` **without passing `encoding=`**.

```
claude = (REPO_ROOT / "CLAUDE.md").read_text()
  -> encodings.ascii.IncrementalDecoder ... UnicodeDecodeError
```

It depends on the process's locale at that moment, so it passes when run alone, while in a full run the locale gets knocked over to
C partway through and it fails on files containing Japanese. It is the kind that **always fails in containers / HPC batch
where the C locale is the default**, not flaky. Not fixed.

### Separate issue: `bin/mdclaw` does not work on bash 3.2

`tests/test_bin_wrapper.py::test_wrapper_is_quiet_outside_a_user_namespace`:

```
bin/mdclaw: line 146: NV[@]: unbound variable
```

The empty-array expansion `"${NV[@]}"` under `set -u` passes on bash 4.4+ but is an error on bash 3.2 (the macOS default).
`"${NV[@]+"${NV[@]}"}"` would fix it. Not fixed yet.

### Artifacts

```

```

Confirmed startup from a read-only CWD in practice (inside the SIF, with a 0555 directory as `--pwd`,

`...-34230ff20567.sif`; it is the version missing one file of the fix** (under the same conditions it

```

sif     ~/Downloads/mdclaw-rikyu-arm64-cuda130-ppm3-a6cad2701ac4.sif

        SHA-256 098df878a4593ecbd1a0c68e89d662402b566ac567e1182632fd0779adff8d72
smoke   Docker 23/23, also 23/23 from the SIF (GPU SKIPped)
```

As before, not pushed to GHCR; the tar from `docker save` was read into the Lima VM and converted.

### `mdclaw --version` fails in a read-only CWD

While validating the SIF, I ran `mdclaw --version` from a read-only directory and it died.

```
File "mdclaw/research/pdb_client.py", line 22, in <module>
    ensure_directory(WORKING_DIR)
OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system: 'outputs'
```

`WORKING_DIR = Path("outputs")` is hardcoded in more than 20 modules, and every one of them
calls `ensure_directory(WORKING_DIR)` **at import time**. `_cli._discover_tools()` imports every
module, so **even `--version` or `--list` digs `outputs/` into the CWD**.
If it cannot, the CLI itself does not start.

`test-container.sh` is green because it first does `cd "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"` to move somewhere writable.
That is, the existing smoke test never exercises this path. On HPC, running it from a read-only bind or a directory
without write permission fails before a single tool runs. As a side effect, merely touching the CLI in an unrelated
directory sprouts an empty `outputs/`.

Not fixed. The right approach is to remove the import-time side effect and create the directory when it is needed (this also ties in with
making the default WORKING_DIR `.`).

## 2026-08-20 — Stopped carrying in the patch's salt. It was the cause of every ion-neutralization branch

In the review of the previous day's membrane-build fix, a defect in `_drop_counter_ions` was pointed out, and before fixing it
I measured the patches' ions, at which point the premise fell apart.

### Measurement

Each of the 7 bundled patches has only **8 ions (Na 4 / Cl 4)**.
Taking each patch's midplane with `_estimate_patch_membrane_center_z` and measuring z with the minimum image
gives:

```
POPC            core(|dz|<15): 0   headgroup(15-25): 6   bulk(>25): 2
DOPC / DPPC                  : 0                    : 3            : 5
POPE / POPC:CHL1             : 0                    : 0            : 8
```

**There is not a single ion in the hydrophobic core.** The POPC patch's lipid tails extend to |dz| <= 19.1,
and the PC headgroups span |dz| 10.2..27.9. The 8 ions are at dz = -26.95, -27.19, +23.55, +18.47 (Na)
and -15.67, -20.98, +20.00, +19.13 (Cl).

The deletion condition is `|z - centre| <= leaflet` with leaflet = 23, so 5 of the 8 (Na 1 / Cl 4)
are removed. 45 over 9 tiles, a species difference of 27 — exactly matching the runtime warning
"dropped 45 ion(s) ... and 27 counter-ion(s)". The code comment said
"ions ... end up in the hydrophobic core of every copy", but **it was the headgroup interface,
not the core**.

### The current code was already effectively "strip everything"

45 + 27 = 72 = 8 x 9: the 2-stage deletion was removing all of the patch's ions.
With `existing_cations: 0, existing_anions: 0`, neutralization placed the full amount (149 Na / 152 Cl).
Not by design, but an arithmetic coincidence of this patch's composition.

### Decision: patches are equilibrated with salt, and stripped before use

The same flow as VMD (the `membrane` plugin's patches have no ions + `autoionize` replaces water) and
CHARMM-GUI (build the bilayer and water, then place ions in the aqueous phase). MDClaw's
`_apply_neutralizing_swap` also already swaps with bulk water outside the leaflet, so
the final placement used the same scheme all along. The only difference was that the patch carried salt in.

Branches that disappeared:

| Removed processing | Reason |
|---|---|
| Deleting buried ions | The patch has no ions |
| `_drop_counter_ions` | No species imbalance arises |
| `pairs_present` branch | `existing = 0` is an invariant |
| Excess branch | Unreachable |

The excess branch did real harm. The docstring of `plan_neutralizing_ions` states explicitly
"never a negative number — ions that are already there are not removed to hit a
target from above", and in measurement, 150 pairs present / 87 target gives
0.258 M, and 300 pairs gives 0.515 M, **shipped without a warning**. Stripping makes it unreachable.

Validated on a real system (SMO 5L7D / POPC): existing 0/0, 149 Na / 152 Cl, net +3,
water 55,026, salt 0.1503 M, geometry passed, density 0.957 of bulk — identical to before stripping.

### Disagreement with the review

cursor opposed stripping everything, arguing "keep the equilibrated ions at the interface and remove the excess in pairs".
The reason: "MDClaw's final placement is a deterministic bulk-water substitution, not CHARMM-GUI's
electrostatics-aware MC, so throwing away an equilibrated interfacial distribution is a regression".

Why it was not adopted: what would be kept is **the 8 coordinates duplicated as-is across 9 tiles**,
an artificial periodicity rather than a distribution produced by equilibration. 72 of the final system's 301 ions
would be that. Artificial periodicity from tiling is also a known issue already recorded separately.

However, **for charged lipids cursor's argument holds**. With POPG/POPS/POPA, counter-ions aggregate at the headgroups,
in larger amounts, and that is real chemistry. When actually making patches with charged lipids,
revisit this decision. At present such patches do not exist and it cannot be validated.

### Fixed at the same time (review findings)

- Imaging contact detection changed from the molecular centroid to the **nearest atom**. The screen is also based on molecular size.
  cursor's reproduction case (20 nm box, a chain touching the anchor at 0.2 nm while extending 12 nm) goes
  3.0 nm -> 0.0 nm
- **xy column check** in the density gate (10 A squares, below 0.35 of bulk, penetrating 80% or more along z).
  Its effective range is bounded from both sides: a channel with a 25% cross-section is already caught by the slab check at 0.729,
  and below 8% (about 35 A diameter in a 112 A box) neither lets it through. It is responsible for the range in between
- Emit a warning when density cannot be evaluated (previously it silently went through as passed)
- Limit the preview's `connect_mode 3` to files where hybrid-36 actually occurs
- system_box for large systems (>= 150k atoms) drops shadows and antialiasing.
  **264 s -> 65 s** (timeout 300 s). `ray=False` is not an option because it produces no PNG when headless

### Added syntax validation of the generated PyMOL script

`json.dumps(True)` returns JSON's `true`, so embedding it into generated Python is a syntax error.
Hit this twice in this session (`axis_views`, `fast_ray`). The second time it had **completely disabled** the
`connect_mode` conditional, and I only noticed when rendering failed after 3 seconds.
Added a test that validates all 24 flag combinations with `ast.parse`.


## 2026-08-19 — Unified the test on the ANM null, found Rg's role, measured 3 replicas, discovered a BLAS bug in the SIF

**Narrowed the test down to one (user instruction "better to narrow it to either H0 or ANM").** The ANM null (27 points at cutoff 7.0-20.0 A,
mean 0.517 SD 0.048 max 0.588) subsumes the random null: something at 0.13 cannot exceed 0.59.
Measured z is: real 1 ns +4.37 / 100 ps +2.26 / 10 ps -2.00 / ANM ensemble -0.05 (dead center of the null) /
isotropic noise -8.00. The random null was removed from the gate and demoted to reporting context. All 5 negative controls fail; only the real run passes.

**Rg was not redundant.** Checking "isn't Rg meaningless?" by measurement led to the opposite conclusion.
**RMSIP is scale-invariant**, so scaling the trajectory uniformly by 1.3× leaves RMSIP unchanged at 0.729 (Rg goes 1.14 -> 1.48).
Likewise for 0.8×. Even with progressive swelling (Rg 1.82), RMSIP is 0.711 and still passes. **Rg is the only check that constrains
amplitude and compactness**, and it alone has the job of catching unit errors and denaturation. It is true that the band is loose (the crystal structure satisfies it), but
that is a separate issue from redundancy.

**Measured the effect of 3 replicas (added 2 with seeds 20260820/21).** Single 0.729/0.743/0.717 -> mean 0.730 **SD 0.010**,
between replicas 0.780/0.851/0.770 mean 0.801, 3-replica pool 0.764 (+0.034). The margin over the null maximum goes +0.142 -> +0.176.
The adversarial side (ANM ensemble, 3 replicas) also gains +0.022 from pooling, so **the gain is real but not dramatic**.
What is really new is **reference-free agreement between replicas**, which goes into the `execution_validity` axis.
Practical implication: **with SD 0.010, differences below 0.03 between agents are noise.** Without replicas this cannot be known.

**The SIF's OpenBLAS was collapsing from creating too many threads (affects the whole project).**
The scorer took over 10 minutes per task, so I profiled it: `anm_null_distribution` took 528 seconds.
Vectorizing the Hessian construction did not help (results matched exactly at RMSIP=1.000000); the culprit was `np.linalg.eigh`.

| Environment | `eigh(684x684)` |
|---|---|
| SIF, no thread env | **16.34 s** |
| SIF, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` | 0.12 s |
| SIF, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=8` | 0.07 s |
| Host python3 | 0.59 s |

`matmul` differs by 3.7×, so this is LAPACK-specific. The SIF's numpy carries scipy-openblas built with
`DYNAMIC_ARCH NO_AFFINITY MAX_THREADS=64`, and on a 32-core machine with no cap set, small problems collapse.
**Always pass `OMP_NUM_THREADS` when running numpy inside the SIF.**
`scripts/_threads.py` guards against it with `os.environ.setdefault` before numpy is imported (over 10 minutes per task -> 7.4 seconds).
The permanent fix belongs in the container or `bin/mdclaw`, but has not been started. Also recorded in memory.

**Final scores**: D01 prep 7/7 md 5/5 (12/12), D02 prep 8/8 md 5/5 (13/13), 13.5 seconds for both tasks combined.

## 2026-08-19 — Water in membrane systems was only 40 % of bulk. Copies were being collision-checked against themselves

Starting from the question of whether PyMOL's green box shows the post-equilibration values, fixed 2 items on the artifact side and
1 item in the core that only became visible in that figure.

### 1. min/eq/prod PDBs were writing the box from build time

`PDBFile.writeFile` takes CRYST1 from the **topology**. The run-side Topology stays as it was when
`topology.pdb` was read, so it is not updated even when NPT changes the box. Measured:

| | box (A) |
|---|---|
| CRYST1 in `equilibrated.pdb` | 118.088 x 118.088 x 175.733 |
| `equilibrated.xml` (actual) | **104.894 x 104.894 x 164.713** |

Overstated by 11 % per edge, 1.4× in volume. In all 3 places, min/eq/prod. In the same repository,
`export_state_to_pdb` (`platform.py:113`) copies the box from the state, and
only the patch equilibration path was correct.

### 2. `center_solute_and_wrap_solvent` was only called at build time

The function is correct. It is only called from `openmm_build.py:1588` and `openmm_system/build.py:607`,
so min/eq/prod wrote the raw integrated coordinates as they were. Measured: water spread to 225 A in x
(2.2× the 104.9 A box). The solute was intact.

Both were fixed by adding `box_vectors` / `image` to `render_simulation_pdb_preserving_resnames`.
**state.xml / .chk / DCD are not touched**, so MD results are unchanged.

### 3. Water added by `extend_water_slabs` was 40 % of bulk

The figure after the fix showed a void at the top, so I measured it:

```
z -45..-30 (the patch's own water)       89-96 % of bulk   <- normal
z  30..95  (added by extend_water_slabs) 35-43 %
```

**Cause: atoms of accepted molecules were added on the spot to the grid used for the check.**
Within one copy, water placed earlier and water placed later were collision-checked against each other. Water is hydrogen-bonded,
so H...O = 1.8 A < cutoff 2.2 A (all-atom check). **The correct structure of water itself
was judged an "overlap"**, and it was thinned down to "a subset whose members are at least 2.2 A apart".
That is about 40 % of bulk.

Confirmed 3 ways: per-copy survival rate of 36-44 % in an instrumented run, offline reproduction of self-thinning alone
43.3 % (measured 40.9 %), and reproduction with heavy atoms only 100 %.

The fix has 3 parts. (a) Check heavy atoms only. (b) Merge a copy into the reference grid only after it is complete.
(c) Derive the stacking period from **the z range of the lipids actually present** rather than the nominal `leaflet`
(the patch's lipids span z -26.87..27.89 = 54.76 A, while the nominal is 46 A. The difference became vacuum at
every seam).

| | Water molecules | Added | overlap drop | Density in extended region |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before fix | 32,149 | 17,338 | 23,819 | 28-43 % |
| (a)+(b) | 50,101 | 41,049 | 108 | 48-101 %, 52 % trough at the seam |
| (a)+(b)+(c) | 54,726 | 40,950 | 495 | 77-100 % |

Packing fraction relative to free volume 54 % -> 91 %. Atom count 186,516 -> 277,768.
**Density of the assembled system 0.625 -> 0.903 g/mL** (measured from the NVT reporters of eq_001 and eq_003).
Before the fix, NPT crushed the box from 2438.7 -> 1812.3 nm^3 (-25.7 %), and even then it stalled at 0.845 g/mL
with an 18 A void left at the top.

### Why it was broken silently

`solv`'s geometry check, the solute containment check, salt concentration, charge neutrality — **all pass**.
Salt concentration was computed "correctly for the wrong amount of water" (87 pairs in 32,326 waters gives
0.150 M, and 149 pairs in 55,027 waters is also 0.150 M). **Nowhere was anything looking at the density
of the material placed.**

So a z histogram of water oxygens was added to `_membrane_embedding_geometry_report`.
It is a function that already reads all atoms, has `box_c`, and has the authority to fail the build, so it costs only one more pass.
The check uses an **absolute reference** (liquid water 0.03344 molecules/A^3) — a relative one (ratio to the cell's own median)
cannot detect a system that is uniformly thin. Measured: before the fix, worst/median = 0.85 would have passed.

```
solv_002 / solv_003 (before fix)  median 0.41 of bulk  -> failed
replay2  ((a)+(b))            median 0.958         -> passed
solv_004 ((a)+(b)+(c))        median 0.957         -> passed
```

### Additional fixes from the cursor review

- Changed `membrane_zs` from the elimination rule "neither water nor ion = membrane" to positive
  identification by Lipid21 names. With salts like Mg2+/Ca2+ in bulk, they were mistaken for membrane, the span expanded to fill
  the box, and the entire extension was silently skipped with a one-line warning (a regression I introduced
  in (c)).
- Made the case where extension is needed but nothing could be added a hard error,
  `membrane_patch_water_extension_failed`. Shipping it as is would be exactly the original 5L7D bug.
- Copy 0 is exempt from the overlap check, since its displacement is exactly a lattice image of `patch_box_c`.
- Advance the chain label before resseq overflows 4 digits (measured 9,343/copy, 7 % headroom).

The contact statistics cursor derived from the manifest were correct to 4 digits: the POPC patch's shortest intermolecular
heavy-atom distance is 2.1164 A, below the cutoff of 2.2 A, but **between water oxygens it is 2.5264 A**, so
the heavy-atom check has 15 % headroom for water. On the other hand, cursor's estimate of resseq collisions
(10,350 molecules per copy, ~1,000 collisions) **did not happen**, with 9,343 measured.
Overhang outside the box also did not occur in this system: the atom z range of 173.70 fit within box_c 173.733.

### Remaining limitations

Packing fraction 91 %, density 0.903 g/mL. 10 % lower than ideal (~1.0). The sources are (1) clipping per molecule at the interval
boundaries makes about 3 A at both ends systematically thin, and (2) the seams are around 0.66 of
bulk. This is within what gentle NPT relaxation absorbs, so it is not pursued this time.


## 2026-08-19 — MDDataBench scoring was far too lenient. Measured 2 holes with adversarial baselines and closed them

**We checked "isn't the score too lenient?" by measurement rather than argument, and it was too lenient.** When we built submissions that should fail and ran them,
3 of them passed with the random-subspace null alone (against the D01 reference):

| Baseline | RMSIP | z | Verdict at the time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Samples from ANM low-frequency modes (**zero MD**) | 0.515 | 46 | **Passed** |
| Real MD truncated to 100 ps | 0.627 | 60 | **Passed** |
| Real MD truncated to 10 ps | 0.420 | 36 | **Passed** |
| Crystal structure + isotropic noise | 0.130 | -0.5 | Correctly failed |
| Copies of the minimized structure | 0.135 | 1.7 | Correctly failed |

In other words, **we could prove "is it the right molecule" but not "was it actually run"**.
`production_ran_for_one_nanosecond` only reading the node's own metadata had the same root cause.

**Fix 1: added a structure-only floor (ANM).** An elastic network built from the crystal structure reaches RMSIP 0.57,
so we require beating it with a margin of 0.05. The floor is taken by maximizing over the cutoff (the cutoff is a free variable for the attacker).

**Fix 2: verify elapsed time physically.** The diffusion coefficient is an **intensive quantity** and cannot be used (1 ns and 100 ps of the same trajectory both give
3.7e-5 cm^2/s). **The total displacement of continuously unwrapped solvent is an extensive quantity**, and it recovered 989 ps from 999 ps, 98 ps from 99 ps,
and 15 ps from 9 ps. A submission without solvent cannot be measured and fails immediately = the correct verdict for a zero-MD submission.

After the fixes, all 5 fail and only the real run passes. **D01's 100 ps cleared the ANM floor by 0.005,
and only the time check caught it**, so both are needed. Added `scripts/negative_controls.py` as a permanent regression.

**Split scoring into prep and md (user instruction).** A single number cannot say whether it "failed in assembly" or
"failed in simulation". The ANM submission and the 10 ps submission both come out **prep full marks, md failed**, so attribution works.
D01 prep 7/7 md 6/6, D02 prep 8/8 md 6/6.

**One bug as a by-product.** The first version of `negative_controls.py` counted atom indices by file line number
(the topology has header lines), so real_full_run came out 0.688, disagreeing with the scorer's 0.729. They agree after the fix.
**Cross-checking every time that the scorer and the regression harness produce the same value** was effective for early detection.

## 2026-08-19 — scorer fixes, D02 added, prompt minimized

**Fixed 2 false FAILs in the scorer.** Reimplemented it as `benchmarks/mddatabench/scripts/score_submission.py`.
Removed the hard-coded `True` and recompute every item from artifacts. The correct locations are
`amber_metadata.json :: parameters.water_model` (+ `forcefield_provenance.openmm_xml`) and
the prod node's `metadata.system_signature.ensemble`. **The barostat is attached at run time, so
it is not in the topo node's system.xml.** Contract atoms are matched by (residue number, atom name), not raw index
(the submission's topology includes solvent). Reproduced 11/11 on D01.

**Added D02: MDDB `A00AJ` (MoDEL 1CSP, Bacillus subtilis major cold-shock protein CspB).**
Taken mechanically as the intersection with MDPrepBench (of the 30 MDPrepBench PDBs, those satisfying CC + Classical MD + 5 analyses
are 1UBQ / 1CSP / 2CBA / 1BNA). **We passed on 2CBA** — the MoDEL deposit has no Zn
(zero HETATM, apo), so it would reward discarding the catalytic metal. That is the exact opposite of the intent of MDPrepBench P26.

What D02 adds to D01 is **side-chain completion** and **nonzero solute charge**. PDB 1CSP lacks the side-chain tips of
Glu 3/21/36/66 and has 505 heavy atoms; the MDDB reference has 521. **The reference itself supplies the equation 505 + 16 = 521**, so
the curator does not have to decide the right answer. Reference scale 201 atoms (67×3), 1 ns window vs window 0.687 ± 0.035,
null sqrt(10/603)=0.129.

**Minimized the prompt (user instruction).** Since the scorer computes both subspaces itself,
**there is no need for the agent to do any analysis in the first place**. Removed all instructions on the analysis contract, report items, chain selection, tautomers, box shape,
and side-chain completion; what remains is only "PDB ID / TIP3P / neutralize / 300 K / NPT / 1 ns or more".
The reference bundle is **never placed in the solver's workspace** (the evaluator fetches it at scoring time), so
the path by which the reference could leak is gone.

**Confirmed by measurement that the minimal prompt is solvable.** With zero protonation instructions, MDClaw
matched the reference composition exactly with 1UBQ -> 602/1231, 1CSP -> 521/1014, and completed the 4 Glu residues of 1CSP without being told.
The 2 runs chose the **opposite** tautomer from the reference (HID on 1UBQ, reference HIE / HIE on 1CSP, reference HID),
but heavy-atom count does not depend on tautomer, so they pass as designed. A ±2 tolerance was added to the total atom count.

**Scores**: D01 11/11 (RMSIP 0.729, z 72.4), D02 12/12 (RMSIP 0.703, z 64.0).
Both show the same picture: direction recovered, amplitude 2-6x smaller. ruff clean, 0 bytes of data in the repository.

## 2026-08-19 — Actually solved D01 with MDClaw: 11/11. The trial run exposed 2 scorer defects

Solved and scored MDDataBench D01, built in the earlier entry the same day, end to end with MDClaw 0.6.6.
One A6000, 1UBQ chain A -> ff14SB + TIP3P, cubic 15 Å, 31355 atoms, HMR 4 fs,
NVT 100 ps + NPT 200 ps, **1 ns NPT production in 2 min 29 s**.

**Result 11/11 PASS.** The core test gives RMSIP=0.729, z=72.4, p<5e-5, rejecting H0.
All 10 canonical correlations exceed the null's 99th percentile. Rg=1.1777 nm (reference 10 ns mean 1.1807,
difference 0.0030 is 1/3 of the 1 ns window SD 0.0102). The prep output matched the reference exactly at
602 heavy atoms / 1231 total / 76 residues / HIE.

**The design's prediction held.** The eigenvalue ratios (own/ref) are [0.60, 0.35, 0.18, 0.18, 0.29, ...]:
**directions are recovered but amplitudes are 2-6x smaller**. As predicted from τ(PC1)=1236 ps, 1 ns does not
produce the variance of the slow modes. RMSIP 0.729 exceeds the ANM floor (0.47-0.62) and is within 0.6σ of the reference's own
1 ns window-to-window self-agreement 0.760 ± 0.053. **An independent 1 ns with a different force field (ff14SB vs Parm99)
landed at the same level as the reference's own 1 ns reproducibility.** The design decision "score H0 rejection, do not score quantitative agreement"
was justified by measurement.

**2 scorer defects from the trial run (both false FAILs).**

1. Looked for the water model directly under `amber_metadata.json`, but it is actually `parameters.water_model`
   (+ `amber/tip3p_standard.xml` in `forcefield_provenance.openmm_xml`).
2. Looked for the barostat in the topo node's `system.xml`, but **the barostat is attached at run time**, so
   it is not there. Read the ensemble from the prod node's `metadata.system_signature.ensemble`.

In addition, the reference's 228 contract atoms must be matched **by (residue number, atom name), not by raw atom index**
(the submission's topology includes solvent, so indices do not match). These were recorded in `scorer_field_map`
in `task.json`. **Even when you profess artifact-as-truth, the scorer lies unless you pin down by real runs where in the artifact
each thing lives.**

Added `benchmarks/mddatabench/scripts/evaluate_submission.py`. ruff clean.

## 2026-08-19 — Created MDDataBench D01: an RMSIP test of the "unrelated" null hypothesis

Created `benchmarks/mddatabench/` and implemented and validated the first task D01 (1 ns MD + essential-subspace agreement).
The reference is MDDB `A0142` (MoDEL 1UBQ, CC-BY 4.0, Amber Parm99 / TIP3P / 300 K / NPT / 10 ns).

**Core of the scoring: a test that rejects H0 = "the two essential subspaces are unrelated" using RMSIP.**
The null distribution is built by Monte Carlo over random orthonormal frames (M=20000 gives mean 0.1206 / SD 0.0083,
matching the analytic value sqrt(D/3M)=0.1209). **No force-field calibration is needed**, so the MD part can be scored without breaking
rev.2's discipline of "do not put thresholds on uncalibrated quantities". Measured (D=10, 3M=684):

| Comparison | RMSIP | z | Rejected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Random (negative control) | 0.121 | 0.0 | **no** |
| ANM (structure only, 10 A) | 0.617 | 59.5 | yes |
| Coordinate-frame mismatch (global rotation) | 0.652 | 64.2 | yes |
| 1 ns window vs 1 ns window | 0.760 ± 0.053 | 81.8 | yes |
| 1 ns window vs full 10 ns | 0.794 ± 0.029 | 84.7 | yes |
| 500 frames from 10 ns | 0.969 | - | yes |

**This test is a validity gate, not a quality score.** An ANM built from structure alone also rejects H0,
so it guarantees "the right molecule was analyzed under the right contract" but not "sampling has converged".

**It turned out that the top modes cannot be compared quantitatively at 1 ns.** The reference's integrated autocorrelation times are PC1 1236 ps / PC2 1081 ps /
PC4 1660 ps, so **the number of independent samples in 1 ns is 0.8 for PC1**. Even the 10 ns reference has 8. Marchenko-Pastur
is inapplicable since q_eff = N/T_eff is 188 at 1 ns and still 38 at 10 ns (the method of PRL 103, 268101 (2009) uses
level-spacing statistics of the bulk, not the MP upper edge). Therefore the continuous RMSIP is diagnostic only and is accumulated as calibration data.

**Numerical evidence that an analysis contract is required.** MDDB distributes PCA eigenvalues and projections but **not eigenvectors**,
so recomputation on the scorer side is required. The contract `pca_backbone_subspace@1` (228 backbone N/CA/C atoms, Kabsch
fit to the reference structure + 3 running-mean iterations, D=10, Å) reproduces the published eigenvalues within -4.8% to +3.4%. The effect of perturbations is
global rotation -0.175 > atom order -0.018 > translation 0. Separately, for Rg, mass weighting with standard atomic weights deviates systematically from the published value by
+0.0024 nm, which corresponds to 24% of the 1 ns window SD of 0.0102 nm.

**Data are not bundled.** `scripts/fetch_reference.py` fetches from MDDB and writes provenance and SHA-256.
Confirmed byte-identical on re-fetch. `.gitignore` forbids committing fetched data. During solve, `mddbr.eu` is blocked;
RCSB is allowed. The accession is not shown in the prompt.

**Rejected the idea of making Rg the primary observable.** Done correctly, anyone gets 1.18 nm, so it has no discriminating power. RMSIP has a wide range:
0.12 (chance) - 0.79 (1 ns self-agreement) - 1.0. ruff clean, validated end to end from fetch to test.

## 2026-08-19 — Looking at actual pictures exposed 5 membrane-building bugs, 3 of them in salt and ion placement

Starting from a hackathon report ("embedding 5L7D in a membrane left the extracellular domain sticking out of the box"),
**actually rendering the assembled system with PyMOL** turned up 4 bugs besides the box size.
All of them passed without raising an error. Had cursor review it twice, and also applied its 2 findings.

### 1. The bilayer did not enclose the transmembrane region

`_estimate_patch_membrane_center_z` computed the midplane as the **periodic mean** of the headgroups.
`_periodic_mean` unwraps at the largest gap, but a bilayer has 2 gaps of similar size, the **hydrophobic core (~34 A) and the water layer (~35 A)**,
and unwrapping at the core returns the **midpoint of the water layer**, i.e. a point **half a box away**
from the true midplane.

Measured on the bundled POPC patch (box_c 76.846): phosphate planes 26.4 / 71.2, true midplane 48.8,
**estimate 10.3**. Difference 38.5 = half the box. As a result, in the assembled system the bilayer sat at z=38.5, and
of the 173 residues that the OPM transfer had placed inside the bilayer, **0 residues** were actually in the membrane.
**Lipids were wrapped around the extracellular domain and the TM helices were in water**.

Changed to estimate from the acyl chains (the core is one contiguous slab, so the unwrap is unique). Estimate 48.5.

### 2. The placement guard was designed so it could not work (cursor finding)

After fix 1 we added a guard that "re-estimates after placement and compares with the target", but cursor pointed out that
it is **algebraically meaningless**. With shift = target − E(atoms) and E translation-equivariant,
E(atoms + shift) = target holds identically. **It always passes even if the estimator is off by half a box.**

Replaced it with an independent check that does not use the estimator: at the target frame position, **(a) presence of acyl-chain carbons,
(b) absence of water, (c) headgroups present and balanced on both sides**. Measured:

```
broken system: tail 0    / water 4252 / headgroups lower 0/upper 440   -> rejected
fixed system:  tail 3604 / water 0    / headgroups lower 210/upper 220 -> passed
```

When evidence is insufficient (stub patches, etc.) it makes no judgement, because rejecting on missing evidence is also a wrong answer.

### 3. Tile molecule identifiers were duplicated — salt concentration was 1/(nx*ny)

`build_tiled_membrane` rewrote **only the lines** and did not rewrite the `PDBAtom` records.
Neutralization groups molecules by `_water_residues` keyed on `atom.chain_id`/`atom.resseq`, so
**"patch water #1" in all 6 tiles collapsed onto the same key**.

- `n_water = len(water_groups)` is used for the salt-concentration calculation, so **only 1/6 of the bulk salt went in**
- The candidate pool also shrank, and ions were unevenly distributed (measured lower 26/upper 88, water 1:1)

Fixed by giving them identifiers with `replace()`. After the fix, lower 77/upper 85 (water lower 7491/upper 7381).
When I fixed the same kind of bug that I had created in the water extension, I should have noticed it was
already present on the tiling side too.

### 4. Neutralization assigned species in z order — charge separation across the periodic box

Candidates were sorted by ascending z and then **all cations assigned first, all anions after**.
Measured chain I: NA lower 5 / CL lower 23 / CL upper 4. Changed to alternating placement.

### 5. Salt was added twice (cursor finding)

The cached patch is **already packed at the requested concentration**, yet `plan_neutralizing_ions`
added the full amount without subtracting existing ions. Once fix 3 corrected the underestimate of `n_water`, this
surfaced as **0.268 M (requested 0.150)**.

Changed to add only the per-species shortfall (counting in pairs, when removing buried ions reduces only one side,
it reads "0 pairs" and adds the full amount). After the fix **0.151 M**, net charge −37 (the amount neutralizing the protein).

### Related: ions buried inside the bilayer of the bundled patch

The bundled POPC patch has Cl− inside the bilayer, and replicating it across 6 tiles gave
25 ions inside the membrane. They are removed during tiling and re-placed in bulk by neutralization (30 removed).
This is **a defect of the patch itself**, so the proper fix is to rebuild the patch.

### Visualization — without it none of the 4 would have been found

Added a `system_box` style to `render_structure_preview`. Protein cartoon per chain,
lipid sticks, water as semi-transparent surface, ion spheres, and the **periodic cell as a wire frame**.
Orthographic, 2 orthogonal views along the x and z axes. The cell is drawn at the **center of mass of water + lipids** (the center of mass of the whole system
would drag the box along with a protein that sticks out of it, making it meaningless).

Per a cursor finding, `orthogonal_view` was restricted to `system_box`. It had applied to all styles, so
`ligand_site` and others had lost their intended camera.

On the skill side, added to `visual-qa.md` "render at each stage that changes the system and **send the images to the user**", and
to `run-loop.md` "after each step report the node ID, the conditions actually used, the system size, and warnings".
**Rendering without showing the user is the same as not rendering.**

### Impact on existing outputs

All existing D473Y / G497W systems are affected by (1)(3)(4)(5). D473Y was rebuilt up to solv.

### Applied cursor's P2 findings

| Finding | Response |
|---|---|
| Tail mean is biased by chain length and leaflet composition | Implemented `_leaflet_midpoint`. Each leaflet is found separately and the **unweighted** midpoint taken. 48.7 on the real patch (true 48.8, tail mean 48.5) |
| Cannot handle a cholesterol-only patch | Fall back in order headgroups → tails → all lipid atoms, each passed through the discriminator |
| 5 A tolerance is inappropriate | The guard was replaced by a density check, so the constant was deleted altogether |
| `solvent_ions` overlays dots on top of surface | The generic block went back to dots; surface is only for `system_box` |
| `system_box` ignores `show_lipids`/`show_ions`; manifest and PNG disagree | Respect the flags and **read back the representations actually drawn from PyMOL** to record in the manifest |
| Periodic cell misdraws a triclinic box as rectangular | Check α/β/γ; if not rectangular, do not draw and record the reason |
| manifest / node metadata lack the 2nd image | Record `views` (axis and image path), `periodic_cell`, `output_png_top` |
| Skill text is contradictory, specifies `system_box` for prep | "**Attempt** rendering at every stage; success is best-effort". prep uses `overview`, solv onward `system_box`. State explicitly to look at both images |

The discriminator was also improved. With headgroups alone, "membrane midpoint" and "water midpoint" are equivalent, so
it decides using **both presence of acyl chains and absence of water** (water alone could not discriminate on a synthetic patch).

Also filled in the CLI side. The `render_structure_preview` docstring now lists the styles, what `system_box`
draws, the 2 views, and "send to the user", and `docs/developer/tool-reference.md` was updated too.

Final check (solv_016): bilayer midplane 0.1, ions inside membrane 0, salt **0.150 M** (requested 0.150),
ions lower 59/upper 68 (water 1:1), geometry passed.

### Not addressed

- Artificial periodicity from tiling (68 ions overlap at 28 xy positions, replicas of identical lipid arrangements)
- **Rebuilding the bundled patch itself** (ions buried inside the bilayer)
- Rebuilding G497W; D473Y also stops at solv

## 2026-08-19 — Bug: patch-tile did not size the z dimension of the box from the protein

A hackathon member reported: "after embedding GPCR 5L7D in a membrane and solvating, the extracellular domain stuck out of
both sides of the box". **It was a real bug in the default backend `patch-tile`.**
Had cursor verify independently too, and it confirmed all 4 points (its 3 findings were corrections to my explanation).

### Root cause

`patch_membrane.py:636`

```python
box_c = 2.0 * (float(dist_wat) + float(leaflet))   # the solute is not included at all
```

Assembly in `patch_membrane.py`:

```python
total_box = {"box_a": nx * box_a, "box_b": ny * box_b, "box_c": box_c}
```

`nx`/`ny` are determined by `_tile_counts` from the protein's XY bounds + 2*dist.
**z has no counterpart.** `_tile_counts` explicitly discards `_minz, _maxz` from `_bounds()`.
There are 3 sources for the box height (cache / the patch's CRYST1 / a derived formula), but
**all of them are the patch's height and unrelated to the solute**.

### 5L7D measurements

```
5L7D chain A membrane frame      z = -30.3 .. +77.9 A   (span 108.2 A)
default box_c = 2*(17.5+23.0)                          =  81.0 A
after build_amber_system +2 A margin                   ~  83.0 A  <- actual MD box
atoms outside box       1131 of 3754 (30.1%)
minimum-image wrap destination                         z in [-40.5, -3.1]
of these, atoms in periodic image's lipid core (|z|<15) 240
```

**The extracellular domain penetrates the membrane of the neighboring periodic image.**

### Why it breaks silently

1. **carve is PBC-aware** (`patch_membrane.py:1795`), so lipids around the wrapped CRD are
   removed "correctly", and **a system with a hole in the membrane is completed without error**.
2. **The geometry check cannot detect it** (`membrane.py:327`). It only looks at the headgroup span and
   "whether ≥15% of protein atoms intersect the membrane". 5L7D passes easily on its TM part.
   It computed neither the solute's z range nor the clearance to the box faces.

### It propagates all the way to MD

`total_box` → CRYST1 + `box_dimensions.json` → `build_amber_system` →
`setPeriodicBoxVectors` in `openmm_build.py:1037-1060` → `system.xml` / `state.xml` →
min/eq/prod prefer the box vectors in the state. `center_solute_and_wrap_solvent` intentionally
does not wrap the largest molecule, so its shape is preserved, but a 108.2 A molecule does not fit in an 83 A box.

### The packmol-memgen path is fine

The upstream source (`packmol_memgen/main.py`) takes

```python
z_max = pdbz_max + distance_wat
if z_max < (leaflet_z + distance_wat): z_max = leaflet_z + distance_wat
```

i.e. **the larger** of solute and membrane. The CLI help also says "water layer over the membrane **or protein**".
The point of divergence was that `patch-tile` borrowed only the name and implemented it as "thickness from the membrane".
Note that the valid values of `membrane_backend` are `packmol-memgen` / `patch-tile` / `auto`;
`full` does not exist (what I first wrote was wrong).

### Fix (permanent)

**Redefine `dist_wat` the same way as packmol-memgen: "padding from whichever of membrane or solute extends farther".**
(Initially we made the patch itself taller, but redid it as described below.)

```python
effective_dist_wat = max(dist_wat, max|z_solute - centre| + dist_wat - leaflet)
```

For 5L7D, 17.5 → **72.4**, box_c 81.0 → **190.8 A**. For TM-only proteins it stays 17.5
(no regression).

**We did not adopt the option of only enlarging the box.** Stretching CRYST1 without adding water creates a vacuum layer and
breaks the density. Making the patch taller fills the added volume with equilibrated water at the correct density.
The cache includes `dist_wat` in its fingerprint, so taller patches automatically become separate entries, and
**no schema change is needed**. The cost is that "the first cold build for a tall protein is long", and
the cold-build notice now says so.

We took a symmetric box (190.8 A) and passed on the asymmetric minimal box (143.2 A). Making it asymmetric would require
cutting the equilibrated patch at an arbitrary plane, and the cut faces are not truly periodic counterparts of each other, so
a seam would appear. About 33% more water, but we prioritized a correct, seamless system.

Added 2 safety nets:
- After assembly, check containment with `solute_fits_box`, and if it does not fit, reject with
  `membrane_patch_solute_exceeds_box_z` (guards against heights from old caches)
- Added `protein_exceeds_periodic_box_z` to the geometry report. It is a **separate failure reason** from the
  membrane-intersection check, so "correctly in the membrane but not in the box" can be detected

### cursor review found a P1 regression in my own fix

**Writing the containment check as atom positions against "membrane centre ± box_c/2" was wrong**. This assumes
the box is symmetric about the membrane centre, which is false for the asymmetric boxes packmol-memgen builds.
As cursor reproduced, it misjudged a 143.2 A box holding a 108.2 A solute as "sticking out by 6.3 A" and
rejected it. Since this runs after the `auto` fallback, it was **a regression that rejects correctly built systems**.

Under PBC the origin is arbitrary, and a molecule crossing a face simply re-enters from the other side. The only thing translation cannot remove is
**a molecule longer than the periodic length**. Changed the check to `protein_z_span >= box_c`
(likewise for `solute_fits_box`. Since the centre is no longer needed, this also resolved a separate finding about the double
interpretation of `membrane_center_z=None`).

### Redesigned again: add water instead of making the patch taller

Received 2 points from the user. **Both were correct, and the first implementation was wrong.**

1. "Can't you make it so the cache works?"
2. "I'd think 23 A covers a lot of membrane proteins"

The enlargement condition is `reach + dist_wat - leaflet > dist_wat`, i.e. **`reach > leaflet` (23 A)**.
**Almost every membrane protein with |z| beyond 23 A is affected**. And since `dist_wat` is in the cache fingerprint,
**a cold build runs every time**. In fact, the 2LOP pipeline test, normally ~100 s, was running
a cold build for **more than 20 minutes**.

**Making the membrane patch height depend on the solute was the mistake**. The bilayer is unrelated to the protein, so
the right approach is to keep using the cached one and **add only the missing water along z**:

```python
low  = min(solute_z_min, centre - leaflet) - dist_wat
high = max(solute_z_max, centre + leaflet) + dist_wat
```

The patch is always requested with the caller's `dist_wat`, so the cache always hits.
The missing volume is filled by **stacking copies of the patch's own water slab along z**. This is the same approach solvation programs use
when replicating an equilibrated water box, and density and ion concentration carry over unchanged.
Boundaries between copies are not truly periodic counterparts, so molecules that come within 2.2 A of existing atoms are
**dropped whole** (also the standard overlap removal of solvation programs).

**The box became the asymmetric minimum.** **143.2 A** for 5L7D (190.8 if symmetric, 206 with bucketing).
There is no longer any need to mirror the extracellular domain's water below the membrane, so the amount of water also went down.

Validation on real data (5L7D real coordinates + synthetic patch):

```
interval        low=-47.8  high=+95.4  box_c=143.2  (extend below 7.3 / above 54.9)
extension       18252 molecules added, 0 overlap rejections
assembled z     -45.1 .. 94.5
containment     fits=True  span=108.2  headroom=35.0
water number density  original slab 0.0330 /A^3  →  extension 0.0329 /A^3
```

**The pipeline test is back to 97.79 s / 4 passed** (cold build over 20 min → cache hit).

Height bucketing and the `membrane_patch_box_too_tall` cap became unnecessary now that the patch is no longer made taller, and
were deleted.

### Tests

Added 4 to `tests/test_solvation_server.py` (verify enlargement with real 5L7D numbers / TM-only does
not enlarge / reject a solute that does not fit the box / geometry case that passes the membrane check but fails containment).
After the review, added 3 more (accept an asymmetric box / reject exceeding the cap / height buckets).
ruff clean, solvation + guardrail + contract + orientation suites 321 passed.

## 2026-08-19 — Ported PPM3 to the arm64 image. The amd64 check was ineffective, and the MODELLER ldd check broke itself on its first real run

To rebuild the SIF for Rikyu, rebuilt `Dockerfile.rikyu-arm64` on a Mac (Apple Silicon /
Docker Desktop). The PPM3 patch present in amd64 had not been ported to arm64,
so this was the work of porting it. It was meant to be just a port, but the **checks** on both sides were broken.

### The aarch64 conda immers has the same bug

Inspecting the pre-port image (`54798ff`), `/opt/mdclaw/bin/immers` **already
exists**. There is no binary in the ppm3 source directory; the ambertools conda package puts
an aarch64 build in bin. Its contents:

```
' tilt=',f7.0'+-',        <- missing comma; same as the bundled amd64 binary
```

So arm64 also needed "patch, re-make, and overwrite the conda one".
`install -m 0755 ... /opt/mdclaw/bin/immers` is that overwrite.

### The amd64 post-check has never fired

```
/opt/mdclaw/bin/immers < /dev/null 2>&1 | grep -q "Fortran runtime error: Missing comma"
```

With empty stdin it dies with "End of file" at the first read in `opm.f:84`. **It never reaches the offending FORMAT
line, so this pattern can never match.** Moreover, since it is a `sed && grep || true` chain,
even if sed does not apply, it is swallowed by `|| true` and the build continues. In other words the amd64 side is
in a state where "it passes straight through even if the patch does not apply".

The arm64 version now checks the FORMAT string inside the compiled binary. After patching it contains
`f7.0,'+-'`, unpatched it contains `f7.0'+-'`, so this actually discriminates. Running it with empty stdin
was kept, but its meaning changed to confirming that "the binary resolves its shared libraries and reaches the Fortran runtime".
The same check was added to `test-container.sh`, applied only to images that declare
`MDCLAW_PPM3_PATCHED` (old SIFs SKIP). Its effect was confirmed by setting the variable on an old image: 20 passed / **1 failed**.

### The MODELLER ldd check (8afd86e) was broken itself, not the image

The first build failed at stage 2, 19/20.

```
libglib-2.0.so.0 => not found
libmodeller.so.14 => not found
```

Both actually exist in the image (glib in conda's `/opt/mdclaw/lib`, libmodeller next to the
extension). The cause was running `ldd` without the runtime's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`; **it was a defect of the check,
not of the image**. As the 2026-08-18 entry said, "the rikyu end-to-end build is
unverified", and this was the check's first real run. Resolved by giving it the same search path
the runtime declares.

### Result

```
image   ghcr.io/matsunagalab/mdclaw-rikyu:arm64-cuda13-dev-f9e628126877  21 GB
digest  sha256:32fde85be54f4582a13129808092881af4ff5fcb225b7564aa23bb3797475ddf
smoke   23 passed, 0 failed   (including PPM3 and MODELLER; GPU SKIP)
```

Pushed to GHCR. The package is public, and we confirmed the manifest can be pulled with an anonymous token,
so the Rikyu side can `apptainer pull` without credentials.

The SIF was converted on the local Lima VM `singularity-ce` (singularity-ce 4.5.0) from a digest-pinned pull.

```
~/Downloads/mdclaw-rikyu-arm64-cuda130-ppm3-f9e628126877.sif
6,774,157,312 bytes
SHA-256 367af38cb733207176703d69b5d115f629707565db40ebf8ad93befb2947d8e4
```

**Container test 23/23 from the SIF as well.** The PPM3 check passing inside the SIF is meaningful:
it confirms that the rebuilt `immers` resolves conda's libgfortran.so.5 (not apt's gfortran) via
the runtime LD_LIBRARY_PATH. What remains is GPU smoke on real Rikyu hardware (`test-rikyu-gpu.sh`), which
only exercises the FUSE path when run from the SIF.

### It builds on a Mac

`build-rikyu-arm64.sh` works on an arm64 host, but `nproc` and `df -BG --output` are GNU-only
and did not work on macOS (the former dies on the spot under `set -e`). Added fallbacks to `sysctl -n hw.ncpu` /
`df -k`. The Docker Desktop VM has 14 CPUs / 8.3 GB, so we limited it to
`BUILD_JOBS=6` (parallel nvcc eats memory). Only SIF conversion cannot be done on a Mac
(no apptainer), so we push to GHCR and `apptainer pull` on the Rikyu side.

## 2026-08-19 — cursor re-review: 10 items. The coplanar rejection and the sparse-perfect ranking were real bugs

Had the same `smo_reviewer` re-review the diff after the fixes. **This time it did not modify any files**
(the request stated the previous violation explicitly and instructed it to put test proposals inside the review document).
10 new findings (P1×2, P2×6, P3×2). **The 2 that change the design were reproduced by me before fixing.**

### What was confirmed by measurement

```
[coplanar]  rmsd=4.5e-15  det=1.000  max|R-Rtrue|=3.3e-16  fit_condition=0.0000  <- rejects a correct fit
[collinear] s2/s1=0.0000  s3/s1=0.0000
[1 helix]   s2/s1=0.0947  s3/s1=0.0929
[rank]      sparse (1.0, 0.2, -2.9) > broad (0.99, 1.0, -0.1)   <- 40/40 beats 198/200
[validate]  max_candidates=1.5 -> None                          <- a fraction passes
[short ATOM] RAISED IndexError: string index out of range
```

### Correction 1: rank-2 suffices for the degeneracy check (I was too strict)

`_fit_condition` used s3/s1 (smallest/largest principal component), but **this is stricter than Kabsch's
identifiability condition**. With 3 or more non-collinear points, the 2 in-plane basis vectors are determined, and **the proper-rotation constraint fixes the normal**.
Indeed, a general rotation can be recovered to **3.3e-16** accuracy from 40 perfectly coplanar points, yet my gate
rejected it with `fit_condition=0.0000`. **Changed to s2/s1**: collinear 0.000 / coplanar 1.000 /
single ideal helix 0.095 / real membrane CA sets 0.86-0.87. Threshold 0.01 kept.

### Correction 2: rounding identity cannot stop sparse-perfect

In the previous entry we solved the 201-vs-200 problem by "rounding support to 1/10 of the best candidate", but
**with identity still as the leading key, 40/40 (100%) beats 198/200 (99%)**.
100% of 40 observations is a *weaker* claim than 99% of 200 observations.
**Replaced it with the Wilson lower bound**: 40/40 → 0.91, 198/200 → 0.96, 200/200 and 201/201 → both 0.98.
Rounded to 2 digits, 201 vs 200 also ties and RMSD decides. The key became the 2-element
`(round(wilson_lb(membrane_identity, membrane_ca), 2), -fit_rmsd)`, and
the support buckets were deleted since Wilson absorbs them.

### Other fixes

| # | Description |
|---|---|
| P1 | **Score all query chains, then decide by a single ranking**. Previously "the chain that first had an acceptable donor" won. A long membrane-bound partner could set the orientation of the whole complex with a donor that barely passes, leaving the actual transmembrane subunit unused |
| P1 | **Do not claim "best" when candidates remain at budget exhaustion**. A donor that passed all gates is adopted (better than falling to another method), but `evaluation_complete=false` and a warning are emitted |
| P2 | **Choose one altLoc per residue**. Taking max occupancy per atom creates **a hybrid side chain that does not exist**, with CA from conformer A and CB from B |
| P2 | **Keep TER**. Dropping it fuses 2 polymers into one chain and creates bonds that do not exist |
| P2 | **Dedicated code for incomplete evaluation** `opm_homolog_evaluation_incomplete`. Reporting "1 rejected + 1 DL failure" as `rejected` makes the agent interpret it as "we checked and it was no good" and not retry |
| P2 | **Reject ATOM lines shorter than 54 columns in a structured way** (previously IndexError escaped) |
| P3 | **Count parameters must be integers**. `max_candidates=1.5` reached RCSB as an invalid page request, and the requester's mistake came back as a "search outage". `min_fit_condition=0` is also forbidden |
| P3 | **Removed the 1-second floor on the budget**. Short explicit budgets lose their binding force |

### Handling of budget exhaustion differs from the review's proposal

The review said "do not choose from a truncated candidate set (= fall back to PPM3)", but we judged that
**discarding a donor that passed all gates and moving to another method is to the user's detriment**. We adopt it and make
"the comparison was incomplete" explicit via `evaluation_complete=false`, a warning, and a record in `report`.
On the other hand, the finding that **returning `rejected`/`no_match` when nothing could be accepted is a false report** is entirely
correct, so that case became `opm_homolog_evaluation_incomplete`.

### Live re-measurement

After the fixes, 5L7D still **adopts 5L7D itself, PDBTM normal error 5.9 degrees** (unchanged).
The mock 4JKV path is also unchanged at 11.8 degrees.

### Tests

ruff clean. `test_membrane_orientation.py` 62 → **75** tests. 467 passed including contract suites.

## 2026-08-19 — cursor review: 10 items. 5 reproduced, and a ranking defect surfaced in measurement

Had `smo_reviewer` (cursor / GPT-5.6 Sol) review the uncommitted diff. 10 findings
(P1×2, P2×6, P3×2). **Ran everything that could be reproduced, and all 5 reproduced.**

```
[min_ca=0]      RAISED LinAlgError: 0-dimensional array given
[NaN rmsd]      accepted=True  fit_rmsd=39.146      <- passes a 39 A fit
[collinear]     rmsd=0  det=1.000                    <- rotation about the axis is undetermined
[multi-model]   residues from model 1, CA coordinates from model 2 (z=99)
[altLoc]        occupancy 0.70 is at z=0, yet z=50 adopted
```

### One procedural problem as well

The review request stated explicitly "do not modify any files", but cursor had
added one test to `tests/test_membrane_orientation.py`
(`test_partial_outage_with_a_completed_no_match_is_not_total_unavailability`,
07:05:36). Nothing leaked into other files (the memo and tool-reference changes are mine).
**However, the finding itself was correct**: when one chain got HTTP 500 and another chain normally returned 0 hits,
my implementation returned `opm_homolog_search_unavailable` ("no chain could be searched").
In reality one chain was searched and answered "no match". The assertion required wording that does not exist,
so it was rewritten, and the code was fixed to "`opm_homolog_no_match`, stating both the results of the chains that could be searched and
the number of chains that could not".

### What was fixed

| # | Description |
|---|---|
| P1 | **Added a gate on membrane-subset identity**. With whole-chain identity alone, a donor that shares a large soluble domain but has an unrelated membrane domain passes. The fit is done on the membrane subset, so that is the subset where correspondence must actually exist |
| P1 | **Validate public parameters** (`opm_homolog_gates_invalid`). Reject out-of-range and non-finite values, and make it **a failure, not a fallback**. Silently loosening a gate is worse than refusing the request |
| P2 | **Query chains with identical sequences share only the search; the fit is done per physical chain** |
| P2 | **Evaluate all candidates before choosing** (user decision). RCSB's ranking is search relevance, not orientation quality |
| P2 | **Reject degenerate fits** (`opm_min_fit_condition`). Collinear CAs pass with RMSD 0 and det 1.0 but the rotation about the axis is arbitrary |
| P2 | **Separate DL failure from gate failure** (`opm_homolog_fetch_unavailable`). A donor that was never judged was being reported as "insufficient quality" |
| P2 | **Use only model 1 and the highest-occupancy altLoc** for both the fit and the output |
| P2 | **Total time budget** (`opm_total_budget_seconds`, default 600 s). Previously 120 s × chains × candidates |
| P3 | **Atomic cache writes and consistency checks**, SHA-256 recorded |
| P3 | **A 200 with empty body is unavailable**. Only 204 is RCSB's no-hit |

### The degeneracy threshold was set by measurement

`s3/s1` (smallest/largest principal-component spread): real membrane CA sets **0.685-0.702**, a single ideal α-helix of
40 residues **0.093**, collinear and coplanar **0.000**. **0.01** leaves an order of magnitude of margin on both sides.
Notably, **the test fixture itself was degenerate** (x and y of `_membrane_path` proportional = a planar curve).
The new gate correctly detected it, so the fixture was rewritten as a truly 3-dimensional helix.

### Evaluating all candidates exposed a ranking defect on real data

Scoring all 10 candidates in a live run:

| pdb | in-membrane identity | in-membrane CA | fit RMSD |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5l7i | 1.000 | 201 | 0.325 A |
| **5l7d** | 1.000 | **200** | **0.000 A** |
| 7zi0 | 1.000 | 197 | 0.181 A |
| 6ot0 | 0.994 | 176 | 1.927 A |

The original ordering (identity → in-membrane CA count → RMSD) **made 5L7D itself (perfect match, RMSD 0.000) lose to 5L7I
by a 1-residue difference of 201 vs 200 CAs**. It is wrong for a 0.5% difference in support to override a 3x
difference in RMSD. Fixed by rounding support to **steps of 1/10 of the best candidate**, letting RMSD decide when they are comparable.

After the fix, **5L7D itself is selected, PDBTM normal error 5.9 degrees**. This is
**exactly the disagreement between the 2 reference DBs, OPM and PDBTM**, and the theoretical lower bound for the transfer method.
It is the favorable case where the query is registered in OPM, but it does prove that the pipeline works
correctly end to end.

The 6.3 degrees (6OT0) and 11.8 degrees (4JKV) in the previous entry are also values for the same 5L7D, so
**the choice of donor moves it by 5.9-11.8 degrees**. It was confirmed again that donor selection, not
fit RMSD, governs the accuracy of this method.

### What was praised (with explicit instruction not to churn)

The I/D direction of the CIGAR walk is correct (checked both ways), restricting to the DUM slab is clearly safer than a whole fit or
trimming, gate-first selection of donor chains, not stopping later chains on partial failure,
per-chain rejection reasons in the JSON.

### Tests

ruff clean. `test_membrane_orientation.py` 26 → **62** tests.
454 passed including contract suites.
